main: A deadly fog is terrorizing our people.
All unsaved progress will be lost.
Loyalty +4, Economy +4 OR Stability -5 (depending on banditism level in the {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom}.)

" …your zeal has not gone unnoticed in Nidal. We are pleased by your success, and this means Zon-Kuthon is pleased as well. The Umbral Court requires a new agent in the Stolen Lands. By Eloander's insistence, the circle of druids recommended... "

"'Grandpa,' I pleaded. 'Leave me.'
He looked at me and silently shook his head.
It was a long time coming. I'd gone out to scout as usual, spotted a handful of monsters, quietly turned to head back – only to find a second pack had crept up on me from behind, as I was watching the first. And then things started happening very quickly. I scurried blind into a side tunnel I'd never explored. They follow me down. I scamper somewhere else – and run right back into them. I spin on my heels and bolt for my life, but they get me in the leg so I'm limping. By the time I hear the song... it was way too late. I had nowhere to turn. I saw her, and she saw me. It was a large cave, well-lit by local standards. She stood in the middle and sang, and monsters of all types lay at her feet. Claws, jaws, fangs, stingers – so many that it seemed like one huge beast made of everything that kills. And she was its heart. The Wicked Chanter.
She is not very Wicked, if you listen closely to what she is singing.
But then it grew very quiet, and she walked right at me. I pressed my back to the wall, and I'm thinking – 'This is it.' And she comes up to me, tilts her head and sniffs me. There's nothing living in her big black eyes, except for something mean and wild. How could she grow up in pitch black darkness with the beasts, and become anything more? She looked at me and me at her. And I say, 'What are you looking at? Never seen a redhead?' And I'm thinking to myself that I might have one quick shot, but then that'll be it. They'll all attack, and bite and slice, and tear me to ribbons – a pool of gore at her feet.
She reached out and touched my hair. And then she turned around and walked away, all the monsters with her. I found a little nook, crawled inside and passed out, knowing that if I ever woke up, it would be when something started eating me.
But no. I opened my eyes and I saw him. The elf. He'd come looking for me, when the others refused.
The scoundrels. He shouldn't have paid them up front.
I'd lost so much blood, I thought I'd never make it back up. I kept telling the elf to leave me, but he wouldn't budge. Then I reminded him about his wife's bones, that he wanted so bad to recover. I told him – 'If you try to save me, you'll die. And you won't get what you came here for.' That was when he finally spoke.
'You're a fool tenderfoot, Red. And I'm a fool too.'
Then he sat right beside me and looked at me with those same black eyes. 'I've come here over and over, gotten two parties wiped out, just to find Rivel's bones. I felt like I'd abandoned her in her moment of need. I know her pendant is still here somewhere... It calls out to me, and led me here. But do you know what? It was all for nothing. All these people died for nothing. I dragged them to their doom just to drown out my own conscience. And it was only when you went missing... only then I realized. I might take this guilt to my grave, but I'll drag that boy alive from the darkness, before I drag out some old bones, even if they are the bones of my beloved!'
As he was saying all this, his face lightened up a little – for the first time I'd ever seen. It was like he'd found something for himself. Something he could call new. And all I could think of was Her, her wild black eyes, and I knew. I could never tell him now. I'll throw away this book when he's not looking. And I'll never say a word.
About the song she sang. And the cradle I found at the camp by the lake."

"... Can one die of love? I will soon find out, for each day I spend without you is like the jagged blades of eternity stinging my body. Yes, I will soon die, die of my love for you!
She was beside herself with anger. She stood and tried to leave, but he grabbed her shoulders and pushed her onto the sofa. She screamed in fear as he sprung forward, grabbed her head and plundered her pink lips with a violent kiss. She dropped her head against the back of the sofa, and he continued to shower her blazing skin, to caress her shoulders, smothering her with his rough manly smell, driving her out of her head, carrying her away on waves of lust.
Breaking through the words of love that rained from his lips, she moaned helplessly, unable to hide the desire in her voice...
"You are but a rude, shameless barbarian..."
"... and he vanished. What was that about being led astray? He should have watched his step!"
"... and independent Rostland for desert! Mmm... mouthwatering!"

"... roaring flames are devouring the Temple of Roses. The petals of the flowers darken, curl up and finally turn to ash – the moment of utter pain and ugliness that comes before final, serene eternity. Burning idols seem to grimace, cry, laugh – and turn their fiery gazes upon me. The heat grows unbearable – but I dare not turn my eyes from this sacred fire, admiring its every precious moment while my eyes still serve me. Laymen will call me a vandal – they'll say that I'd destroyed a priceless piece of art because I hated everything beautiful. But do not believe this. I loved the temple more than my life, and I lit it with the fires that burn in my heart. For can there be a higher devotion than melting together with the object of your admiration, into the shining splendor of oblivion?"
"...All right, boys. Back off. But you, you lowlife..."
"...Don't even start! This is..."
"...How much?"
"...Maegar, can you even hear yourself? What utter rubbish..."
"...The darkness settled o'er the lad, and on the spot he then went mad!"
"...The skull came flying down the hall, as a baneful wrecking ball..."
"...The stranger shook his head – 'my dears, I have been dead for fifteen years!'"
"...To the doomed kingdoms. No, I will not search any longer. But... but I must find it! Come now, start searching! It must be here in the Stolen Lands!"
"...What for, teacher?"
"...Why search for that which has ruined me? He said... he said, 'Let your unrequited love guide you.'"
"...and so I say, 'Where are three cubits here? Is he measuring cloth in gnome cubits?!'
"...no, no, and no! You have no idea..."
"...no, you need to listen to me..."
"...not before you read the rules."
"...say whatever you want, but I will not tolerate..."
"...the sky will split, the waters will part, and the ground itself will devour the evil that comes to us from the lands of death!"
"...you are single-handedly destroying everything we've worked so hard for, these many years..."

"1. The youth shall leave their malady behind!
The Bleaching does not cling to people until they mature.
2. What is the color of your skin?
Apple-cheeked yesterday, but deathly pale today? That's an alarming sign! Closely monitor the condition of your skin, hair, and eyes.
3. Never be bored.
Curiosity is your best protection. Have a finger in every pie!
4. Don't break your neck.
Be prepared to stand up for yourself or run for your life when you venture out to seek adventure.
5. Never give up.
There's a remedy for the Bleaching – and it isn't pills. But a new wardrobe or a new lover can stop the disease. And a proper journey can prevent its onset for a long time!
6. You are not alone.
Find yourself some soulmates. They might just give you a new lease of life."

"16.
Hello, Farnirras. I'm glad to be able to talk to you at last, though only via the written word. Have you already figured out who I am? I suspect you have, or else you wouldn't have put so much effort into hiding the phylactery.
That poor half-orc youngster cursed you, predicting you'd once meet ‘your worst enemy'. And that's how I was born — from the pieces of your soul that you haven't yet contaminated with evil. At first I was weak, and had barely enough power to steal a moment of life from the body we shared. While you slept, I rose and wandered the tower, trying to realize who I was and what should I do. Your protective spells didn't harm me — nor could they, for I was still you. The longer I thought about it, the more clearly I realized how disgusted I was by your life and your deeds. I dreaded to contemplate what you would do after you finally completed the ritual and turned undead. Would you follow the example of the cyclopean tyrants, whose ruined palaces serve as the foundation of Iobaria? Even the thought of it sickened me.
I started by trying to help your prisoners — a not entirely successful attempt, alas. But after they died, I realized that I had to do much more than that. I had to kill you… to kill both of us.
I share your curiosity, your magical powers, and your ability to invent unusual solutions. But even this wasn't enough for me to rid the world of us both. You've been fussing over your life too much, and your carefully tangled cocoon of protective spells would save us from every sort of potential danger. It would take days for me to try to untangle this web we'd created with our common hands. Besides, this might have made you suspicious and put you on alert — so I just had to remain undetected put my own plan in motion. In the short time I was awake, I worked over every piece of this magical prison, with our common phylactery being the key to it. I've enchanted the door so it will destroy the key after being opened, and would open only to the strongest monster-slayer. I developed a system of tests, to make ensure the one who would someday open this door would be capable enough. After all, he or she would have to face you in the end.
Well, my plan has worked. I've managed to lock us in here, inside this ancient cyclopean barrow. Our dear Iobaria was built upon the ruins of Koloran, and under these ruins, you and I will spend the upcoming years and ages. Some day, everything will work out as I have planned. Someone able to cut you down will enter this vault. I came to this world for one purpose only — to prepare my own death. And I cannot wait for this moment to finally come."

"2.
An unfortunate incident. Yesterday some thieves managed to break into the tower! They tried to free some of my test subjects. I do hate it when someone encroaches on my property. I hate it even more when useful resources are wasted. — The guardian golem and my protective spells killed five of the thieves before I had time to intervene. The sixth is still alive, and I hope he'll make it. A half-orc-sorcerer is exactly what I need for my experiments — perhaps the spells will work differently on him."
"4.
I've turned all the dead thieves into zombies. Then I pitted them against the will-o'-wisps and watched them fight through the window. It was a bit of fun, at least."
"6.
One of the test subjects was killed when I was trying to artificially slow the process of turning undead, with the intention of documenting all the stages precisely. Everything didn't go as planned. I think I shall repeat the experiment again in a week — and maybe this time I'll use the elven girl as a test subject. Her longer lifespan may, in theory, affect the duration of certain processes."
"8.
Today my test subjects have escaped. All of them! They acted so nimbly I hadn't noticed a thing when I went down to the cellar to prepare the next experiment. Well, the golem is malfunctioning — that's odd but within reason. But how did they manage to circumvent my whole system of protective spells?! I couldn't even identify which way they went after leaving the tower. It's obvious that some arcanist helped them escape — someone as capable as myself. Which is outstanding in itself! But even more surprising is that I didn't find him in the company of escapees, once I finally caught up with them. The fools ran into a wyvern's nest and nearly all of them perished. The only one I managed to save was the elven girl. She almost threw herself at me in relief, but then when she looked into my eyes, she shrieked and fainted."
"10.
After so much effort spent saving the elven girl, it was a pity I had to kill her. But time is of the essence. — After all the strange things that happened in the tower, I don't want to delay the ritual of phylactery creation. The last thing I need is a failure at the final stage — with two dozen years of hard work and my potential immortality at stake."
"12.
I must find out what's going on. It's impossible that my unknown enemy is so much stronger and craftier than I!"
"14.
The alchemy storage was not only burned to the ground. — Many ingredients were stolen before the rest was destroyed. Many artifacts were also stolen… I have a good idea of what purpose these will be put to. So, you steal from me, and you prepare a trap for me as well! But who are you? I'll find out. I'll most certainly find out."

"A Discourse by Trebricent of Cordelon on Trueborn versus Self-Proclaimed Rulers, or the Pitaxian Lion and the Flea of {kingdomname}.
... Shall I compare them to a lion and a flea? The former is strong, noble, and wise, his temper calm and his manner unhurried, for he is aware of his own grandeur. But one shouldn't stand in his way — his mere roar instills awe, and one blow of a clawed paw can smite anyone. Nature itself placed a crown upon his brow, urging other nations to surrender!
The other brings to mind a bug who can't see beyond its nose — a {mf|flea king|flea queen}, having spent some time at the court of a monkey ruling in Restov, rubbed against her skin and tasted her blood, {mf|he|she} imagines {mf|him|her}self worthy of a crown because {mf|his|her} belly is full of that which flows in veins of kings. And the monkey, who herself rules due to a misunderstanding, granted {mf|him|her} a title, appointing {mf|him|her} owner of a patch of uninhabited wasteland!
Printed out in Trebricent's Printshop, Littletown"
"A Thousand Revolutions"
"A bandit fort, a flourishing city, a cesspool of beasts. This place has a rich history! I admit, I missed it..."
"A barony of our own? That's quite an – undertaking. Ha ha ha!"
"A battle like the legends I used to read as a child!"
"A battle of spellcasters! Secrets of the unknown!"
"A battle worth being born for..."
"A bow."
"A commendable decision, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."

"A common law made up by bandits has lasted for centuries in the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}. It says that every troublemaker has the right to talk about whatever they like, that there is no law beyond an oath. Every tramp is free to wander wherever they want. – And no merchants are obliged to pay royal taxes."
"A curse upon you!"
"A deal? What deal would that be?"
"A death for a death!"
"A delightful dwelling indeed. — But I'm ready to flood it with blood, just say the word!"
"A demon?! That's impossible!"
"A feast in times of pestilence... A ludicrous attempt to sink into reverie, to digress from contemplating one's own insignificance..."
"A feud can be stronger than blood ties, and blood ties can be much like a feud."
"A fierce battle awaits us, but we are fighting for a good cause like never before."
"A fight with a deity from another world is not among my competencies, but the threat must nevertheless be neutralized."
"A fighting staff."
"A fire's burning inside me! Who wants to share in it?"
"A gloomy place. I hope this will soon be over. We'll save the kingdom, and return home!"
"A glorious day!"
"A good fight and no paperwork. Oh, I've missed this!"
"A good fight for Aldori swords!"
"A good fight. My trust in you was not in vain."
"A good joke is a powerful weapon. And a bad one can seal the joker's fate."
"A good master can always find a place… Ah, but without my tools!"
"A great celebration. It's nice to see smiling faces all around... and to forget our troubles for a while."
"A great deal of trust has been placed in you. Do not let Lady Aldori down!"
"A license, huh? Show me."
"A little more rain like this, and we'll be able to travel the barony by boat!"
"A living soul imprisoned in a dead body... Is this all I am now?"

"A long, long time ago, in a time before remembering, there was a furious god known as Rovagug, a terrible giant worm with a thousand teeth and claws. He devoured every world in his path, one after another. But the great gods were displeased with the beast, and delivered unto Rovagug their scourge. Many laid down their feuds to combine forces: mighty Torag, brilliant Sarenrae, vicious Asmodeus, crafty Calistria, cold-blooded Pharasma, and many, many others. Together, they faced Rovagug as he arrived to swallow Golarion.
The Goddess of the Sun, Sarenrae, forbade Rovagug's death, and so the gods imprisoned the fiend deep in the ground, shackled and sleeping. Asmodeus himself would keep the keys to his bonds. The terrible monster remains there still, asleep in his prison. Whenever Rovagug rolls over in his sleep and scratches his back against his prison walls, the earth trembles, and volcanoes spit fire."
"A mage acting like a soldier? That doesn't stop them from being a dodger and a coward. Don't trust anyone who avoids a fair fight."
"A monster might not... But I can try!"
"A most peculiar plant. Everything in this place is imbued with magic, but nothing near as much as this flower."
"A new place – a new life!"
"A new triumph of the brilliant Irovetti!"
"A nice inn, this one. Quiet and calm... usually..."
"A pinch of my world added to yours has made everything much more interesting, hasn't it?"
"A pirate gang led by Ilora Nuski worked for Irovetti."
"A pirate names himself such from the start, then has the audacity to ask for help! Life in the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g} is insane. They really need a change."
"A pleasure to meet you, Your Highness! Congratulations on your coronation."
"A problem demands your personal attention, Your Grace. Your acquaintance, Oleg, has been refusing to pay his taxes for months now, even though his trading post is located in your lands."
"A question about the traps..."
"A quick and painless death is the final mercy given to those like Ruthgert."
"A quiver of arrows."
"A rash decision. We'll reap its consequences soon enough..."
"A real fight, finally! No better feeling than cutting your ex-brethren's throats!"

"A rush of madness has passed, and a veil of darkness has been drawn. I managed to go further than before into the dungeon, without the risk of becoming a puppet to the forces of evil. I have returned with some powerful items. I think they will interest you."
"A sacred artifact of incredible power! The one who accepts it will build such an empire, all the glories of the past will pale!"
"A spear."
"A special piece? Why, of course, my pleasure! What sort exactly?"
"A stuck-up alchemist, a scribbler, a failed explorer, and a gluttonous gnome walk into a bar..."
"A thousand apologies, but there's absolutely nothing I can do without a workshop! Please, have one built for me. – Rest assured, the expense won't be wasted!"
"A toast to {mf|His|Her} Highness!"

"A town councilor was killed by dread magics and a shining stone in the last inn I stayed at. They invited two foreign experts to investigate. To be honest, magic murders were the least of that town's problems..."
"A true leader is someone who has their priorities straight, not someone who would put a valuable ally's life in danger for the sake of some servant."
"A very reckless decision. Very well, as you please."
"A warrior like Amiri would honor any tribe!"
"A wench? You? You're gonna need way more money than that to make up for that foul mug of yours..."
"A woman alone on the edge of the swamps... what are you hiding?"
"A woman named Rivel was trapped in the dungeon with her unborn child. The Wicked Chanter is her half-elf daughter. Why didn't you help them, Xelliren, before it was too late?"
"A wooden shield."
"A-a-ah!!! Did not expect this?!"
"A-and then I told him... Uh... Yeah, so h-he told me..."
"A-mi-ri! A-mi-ri!"
"AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!"
"AAAAAAAAAAAHHHH! Help!"
"AAAAAAAAH!"
"AAIIIEEEE! Enemies attack! Smash them!"
"ABYSS CALLS TO ABYSS."
"AH, HA HA!"
"ARRRGHHH… DEATH TO TYRANTS! DEATH TO JAILERS!"
"Aaa! Longshanks!"
"Aaaaa!"
"Aaaaaaaaa!"
"Aaaaaaaah!"
"Aaaaah!"
"Aaaaargh… Ooooohhh..."
"Aaaahhh!"
"Aaannd, there you go. No more license."

"Abandon hope and embrace the inevitable end." – That's the kind of speech that Harrim's companions must endure. Every. Single. Day. A priest of Groetus, Harrim left his dwarven home to spread the word of the God of End Times throughout the Stolen Lands. Although if you ask me, Harrim's just a whiner – a one of a kind!

"According to legend, it gave its owners control over planar travel. But only pairs of wizards bound by unbreakable ties could use it. While one of them traveled the planes, the other was his 'anchor' in our world, and they could switch between. Do you see now why we so desperately wish to find the Disk? It might help us understand how the 'switch' between me and Kanerah works. And it should make our divine patron happy. – Nethys and his assistants value the desire to understand the mysteries of magic above all else."
"Achoo! Goddess, save me from a cold..."
"Achoo! It was much easier to walk through knee-deep snow when I was twenty years younger..."
"Acid can still kill you, so you're not truly immortal. Allow me to demonstrate."
"Actually, I just wanted to watch you run. Better keep it up, or..."
"Actually, I rule these lands."
"Actually... there is something..."

"After his death, a rebellion broke out. — That's nothing new for {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g}. As his accidental killer, I was named the rebellion's leader. But I assure you I fled the first moment I could — leapt upon my ship and set sail. A month later I found out I'd become the main reason for a great tragedy, and an enemy of the Chelish people."

"After two years in the Tenebrous Depths, I've come further than any before me, and have nearly reached my goal – a passage to the place where the Spawn slumbers. But I fear that I am lost. Not in the dungeon, no. In my own soul.
Two years I have spent in a place imbued with the magic of madness. I have discovered all the strange and horrifying secrets of this place, and now I write in a vain charade, as if anyone will ever read these words. I have summoned a deadly beast from the Abyss, and kept it on a tight leash. It waits in ravenous quiet for the chance to devour my soul. In my spare time I've taught it to read and write in some of the languages I know. The monster's horrible visage is the last thing I see before I sleep, and the first thing I look upon when I awaken.
What are you contemplating, Zirhaische? When you first appeared inside the summoning circle, when I tore you from the Astral Plane, you shook with rage at the one who would dare subdue you. You were so different then. A wild predator, with but a single thought – the hunting of souls. Now I see something different in your eyes – something I cannot classify.
Perhaps this final riddle is the last thing keeping me alive. I am among the greatest dark wizards of my age, and here I am, dying in fear.
Before I ventured into the Tenebrous Depths, I knew exactly who I was and what I wanted. Hundreds of times, I've bathed my hands in blood, feeling no pang of conscience. I've sacrificed a dozen babes, without a care. Many among the hundreds I've killed appeared quite innocent.
But now... who am I now? Trapped within this crazy scheme, to save the pitiful River Kingdoms. They will be destroyed in one fell swoop, should the Spawn ever awaken. For two years I have wandered this darkness, finding epitaphs of all the other would-be conquerors of the Tenebrous Depths. I have studied each closely, and I scarcely even noticed when I first began to... pity them...
And most absurd of all – yesterday I risked my life to save my daemon. It is a slave, summoned for the exact purpose of protecting me! I saw Zirhaische facing a horde of beasts from the depths, and I revealed myself to cover him with a magic shield. It was our greatest fight yet in the Tenebrous Depths, and it's a miracle that we both survived.
It is time for my confession. I recognize what a monster I once was, and repent. I now go to face the Spawn, my head held high, and atone for the evil that I have done.
But no. It will not be. Yes, I am but one step away from the end of the nightmare from the Tenebrous Depths. But I refuse to awaken! If I cannot be healed and become my former self again, then I will die before becoming someone else.
Tomorrow I will lift the subduing spell from my daemon. Then we shall see, Zirhaische, how deeply you crave your master's soul. I shall perish utterly, but that will only be the beginning of my story. I will die with a smile on my face, inviting the Spawn of Rovagug to awaken to a feast of blood."
"After what we've been doing, no monster is going to surprise me!"
"After what we've been up to, no adventure could surprise me!"
"Agai said this one is not an enemy."
"Again, Reg? Please don't. Just leave him alone."
"Again, that was you, not me. I'm just supplying a demand, got that? All right, lads, get him out of here already!"
"Age after age, generation after generation..."
"Ages."
"Ah ha ha!"
"Ah! My ears are freezing!"
"Ah! My respects!"
"Ah, Tiressia, we would have missed so many miracles, had we stayed in our forest!"
"Ah, and here's the old lizard now. So..."

"Ah, guests. You are standing on the threshold of the castle of Hargulka, the troll king." {n}Each word comes out as a rasp, like steel dragged across stone.{/n} "King Hargulka not invited you, borba." {n}The trolls surrounding him stare at you silently, hate in their eyes.{/n}
"Ah, he is such a joker! The locals must be thrilled that he's brightened up their humdrum life!"
"Ah, here you are! Right on time. We've rebuffed the first attack of these dark creatures, and we're expecting another one any time."
"Ah, my beautiful peacock! You can't tell love from gold. You sell and you buy, you rob and steal..."
"Ah, snowfall! I hear it's good for the crops!"
"Ah, this ball is pure poetry!"

"Ah, tongue. One can flap one's tongue. Traps are things to be shut." {n}The gnome's face withers under Amiri's glare.{/n} "I... I just wanted... for purely academic purposes..." {n}He falls silent and steps behind you.{/n}
"Ah, yes... I see good old Restov hasn't changed a bit. Even the smell in the streets is the same."
"Ah, {mf|King|Queen} {Name}! We've heard so much about you!"

"Ah, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, do you really expect gratitude from {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}? I need scarcely remind you that the elves can be quite arrogant towards their neighbors, and are unlikely to offer any generous gifts in return."
"Ah-coo! I think I caught a cold! Why won't kobolds give their prisoners a warm blanket?"
"Aha! See?!"
"Ahem, ah... So much smoke!"
"Ahem. I had a feeling some disaster just bound to happen today. Let's go!"
"Ahem. Uh, thanks, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}."
"Ahem... can you hear me?"
"Ahey, Your Highness! Come over here! Got all that useful stuff lying around..."
"Ahhh!" {n}Waine breaks into a sprint. He stumbles, gets back on his feet, and continues to run without looking back.{/n}
"Aid me, warmblood! This Thickskin, they no mercy!"
"Aiii! Protect treasure!"
"Alarm! Alarm! Call the Stag Lord!"
"Alarm! Get spears! Kill warmbloods!"
"Alarm! Warn the Stag Lord!"

"Alas, those who've left for Pharasma's chambers are eternally separated from the living. But there is still one more soul that cries out for salvation — the wounded soul of the murderer who committed such a dark act."

"Alas, we cannot change what's done, and some evil deeds cannot be remedied. But even dark evil can be atoned for with good acts — a barren desert can still give way to a lush garden, and a soul suffering in darkness can still find its way to light."

"Alchemy is the triune science of: primes, or basic elements, of which all things are composed; forces, by which those things are set in motion; and families of all such things which a studious mind can perceive in our world. An art most formidable, it grants its practitioner power over nature, and even over that which beyond nature lies; he who has mastered it fully shall become like the gods, yet woe be unto he who sets about its study without diligence and zeal, for his days are numbered. The path ahead is perilous and arduous in equal measure, and he who sets his foot upon it heedlessly shall not find wisdom, but only a quick and grisly end."

"Alick's gonna marry Martha, you see," {n}the third man adds,{/n} "so we were gonna carve their names into this trunk here. I was gonna carve a picture of her tits, too, but Alick said that was too bold."

"Alkenstar is halfway around the world. You see, magic... how can I put this... It doesn't work in our lands. Don't ask me why. That's a question for the researchers and historians. But we ordinary people of Alkenstar managed to turn this nuisance to the greater good."
"All art is illusion, but not every illusion is worthy of being called art..."
"All clear, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!"
"All day in the sun... when's the next shift already?"
"All day on the watch... could really go for a pint right about now..."
"All dead, huh?"
"All dogs try to bite their master eventually. They shouldn't."
"All fear go away."
"All for the glory of Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}, of course," {n}the bandit leader says with a grin.{/n}
"All go — all fall... What trouble..."
"All go... all fall… Sssorrow, sssorrow…"
"All is lost..."
"All is... Lost... No... Hope..."

"All matter is, in itself, both poison and cure – like water, which lies at the foundation of every process. All living things perish without water; all living things shall drown if in water submerged, for even a fish leaps from its lake each day to breathe in the air. All other matter succumbs to this universal law. That which the unlearned call poison is only the measure of a substance that the body which imbibes it cannot overcome. However, if diluted threefold, fivefold, even tenfold, that same substance may affect the body much differently, strengthening or cleansing it. Therefore, not every poison-maker is a villain, as is often believe among the common herd. The art of handling poison is neither dark nor evil in itself..."
"All of high society is here — even Natala Surtova. There could be an assassination, a provocation... anything!"

"All of this sounds like the work of the Ebon Destroyers Cult. They are servants of Dhalavei, the goddess of unmaking and secrets, of ruin and degradation. Perhaps you know her by another name. She appears as a beautiful three-headed woman with deep black skin and dark hair. Her servants range from monks and priests to politicians to the undead. You may trust in this, for I have heard it spoken by a severed eunuch's head, who was among their victims. Most of Dhalavei's cultists are pathetic rejects of the lower castes, who are of no interest to the other gods. Together with Vasaghati, her spirit sister, Dhalvei brings death and decay. The Ebon Destroyers seek out secrets, while the Knife in the Dark, Vasaghati's cult, can infiltrate the ranks of any organization and slowly destroy it from within."
"In the ocean that surrounds Vudra lies an island known as Gho Vella. It is a land of lepers, and those who live there suffer from incurable curses and afflictions. Certainly, the gods do not burden pious men with contagion, for all such affliction is a lesson meant to show that a man has led a sinful life, and to show others they'd be wise not to know him. Trust me, for I myself have seen men struck with leprosy on the very spot for their woeful ways! A group of philosophers, known as the Curse Shepherds, has taken upon itself the duty of seeking out those punished by the gods. Their black boats ferry the misfortunate to Gho Vella where they may contemplate their sins in peace."
"I have heard of the First World. The ratfolk practitioners of the ancient art of rantagi have long led their caravans between the worlds, through breaches they make in the fabric of reality. Trust me, for one of them ventured into the first world and revealed the truth of it to me. Once this wondrous world was the home of the heavenly harems and treasuries of the gods. Their slaves, however, rebelled against their masters, craving their masters' power for their own. For their insolence, the gods separated themselves from the First World, and instead created for themselves Nirvana. Their slaves remained in their old homes, and were henceforth known as Asura – rejected servants. They serve as a reminder of the cataclysm one causes when denying one's rightful place in the cycle of reincarnation, and living blasphemy. They hate the gods for their condition, and seek to avenge it. Do not trust the Asura of the First World, for none of them wish you well!"
"All of this was a long, long joke... And you're the punch line! Let's have a laugh together!"
"All of this was just a long, long joke... And you're the punch line! Come closer, let's have a laugh together!"
"All right, Amiri. He's yours."
"All right, I get mood swings sometimes too. Such stupid thoughts... I love you too."
"All right, I'll hire you. But only if you promise to straighten yourselves out and quit banditry."
"All right, I'll hire you. The {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} has been lacking manpower recently. But all the taxes you collect WILL go to the barony treasury."
"All right, Octavia. Try to calm him down."
"All right, but then the castle should go in a feverish swamp!"
"All right, cut it out. You should settle down as well, neighbor. Let your son grow up and make his own decisions. Maybe they'll let him work underground after all!"
"All right. Let's try to keep our love alive."
"All the best, baron{mf||ess}. I hope this warrior serves you better than her goddess."
"All the members of old families kidnapped by Irovetti are dead. Their bones lie at the bottom of the underground pond at Whiterose Abbey."
"All the more reason not to linger. Farewell."
"All the rum is stored behind that locked door. Let's bring in a cannon from the ship. A single shot, and the rum is ours!"
"All the tombs around the town make me feel uneasy. Like we settled down in a giant cemetery!"
"All these shrines make me feel uneasy."
"All tribe like exiles now."
"All who fall to their knees and devotes themselves to the Goddess will be cleansed."
"Ally! Come join us!"
"Ally! We look for useful thing around, bring you! Honest!"
"Ally! We rest war now, make new war soon! You come again!"
"Ally, I help you! Lead my mite to battle! Big fight us come. Sweet!"
"Almost gone, don't miss your chance!"
"Alright then. I have to go."
"Although… if you promise…" {n}The elf looks at you with hope in his eyes.{/n} "I'll tell you if you promise to help me!"
"Always put a broom in conspicuous place. Everyone will think that you are so busy!"
"Amateurs! Who taught you to hold the ritual like this?"
"Amazing! You managed to get them to reconcile. Good work! I thought a fight was inevitable."
"Amid the whirl of steel and blood, a warrior finds peace!"
"Amiri is no longer our sister, but she is a hero — and people will sing of her to the end of time."
"Amiri is so powerful! And we drove her away!"
"Amiri! She has the nerve to show her face among us again!"
"Amiri! We need Amiri!"
"Amiri, stop! Enough — he's already got what he deserves!"
"Amiri... breathe... for the lassst time..."
"An Ancient Curse" Quest
"An absolutely incomprehensible decision. Then again, that's nothing new..."
"An armory! I'm sure Jamandi wouldn't mind if we borrowed some weapons!"
"An attack is no reason to break into rooms in someone else's house and pocket their property."

"An egg laid by the abominable {g|Rovagug}Rovagug{/g} has cursed this dungeon for thousands of years. The larva of the Beast will destroy half of the River Kingdoms if it hatches. The shell that surrounds it is a labyrinth of darkness and madness, inhabited by thousands of its former victims. Hundreds of heroes perished as they sought a way through it. But now I know where the egg is, and the path to it is almost clear. Almost..."
"An empire once so great... where is your strength? Does the same fate await us? No answer..."
"An extremely short-sighted decision, Your Highness."
"An honor to meet you!"
"An impossible task? No. Let your unrequited love guide you — it guided you to your first kingdom, so it shall again."
"An unheard-of atrocity! Mark my words: we'll find out who was behind it!"
"Ancestor wise! Ancestor know better!"
"Ancient faith returned to holy walls."

"And I can bring them here! The only sure way to get here was the portal at the Castle of Knives. The location of this place keep changing – it's the First World after all. But now when I'm here, I can summon my friends from Golarion."
"And I thought it was I who had complicated relationships…"
"And I will get it, and perhaps more besides. And the shadows from the Cup will help me do it."
"And I'd like to know the names of all your players. Do you have any idea how dangerous demons can be?"
"And I'm not surprised, not even a little bit. Fanatics…"
"And I'm to serve shoulder to shoulder with these people?! Maybe following you wasn't as good an idea as I thought..."
"And I'm... I'm a cook! This isn't a sword, it's just a kitchen knife!"
"And a deal's a deal. So cough up our money, sweetheart."
"And a waterfall! Now I see why the Taldans decided to settle here. I'd live here too!"
"And did I make you try it? Did I make you pawn everything you own? No, that was you. It's your problem, not mine."
"And here comes the dessert! How delightful! Come, my sweet: I cannot wait to taste your dying pain!"
"And how are we supposed to return to peaceful life after this? At lease, I'm grateful Svetlana doesn't see this…"
"And how did this Disk come to be in the Stolen Lands?"
"And how is it you began to live 'in turns'?"
"And how is that MY problem?"
"And it is! See, those there are magic runes..."
"And leave the city for that gods-forsaken bog?! If you wish to scramble in the dirt to the end of your life, you can go there yourself, thank you very much!"
"And now I shall return to the place of my vigil. These wounds are well-deserved, but they will heal."
"And now that you've got all your papers in order, you can build and extend to your heart's content!"
"And now — farewell!"

"And now, with the competition over and the prize awarded, let's get on with the main part of the celebration — the banquet! I can hear your stomachs growling from here — let's get to the table! And later, we'll see an unforgettable fireworks show!"
"And now... Hello, dessert!"
"And on they walked, through the white gloom..."
"And remember the Blacksoul Tomb? That gods-forsaken cave in Varisia?"
"And she didn't do a single love ballad! Damn."
"And so begins a glorious story that'll win over all of Golarion! The first page is being written here and now!"
"And thanks to whoever did — before {mf|him|her}, no one could even hope to fight the Stag Lord's power!"
"And that day, nary a single lich sitting atop piles of treasure was found..."
"And the building in front of us is your residence. That's where we'll head to now."
"And the way he looks at you, it's like he's examining you. Like he's considering to crack you open to see what's inside. The chills!" {n}Dalton shivers.{/n}

"And then Irovetti appeared. We underestimated him, thought him nothing more than another adventurer like the thousands of others in the region. He handled matters quickly and chaotically, with assets running through his fingers faster than chips at a card table. His wealth grew rapidly, but he still wasn't a big fish... for a while, at least."
"And then again... And again!"
"And then you..."
"And then, we were seven. Seven paladins of Iomedae."

"And then..." {n}The goblin hangs his head.{/n} "He strike me in my ears and said I can tell it to beast bellies. He do that a lot recently, to many, many now in beast bellies. But not Nok-Nok, no way Nok-Nok can die! Lama protects me!"

"And there is one more gift we offer – the word of truth. We have long meditated, seeking knowledge of the power that opens portals. Here is what was revealed to us. The one you've been fighting since the day you set foot in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}, she is not only the fountain of evil, but its greatest victim. As she prepares to sting you with her dagger, a sword hangs above her head, in the hands of another. It is in your power to save her – if you would brave the wrath of those who could make even her tremble."
"And they didn't arrest him? I mean, isn't he technically a criminal?"
"And to die at such an old age, peacefully, asleep in his own bed..."
"And to whom will you be complaining?"
"And us being quick and smart, their stuff's now ours. Clothes and all."
"And what about a love song? Something to make our souls weep!"
"And what about you? Aren't you worried for your husband?"
"And what did this criminal do, exactly?"
"And what do I get in return if I help you?"
"And what do you know?"
"And what gold would that be?"
"And what happened to the other party members?"
"And what have we here?"
"And what role do you picture yourself in? You'll hit or take the hits? Hehe-ahemmm... No, don't answer. Let it be a surprise for me."
"And what shall I do with this one?"
"And what will your dying pain taste like? Let's find out!"
"And what'd that get them, huh? Hundreds of deaths, maybe more! No, no one's right in this feud, no matter what you say."
"And what'll I do with it?! My wife'll kill me if she finds out I knocked up a maid!"
"And what? Why should someone else be deciding what my child can or can't do for a career?"
"And where exactly do you expect me to work? Right here, on the ground, out in the open? First provide me with a forge, then you can demand results!"
"And where is Kaessi? She was supposed to wait for us here!"
"And who are you?"
"And why is there a river under the ground? Are there fish in it? What about mermaids? I'll go look for the mermaids!"
"And why is your face so grim?" {n}Octavia says sharply.{/n} "Did you study grimacing in some academy?"
"And why should I concern myself with what the thieves' guild is doing? Truth be told, I think the bloodbrush extract is no more harmful than well-aged wine!"
"And why, pray tell, would you and Cephal drag me into an alliance with daemon worshipers, if now we're going to betray them?"
"And yet I welcome you, and would see you among my assistants. Oh, but why use words if I can show you..."
"And yet I'm saying no. To put it bluntly, you are asking me to betray a friend who I deeply respect. Some friend would I be if I gave in to blackmail!"
"And yet, I'm still not certain I can trust you..."
"And you can't control these 'switches'?"
"And you don't like it, you're free to go. We're truly free — no one tells us what to do."
"And you're already familiar with every nook and cranny here, aren't you?"
"And you're happy to help them?!"
"And you... You become just like those murderers and thieves!"
"And you... You...!"
"And, just as before, it shall remain a cruel thing to do."
"And?"
"And?" {n}The elf peers at you with wide-open eyes.{/n}
"Annoying little thing die now!"
"Another brawl with the Swordlords? When are they going to give it up?"
"Another button's lost… And this patch — it just won't hold, the threads are already wearing out… Torag, oh, Torag, why do you treat mortals in such a malevolent way..."
"Another mediocrity I'll sweep away!"
"Another of Nyrissa's shelters. Everything here screams of suffering, despair and anger."
"Any information about the First World would be useful."
"Any other dangers on the road?"
"Anyone who stands under the enemy's banner will be crushed by the same unrelenting force that inspires me."
"Anyone... Open the door, I beg you!"
"Anyway, it's much easier to breathe in the open air than in this... eatery. I have no idea what you're doing here, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}."
"Anyway, poor guy almost soiled his pants — must've been terrified by his own tall tales!"
"An… interesting… decision. Especially in light of other decisions Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness} has made earlier." {n}"Maegar" grins at you knowingly.{/n} "But as you wish."
"Apologies, friend. We came here to kill Kargadd, and anyone else we found."
"Apology."
"Apsu, father... Do not abandon me!"
"Apsu? Who is that?"
"Ar-mag! Ar-mag! Ar-mag!"
"Are they coming?"
"Are you Amiri? That sword… Thief!!"
"Are you both insane?!" {n}Octavia shouts.{/n} "Keeping a living creature in a cage, torturing it... This is inhumane!"
"Are you going to let this savage rob someone before your very eyes?!"
"Are you hurt?"
"Are you looking for a gift from your god? What if it's been under your bed all this time?"
"Are you mad?! Attacking your own people to help some freak? You're scum!"
"Are you out of your mind?! There, look, there is Erastil's symbol above the chimney! I serve the hunter's god!"
"Are you prepared to keep fighting for those who never appreciate you? Those who despise you and think you a monster?"
"Are you saying the Honest Guy isn't fair? That I have no shame?!"
"Are you scared?"
"Are you serious? You think we'll be able to live in peace with them? It would be great... I hope you're not wrong!"

"Are you seriously going to judge whether Valerie is favored by Shelyn, based on her saving some guards from a fire?! Why? Would followers of other gods turn away from dying innocents?! Valerie's behavior was common decency, not a sign of special respect for Shelyn!"
"Are you suggesting I should drag myself all the way to the capital? No way. It's your own fault you ran all the way out here. But now we've got you!"
"Are you the one who helped Darven protect Brineheart? Thank you!"
"Are you... embarrassed? I didn't think you were capable of it."
"Are you? Am I the only one who sees that?"
"Aren't you hungry yet? Let's stop and eat something!"
"Aren't you tired of living? We could help with that!"
"Argh. What's happening to me? Help!"

"Argun was knocked flat. He laid gasping, arms spread, a lump of rage rising in his throat. He remembered his dream. Black soil, red ravens in the empty sky, their coarse croaks ringing in his ears, like a taunt...
Choral would never take Rostland! Never! Aldori sprang to his feet, as if the blood-soaked soil was driving him forward. With a cry of rage, the Swordlord rushed into the battle. The sky turned scarlet with blood, as he furiously chopped off his enemies' heads. The scarlet horizon drew closer, and its roar nearly drowned out the sound of battle. Argun looked to the sky, and a fiery blast descended upon him. These were no ravens that circled above him. The fearsome breath of the Red Dragons of Choral melted the soldiers' armor and turned living flesh to ash and dust..."
"Armag abandoned us!"
"Armag can no longer be trusted!"
"Armag remembers his duty. Count on me!"
"Armag will flay you!"
"Armag's a traitor!"
"Armag's not chieftain anymore!"
"Armag, a traitor?! That scum!"
"Arrest him and deliver him to the judge for trial. His gang won't give up without a fight, so we're permitted to use force where necessary, but there will be no mob justice!"
"As I proposed?" {n}Bartholomew catches your eye hopefully, but then loses interest.{/n} "I see. Simple coining. Without applying my wise and thrifty advice. Not that you've ever paid attention."
"As far as I can tell, not one person in this family possesses the ability to think through the consequences of their actions!"
"As for bandits, we're not afraid of them. They don't cross us because we don't have two coins to scrape together."
"As if Jamandi best not learn where we live! If there were an envoy was with us, I would already be feeding them misinformation!"
"As if we can't see that someone is trying to run down the clock. Oh, if you only knew as much about stretching time as we do..."
"As if! We fought off bandits twice to protect your wares! Barely made it out alive, but all your cargo's intact. And now you want to cheat us?!"
"As proof of your unfaltering loyalty?"
"As usual, the masters celebrate while us grunts have to work."

"As you command, boss — er, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}." {n}The bandit leader's face is almost glowing with joy.{/n} "We'll finish sorting things out here, then head straight to your capital. Everyone, you best thank {mf|His|Her} {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness} now."
"As you say. I'll gladly tell you all that I know. What else can an old man like me do?"
"As you say."
"As you sought to steal a kingdom for yourself, so must you do again, a thousand times over. For a theft, a true theft, must be practiced to be earned."
"As you wish, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}". {n}After some hesitation, Kesten continues:{/n} "However, tensions are rising. I hope we do not come to regret this decision."
"As you wish, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}. I must inform you, however, that this decision will prove costly."
"As you wish, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}. Please, be my guest."
"As you wish. But know this: no matter what shadow darkens your soul, there are those unafraid to enter it and reach toward the kindness you hide in your wounded heart."
"As you wish. But trust me, you're making a huge mistake."
"As you wish. Do not be surprised, however, when this opera casts you in a much different light than you'd prefer."
"As you wish. I'll think of something."
"As you wish. So are you buying anything? Fair trade is my principle!"
"As you wish. We would not bind you to anything, but be assured, if someday you decide to accept the Wise Way, we shall welcome you with open arms."
"Ashes and dust — that's what this dwarf is. It would be amusing to find out how strong his faith is."
"Ashes."
"Ask Hassuf! He'll tell you himself!"
"Assist me!"
"At last! If I make it out of this alive, I'll never set foot in these lands again!"
"At last... free..."
"At least I don't tell passers by that I'm just waiting for the chance to rob their dead bodies."
"At least I'll still be alive."
"At least it looks better than the paintings king Irovetti awards his prizes to!"
"At least there is one ancient evil here – and today I will destroy it!"
"At the end, he said he knew where the barbarian chieftain's buried, promised he could show us."
"Atonement."
"Attack {mf|King|Queen} {Name}!"
"Attack!! Follow Armag, warriors!"
"Attack!"
"Attacking one who was cleared of all charges by Shelyn herself! And in the temple of the goddess! Unbelievable!"
"Avant-garde at its best!" {n}Octavia laughs.{/n} "But, frankly speaking, there were even odder... pieces of art... stored in my masters' galleries."
"Aw, cut him some slack. Everyone who lived there was scared of that hole."
"Away with Irovetti! Hail freedom!"
"Away! Byrk getting angry."
"Away, witch. Your deceitful words may touch my ears, but not my heart."

"Aye, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}, we're ready and willing to serve. We'll take a pledge right now, if you want. We'll kiss your boots, your ass, whatever you need! We're sick to death of hiding in the woods and sleeping in the dirt. Why be bandits when we could take from traders legal-like?"

"Aye, and the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} himself's quite the man, too. Bet he'd do more overnight than you could handle in a month!" {n}Berta glances at you.{/n} "Say, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}, would ya care to take me to your fairy-tale castle?"
"Aye, you sure had yourself a time of it! If you forgot yourself, no matter, the locals will be sure to remind you — for a long time to come."
"Back when I was a slave, I would sometimes see my masters behave like this. It seemed to happen after inhaling some kind of drug. The same slow movements, incoherent muttering, drooling..."
"Bad party. Short on food".
"Bah! What does he think we're doing here, having a tea party?" {n}Grumbles Regongar, playing with his weapon.{/n}
"Bandits? Nonsense! We're the Free Forest Brotherhood!"
"Barbarians, you say? If I remember their customs correctly..."

"Bard Battle of the Century!
Unrivaled Annamede Belavarah to share stage with two foreign stars!
Annamede's adversaries:
Maestro Ranunculus, the silver-tongued heart-stealer from faraway lands! Performs love lyrics and historical sketches.
K.R., the towering troll bard from across the sea! Performs a set of ballads about his travels in mysterious, ancient dungeons.
Event sponsored by Pitax City's esteemed magistrate. For tickets, contact your town hall representatives."
"Bard Battle of the Century!"
"Barely survived..."
"Baron Hannis Drelev, the new master of Glenebon. Captain Maegar Varn, the conqueror of Dunsward. And finally..."

"Baron Maegar Varn,
I am writing to you as your ally and well-wisher. The reason for my letter is the lack of foresight in your actions. You're trying so hard to become friends with the ruler of the Shrike Hills barony. You invite your neighbor to pay you a visit, you even send rich gifts. Have you nothing more to do in your lands? I strongly recommend you to stop flirting with this upstart person and turn your gaze to the affairs of the day. You are trying to cross the path with powerful forces that can reach you even in your own castle. You should know your place.
With wishes of good health and calm sleep,
your friend"

"Baron Maegar Varn,
I am writing to you as your ally and well-wisher. The reason for my letter is the lack of foresight in your actions. You're trying so hard to become friends with this {mf|baron|baroness} from {kingdomname}. You invite {mf|him|her} to pay you a visit, you assure {mf|him|her} of sincerity, you even send rich gifts. Have you nothing more to do in your lands? I strongly recommend you to stop flirting with this upstart person and turn your gaze to the affairs of the day. You are trying to cross the path with powerful forces that can reach you even in your own castle. You should know your place.
With wishes of good health and calm sleep,
your friend"
"Baron! Baron! Kjerdi is looking for you urgently!"
"Baron! General! It was a pleasure doing business with you!"
"Bastard!"
"Battle in the Valley of Fire" by Lurus Aldori
"Be careful — nothing is what it seems here. Especially the chests! And the doors, the doors!"
"Be damned, all you two-legged monsters..."
"Be my peacock. Shine. You will become a king whose glory shall overshadow all within the River Kingdoms."
"Be on your way."
"Be quiet! You all scare {mf|him|her} off!"
"Be silent, you've led us into enough messes for the day, don't let your tongue lead you into another."

"Be warned that the Captor does not appear alone. He is always accompanied by a disgusting beast that he summoned from beyond the world. The two are firmly bound in death, and can revive each other, so they must both be killed at once."
"Be."
"Beassst not wake!"
"Beast be hungry! Run!"
"Beautiful places!"
"Beautiful weather for a battle! Although I admit, I do prefer feasts and hunting..."
"Because we paid too little and he held a grudge! I told you. 'Don't be greedy,' I said. 'Get your stash out of your boot.' And what did you do...?" {n}The villager gestures frantically.{/n}
"Beg for mercy, mortal worm! I'll make a rattle-toy from your bones!"
"Beings like me must be healed with negative energy. Try something else — you may be surprised by the effect."
"Belly on fire! Head be stone! And ground go round — oooh!"
"Bet 500 gold coins on the blue team."
"Bet 500 gold coins on the red team."
"Betrayed! Abandoned! Ran away! Cowards, cowards!"
"Better."

"Between the bogs of the River Kingdoms and the infertile clay soils of Brevoy, lies the region called the Stolen Lands – a picturesque area, which combines the worst features of both previously mentioned countries. It's a woodland, where herds of deer, swarms of mosquitoes and gangs of bandits have their pastures. Though the latter were formidably decreased in numbers thanks to the efforts of the local baron{mf||ess} – a protégée of the Restov Swordlords who's promised to bring some resemblance of order to these lands. Hoping to learn to what degree {mf|he|she} succeeded, your faithful servant went to the Stolen Lands himself.
Certainly, I preceded my visit with a letter, but mailing service in this new barony functions with an efficiency of zero. No one came to greet me, except for a horde of hungry kobolds — here these creatures can be met way more often than guardsmen or, let's say, street cleaners. I barely managed to fight off those pests, then I narrowly escaped drowning on the river ford. The only thing here more rarely met than a paved road is a good, well-maintained bridge. Every ruler ought to remember that the realm's roads are {mf|his|her} face, and here they are filthy and in a desperate need of good old stone.
After all those misadventures, I finally reached the capital. Compared to other parts of the barony, the city looks relatively good, despite the smell. I should give credit to the ruler's efforts: there's building in progress everywhere. Passing-by traders praise the Baron{mf||ess} for eliminating the bandits and express hopes that someday {mf||s}he'll deal with the wildland monsters as well.
I wouldn't recommend that you choose this destination for your summer vacation, but if you are tough and unpretentious, if you can work hard and defend yourself, you might try your luck here – working hands are in great demand in the capital. Also, there are plenty of jobs for sellswords and free adventurers – after all, the local baron{mf||ess} used to be one of them not so long ago. As for me, I guess I'll stay here for a while to watch how the new barony grows. If I don't drown in some swamp, become a snack for some owlbeast or die of dysentery, we'll meet in the next issue!"
"Beware false rulers! Their foul walls and rotten locks will not protect their henchmen from nature's wrath."
"Bite their hand, kick their teeth! Cut their scalps and bring to chief!"
"Blasphemers! How could you say that?!"
"Blishhhfulneshh?"
"Blishhhfulness."
"Blissfulneshhh?"
"Blood for Gorum!"
"Blood! I thirst for blood!"
"Blood! Sweet, bright blood!"

"Bold dog barks loud... while cunning one readies to bite. Cunning, short, but stubborn. He is now in an ancient tomb that lies south of the {g|Oleg's Trading Post}trading post{/g}. Searching for the great power that once gave joy, and now brings only death. You don't want my nonsense? Then you'll hear sobs and screams.
Once stolen, the land should be reclaimed... Once reclaimed, bound with the claimer shall it be. Bound, merged, joined by unbreakable ties. Claiming the land, claiming its pain, claiming its death..."
"Boo! Scared? Don't be. I'm not a Jabberwock. No, though I'm far worse..."
"Booo! Armag's a traitor!"
"Booo!"
"Booooo!"

"Dedication
When we speak of the fine arts of Pitax, we must always keep in mind our great ruler — King Irovetti, our patron and philanthropist. Poetry means Irovetti and Irovetti means poetry, and so it will always be as long as at least one poet still composes stanzas within these blessed lands.
The poet's heart is like a fluttering goldfinch in the tender arms of a girl, and within Pitax, the heart of every bard reacts to Irovetti's name with that same fluttering. Each rhyme of this anthology was born under the shadow of the wings of our wise King's fatherly love. Each line is imbued with blood shed on the battlefield beneath the victorious royal banner. Each symbol burns with the heat of the defeated enemies of Pitax.
We create poetry, and our King helps us to capture that elusive imagery. We fight, and our King covers us with an invisible shield. We set out in search for new lands, and our King waters the parched lips of the tired travelers with life-giving moisture.
Wherever we are, whatever we do, our ruler is always with us. He soars above us like an invisible guardian angel. And with indescribable pride, we dedicate this collection of poems, 'The Lyre and the Sword,' to that Great Patron of Arts, King Irovetti. May His heavenly azure soul flourish along with His unfading mind and His invulnerable body!"

"Do you know what irony is? It's when you are a dark wizard steeped in blood to the elbows, when suddenly a silver dragon comes to you in your dreams, entreating you to perform a noble feat and save a few feeble kingdoms from the Spawn of Rovagug. At first I couldn't even come up with an answer. I've done many colorful things in my life – mass ritual murders, for example. But not feats. Never feats.
What made me agree in the end? Curiosity, perhaps. And vanity. The dragon had given me enough information to excite both. The Spawn of Rovagug slumbered in the depths. A sphere of madness surrounded it. Many heroes had been summoned, only to fail in the task. It sounded like a perfect challenge for my skills.
Besides, I had long desired to test a hypothesis – that kinder, nobler souls are far more susceptible to madness. I have often thought how fragile and cumbersome all these lofty ideals and strict morals must be. How crushing, how blinding, the need to suppress one's selfish impulses – the essence of what others call 'goodness'. Then it all crumbles under external pressures and internal contradictions, and the mind and spirit lie in ruins. 'What have I have to fear?' I asked myself. 'I, who has never been tormented by the pangs of conscience, and always act with cold-blooded premeditation?'
So I agreed to the dragon's proposal, and took myself down to conquer the Tenebrous Depths.
My approach is different from the other heroes who came here. There's no point in rushing forward haphazardly, hoping to accomplish the goal in one daring attack. I move slowly, studying the magic background of the dungeon, capturing local creatures and using them for experiments and sacrifices. I must admit, this place is significantly more dangerous than I expected. I've already had to fight for my life twice, and fallen exhausted afterwards.
I think I shall require an assistant, someone who can drive away the monsters while I'm busy with my research. My skills easily enable me to summon and bind a powerful servant. But will this be enough?
I've been thinking recently... What if rational, cold-blooded scoundrels like me are nevertheless susceptible to madness? Only for us, madness manifests in needlessly risking everything in noble escapades. – Like my crusade here to this damned dungeon."

I've reached Varnhold — a stronghold of civilization. Here, I shall start my search for that which shall forever put my name in the annals of Golarion. Long ago, ancient kingdoms flourished here, but it is unlikely anyone has ever conducted a proper excavation in these wilds. I, Willas Gunderson, shall right this historical oversight by carefully surveying the surrounding lands, by putting points of greatest interest on the map and, finally, by finding artifacts that shall become prized pieces in museums throughout the world!
- Day Four of the Grand Expedition to Tors of Levenies
Tors of Levenies are almost in reach: I've already made my way around the foothills, and I came dangerously close to getting lost in the plain a few times. I've located a promising tomb, but something stirred inside of it, and I decided against disturbing it further!
- Day Seven of the Grand Expedition to Tors of Levenies
I've scoured the vicinity. My legs are sore from all the walking, and I am low on coin. If I don't find something in the next two days, I'll be reduced to cleaning the floors of the Varnhold tavern.
- Day Ten of the Grand Expedition to Tors of Levenies
It seems Desna has heard my prayers! As I was returning from my latest outing, the evening outpaced me, and I was forced to spend the night in the hills. As I slept, I suddenly heard a voice... a majestic, proud voice that could have only been the voice of the divine! It commanded me to stand up and follow its call. I wandered as if in a dream, following where it led.
But the night grew darker with each step. Utterly blind, I suddenly realized soil had given way to slabs of stone under my feet... searching about me, my hands fell on a shattered amphora filled with gold and jewels... words fail me, but as my hands touched the amphora, I felt as if I had disturbed something. Consumed by fear, all I could manage was to grab a bracelet lying on top of the precious heap, and flee back into the moonless night.
The sun is already rising as I am writing these words. I don't know how, but I found my way back to the plain. It must have been Desna herself that led me through the darkness and despair!
Oh great goddess! I beseech thee, show me the way back to civilization! Otherwise all I shall ever contribute to history will be my corpse, picked clean by ravens, and this wretched diary.
- Day Twelve of the Grand Expedition to Tors of Levenies
I can see Varnhold! Praise be to Desna! I feel her gaze and her blessing upon me!
At last I will be able to show my find to Maegar — he knows his treasures, and values those who find it! The bracelet I retrieved seems to be carved from a single piece of jade — even if it wasn't a relic, it would still be worth a fortune!
- Day Fourteen of the Grand Expedition to Tors of Levenies

I am beset by terrifying dreams. In them, I claw out my eyes and am buried alive. I wake up covered in cold sweat, then fall into sleep again — only to see the same thing.
Is Desna testing me? What must I do, great goddess? Send me a sign!

"Exhausted, Ugumash fell upon the tangled sheets with the tired grunt. Sweat poured down his forehead and blinded his eyes, already swollen with fatigue and strain. Or was it his tears? He would prefer the sweat — the spicy perspiration of a warrior and a male. Or, better yet, blood — the blood of his enemies, red and hot, shed in the midst of ferocious fight. But reality stood against his wishes, trying to convince him of what he couldn't accept: that he was lying on the silky sheets, languishing of lust like some beardless youngster. All he could do was jump off the bed without delay and flee this nymph who had bewitched him with magic known only to the most lascivious of women.
Ugumash's empty stomach lurched with hunger. Yes, that was what he needed! He would happily swallow a big piece of meat in the tavern downstairs. The half-orc sat on the edge of the bed and contemptuously spat sticky saliva on the already soiled plank floor, then glanced at his prey.
Elieira! That damned witch! The long-legged, curvaceous elf was completely nude, hair caught by a bone dragon. She lay on the bed, her finger drawing intricate patterns along her insatiable body. These beckoning gestures clouded Ugumash's mind. He was unable to think any more, and he could not decide which part of his body craved more immediately for satisfaction.
'I'd heard a thing or two about half-orcs,' Elieira said, adding oil to the flames. 'But from what I can tell, even best of them can't match mighty Irovetti. It seems as though, after His Majesty, there will be no more miracles in my bed. I suppose I'm destined to content myself with mere shadows from now on. But worry not, my warrior…'
Ugumash had little time to ponder over Elieira's words, as the normal rumbling sounds of the ground floor of the tavern ceased, as though severed with an axe. It was instinct that compelled Ugumash to reach for the curved sword hidden beneath the clothes on the floor, and a moment later, the door to the room flew open and an ominous shadow appeared on the threshold.
Ugumash grabbed his weapon and straightened himself, looking the stranger up and down. Shadows do not scare half-orcs — it is their appearance that makes others tremble. The stranger, clad in dusty rags, stepped forward to meet him. His eyes flashed with fierce rage from under the hood, but the sword in his hands shone even more dazzling. The half-orc immediately recognized Albaldir's Retribution — how could he not? But how did it end up in the hands of some tramp?! Comprehending the situation seemed an impossible task for the half-orc, but answers were not what he was after anyway — with a roar, he raised his weapon and rushed toward the intruder ... "

"Great Detective Izamir Grimblock: The Case of Six Invisibles"

"Great Kings and Queens of the Past: Jason Scott"
King Jason Scott was undoubtedly enthralled with the mystery surrounding the disappearance of Aroden, the Living God. He organized several expeditions, searching for any clues that might shed some light on the mystery, and he's said to give inspiration to the Archknights of Avistan themselves.

"Great Kings and Queens of the Past: Joel McGillivray-Bove"
It is rumored that King Joel was a pirate and an adventurer in his youth. Joel raised his own kingdom from nothing, and he was well-loved by his people. He often joked about getting back to sailing the open seas, and his advisors constantly worried that it wasn't a joke.

"Great Kings and Queens of the Past: John Spiropulos"
King John is remembered and respected across Golarion as a noble peacemaker. Rumors say he was one of the patrons of the Suramgamin and a close friend to their founder, Avalo himself.

"Great Kings and Queens of the Past: Magnus Borge"
King Magnus was a prominent ruler and a famous collector of folklore. He gathered, studied, and published many books of fairy tales and ballads of various creatures that lived in the Stolen lands. His "Goblin Poetry Collection" soon became an international best seller.

"Great Kings and Queens of the Past: Warren Blake"
King Warren inspired numerous artists to paint portraits of His Highness. Thanks to these portraits, his special "royal" mustache style became extremely popular in countries across Golarion.
"Great ancestor eat our souls..."

"Guy met many friends on his travels, and some even had the right metal to join his quest to find Aroden. Deo was another founding member of the Archknights. A barbarian of great renown hailing from the Storval Plateau, Deo made a name for himself among the northern nomads of Varisia. He cut his teeth in battle against Shoanti tribesmen and the Orcs of the Hold of Belkzen as a young man. He grew to over seven feet tall as he reached his maturity and swung a specially made axe that was said to be wider than most men, and too heavy for most to lift let alone swing.
Clar, a fleet-of-foot Halfling, was the band's infiltrator, sneak, and purveyor of necessary goods when the situation called for it. He wasn't the nicest member of the knights, having grown up on the mean streets of Westcrown. Orphaned by a Pathfinder father who was never around and when his mother grew ill and died, he was born in the shadow and learned to use it as a cloak. Recognizable by a milky eye, this Halfling may have been small but his loyalty to the Archknights loomed as large as his best friend Deo.
Another member that exuded class was the group's battle caster, Vivreal. A fugitive on the run from the Maurya-Rahm in Jalmeray, this exotic beauty found a family among the Knights that was infectious and inclusive. She added a touch of grace to balance out the Knights' wilder members. Said to summon arcane energy weapons in battle and to cast spells between swings, she wasn't one to sit back and let the men do the heavy lifting. She broke many hearts, but never stole any. Some thought she left a lover behind on that southern Isle and held out hope of seeing them again one day.
A non-traditional Knight by any standard, Beloq-Nur was a bowman with few peers. Tortured as a captive of a sadistic orc war band on the outskirts between Belkin and Lastwall, this man was covered in burn scars head to toe. He didn't like what he saw in the eyes of onlookers, so he most often kept to himself. But the party always knew he was around in a pinch because their enemies began to sprout arrows at an alarming rate.
The chronicler of this tale also happens to be an Archknight of Avistan from the cosmopolitan streets of Absalom. I am Ashwyn Blackstrand, greatest Magi of the age, or so I hope to be for Serenrea's sake. My friends call me Ash, and my enemies will tell you I do not exist. Some will say the Archknights are myth, but do not be deceived. We are out there, searching for Aroden still. As Guy would say, we seek the god that gave a damn. Look for us on the path to knowledge and glory. We will be there, carrying light into the darkness..."

"Have you ever dreamed of becoming a baron? It's not that hard. All you have to do is go to the Stolen Lands – a tiny region located between Brevoy and the River Kingdoms, and a source of dispute for those two for many years. Miles and miles of woods, swamps and infertile clay soils infested with monsters and bandits. It's something like a white elephant: one can't hold it but also can't give up on it and let the neighbor have it. For many years, the Restov Swordlords have been promising a title to anyone who manages to bring some resemblance of order to this gods-forsaken land. This is just the usual way rulers solve their problems: there are plenty of adventure-seekers, and you can always find another naïve brave soul who'd gladly risk his or her life without prepayment. There were many who took the bait — their sun-bleached bones still litter the banks of muddy lakes and lie in piles under crooked trees.
You can imagine how astonished I was, then, when someone managed the feat — breaking the antlers of a local kingpin called the Stag Lord and turning the bandit's fort into the capital of a new barony. Of course, I departed for these lands immediately, to witness with my own eyes the one who managed to install control over the Stolen Lands.
Let's be honest: the achievements of the new baron{mf||ess} are still quite moderate. My letter didn't get there in time (I hope the courier who had to deliver it is alive and well). Since no one could meet me, I decided to get to the capital on my own, which was a strategic mistake, for the road-building in the barony functions even worse than its mailing service. I barely made my way through the mud and wind-fallen trees, just to narrowly escape drowning at the river ford — the only thing that kept me going was the anticipation of the joy the baron{mf||ess} would express when I told {mf|him|her} about the marvelous scientific novelty called a "bridge". Furthermore, a horde of hungry kobolds jumped out from the underbrush. But just when I was getting ready to kiss my life goodbye, the baron{mf||ess} {mf|him|her}self emerged from the woods, fought off all the pests, and helped me to get to firm ground.
As it turned out, the baron{mf||ess} has a strong justification for neglecting roads and bridges: while {mf|his|her} capital is under construction, {mf||s}he lives on the road and with the help of {mf|his|her} companions patrols the realm, dealing significant damage to the local, ever-hungry fauna (may the plague take it). Trolls, boggards, will-o'-wisps and giant spiders really impede the improvement of public services.
I've offered the baron{mf||ess} my advice and my active help – you can spit in the faces of those who claim Jubilost can only criticize. You can try out your luck as well: though the title of the ruler is already taken, the young barony offers plenty of vacancies both for laborers and for sellswords. Just don't repeat the mistakes of your predecessors: demand payment in advance! As for those of you who prefer to learn about wild lands and dangerous adventures from the magazine pages, we'll meet in the next issue."
"Have you ever met the Lantern King? They say he's so... Amazing!"
"Have you executed my order?"
"Have you found a cure?"

"Having you here is a great honor for us!"

"He and his senses have definitely parted ways." {n}Jubilost nods, then glances at Amiri.{/n} "And we have too many halfwits in our little band already. I'm afraid our Madcap Inn has no room for another."
"He avenges the simple folk. They say he's the best bowman in the world."

"He calls to her again — his Queen. He drinks, he calls to her, he drinks again. I have no idea who she is. I can't even tell if she exists outside his own drunken vision. But I know he'll call to her, and then he'll crash around angrily, yelling that she didn't come. Then he'll come for me.
I obey the rules. I do as he says. I keep silent until he allows me to speak. But he still beats me every time he drinks and rages.
He said he'll burn my hands in acid next time. Will I still be able to write? I..."
"He can wait for as long as he likes. He's not getting my crown."
"He could work off my debts!"
"He couldn't have lied to us! He was honest, I could see it in his eyes. I know people good, I do!"

"He did not anticipate victory, but hoped at least for an honorable death. Alas, the darkness reached out to him from the abominable Spawn of the Beast, and refused him even that. An aura of madness filled the gnome with delusions of grandeur, and transported his mind into the marvelous fey world, where he sits, a godlike ruler."
"He doesn't look good. Perhaps, we should... great gods, he's bleeding from his mouth!"

"He has become a frightening, dangerous, and pathetic caricature of his former self. – A king without a kingdom, the god of a rotten soul. Immersed in sweet dreams, he wanders the halls, barking orders at the wandering monsters... A sad sight to behold. His death will bring him not only peace, but also restore the dignity he's lost."

"He invited representatives from all the trade houses to play cards. No one really knows exactly what happened, but by morning, he owned most of their assets, including the crown. They suspected a rigged game and sent representatives from the families to discuss the matter with him — and then a wave of disappearances rolled across the city. My brothers, the former kings of {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, disappeared, along with many other honorable people — and Irovetti made it clear that the lives of his hostages would depend upon our obedience. He was king, and our wealth and power lay in ruins."

"He may be cruel, but he's devious. I think he wanted to test my loyalty and eliminate rivals at the same time, so he recruited me as a spy. It seemed natural, what with my husband in the guards. I couldn't just refuse — that would make me look like a threat to the state. The king is already putting the squeeze on the city guard hard enough, so that would threaten my Talwyn too. Now I've concocted a story to get you to attack someone on the pretense of piracy, knowing that it wasn't true." {n}Eimar withers with shame.{/n}
"He never finished that bridge"
"He only killed villains"

"Hell yeah! We're going to have some fun! It's way too soon to retire!"

"Her father didn't live much longer than our mother, so I decided to try to help Irenna. I brought her here, to {g|Stolen Lands}the Stolen Lands{/g}, though Oleg was against it. And once here, she immediately fell under the Stag Lord's influence. She never even needed to meet him — the stories and rumors from local hunters and bandits were enough to win her over. She would tell us how he was a real leader, unlike {g|Restov}Restov's{/g} 'softies.' Eventually, she ran away, only to return under a new name with a pack of thugs to 'collect taxes' from us. What's worse, she participated in the torture and execution of prisoners alongside the Stag Lord's minions."
"Her name is Tioko Sakasama. She led a party of adventurers here, noblest heroes and truest friends. Together they'd defeated many foes... But they'd never faced anything like this."
"Her name is the Dawnflower, for her boundless patience is like the warm light of the sun."
