"Hey, hold on, everyone," {n}the bandit leader says as he sheathes the sword he'd drawn just a moment ago.{/n} "And Shortie, stop your foaming. Look here, this is our glorious {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} {mf|himself|herself}! Come now, bow down, everyone, bow down!"
"Hey, how long are we supposed to be waiting here?"
"Hey, kid, you have quick hands — no problem at all catching that coin. Happen to know anything about locks? Wanna join us?"
"Hey, look! If it isn't the {mf|king|queen} {mf|him|her}self! Let's go!"
"Hey, no idling! To work now!"

"Hey, servants! Those were wise words. Someone write that down!"
"Hey, settle down, now. I'm not taking anyone anywhere."
"Hey, shatstank drench-breeches! Come out, fight — you, me!"

"Hey, sis!
We're rich. We've gotten lucky after all. If we play our cards right, we'll finally be able to quit running around the woods, we'll piss on the damned boss and his gang, go to Brevoy and live as happy as pigs in shit. The point is: you must take care, you know very well what these fellas do to those who try to con them. And we are going to con them hard, sunshine!
See, while you were away, we caught this dwarf. All dressed up like a dog's dinner, fancy mail armor, tall tales – one could immediately see he was the city mouse. He kept on treating us like dirt until we'd set his beard on fire – after that he started spilling his guts in no time.
Long story short, his ancestors – Fortash-or-something – the ones who built the ancient tower – had hidden some real treasure inside. And, you see, he decided to return there after several centuries to claim his family fortune, all alone, with no guards — it made me laugh my ass off. He had no idea about the exact place where that treasure was hidden, but he brought the key to open the place – a white metal thingy, something like a cog. When the fellas heard about the treasure, they literally started rubbing their hands together, and I thought to myself: well, what happens when we find it? The boss seizes the lion's share, and we are left with meager peanuts!
All these things considered, I snatched the key away while the rest of the gang was sleeping, and made it look like the dwarf had run away with it. The fellows have been running across the woods since then, searching for the midget but they'll have to search really hard, I buried him rather deep. They stay away from the tower for now – what might they do there without a key? So, make use of it. When you return, do not go to the camp – go to our place instead, I've hidden the cog in the hollow of the tree trunk. You know which one I mean. Take it – and get to the tower, look around and find what you can open with it. You're smart, you'll manage. Take away all these dwarves have hidden, and… well, I don't have to tell you what to do next.
Be careful, don't blow up our best chance!
Hugs,
Bergen"
"Hey, take it easy on him!"
"Hey, those are Technic League goods! Stop right there!"
"Hey, wait. Where do you think you're going? We saved you, didn't we? So we deserve a reward. Get out your coin purse!"
"Hey, wake up! Enemies!"
"Hey, what are you doing? Think I can't do it alone?"

"Hey, what're ya sayin'?" {n}Shortie shakes his head in confusion.{/n} "If that's the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}, the only job {mf|he'll|she'll} have for us is as noose tighteners! I say we cut {mf|him|her} down and call it a day!"
"Hey, why he be roaring?"
"Hey, why it be? How it be?! All, hear my orders! Strate-tactical wardrobal!"
"Hey, why you be pushing me?"
"Hey, why you pour me less?! Pour more, or I make you headhurt!"
"Hey, you there! What's going on here?"
"Hey, you there!"
"Hey, you vagrant! Get lost!"
"Hey, you! We're running short of provisions!"
"Hey... hic, over there... Demons, hic! From the First World! Attack, hic!"

"Heya, Dogbee!
So, finally decided to suckle from our Pitaxian teat, huh? Good for you! Maybe you're not the half-wit you seem. Read this carefully, and do as you're told to — if anything goes wrong, I'll know… and I'll certainly give you something to cry about.
Pillaging {name}'s lands won't be enough. You have to leave scorched earth behind you. Whatever you can't take, you burn or break. Set fire to homes, stables, barns, sheepfolds... anything with food or livestock. Ruin their smiths, weavers, potters — anyone capable enough to use tools. Maybe even salt the earth while you're at it!
Your reward is whatever you can snatch. Keep an eye on your men — don't let them be greedy pigs. And don't overstuff your carts, or they'll get stuck in the mud. I figure Pitaxian gawks like you won't know where to fence their loot, so I made a deal with the local tallymen — they'll take the goods straight from the camp. You can find us using the map I left you.
A few days ago, a poisoner from Galt arrived. She looks like a normal halfling, like you could smash her with a thumb, but her eyes are like two unearthed graves. I bet she's murdered more living souls than the both of us combined. I've heard a thing or two about her kind, worshipers of Blackfingers — Norgorber's avatar that oversees making poisons. Rumor has it they're all half-crazed thugs. She'll provide you poison for the wells, though no one's stopping you from coating your blade in the stuff, as well — just watch you don't get any on you.
Do as you're told, and wait for new orders. Trust only our inner circle, don't expose your throat, and sleep with one eye open.
I.N."
"Hic... Think we're out of booze."
"Hic... You see, you got your half-orcs. And then you got half-elves. But what I wanna know is, where are the half-halflings?"
"Hide it! Queen Bdaah never find!"
"Hip-hip!"
"Hip-hip, hooray!"

"His Highness Irovetti is ready to lend you a helping hand. Reject this unbearable burden of power, kneel to him and abdicate the crown. He will rule the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} as wisely and fairly as he rules his own country. His Highness is expecting you at his palace in {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, ready to accept your oath."
"His Highness is expecting you."
"His opera should show that each of us is the architect of our own fate. Hard work and perseverance lead to success and prosperity."
"His prices are outrageous!"

"His reign be just, and strong his hand -
King Irovetti should rule this land!"

"His rivals set a trap for him during a competition. He died, giving his life to protect the other participants, but his glory lived on even after his death. Few mortals are deemed worthy of joining the godly host, and Kurgess was among them!"
"His work should tackle the all-important question of faith and piety."
"Hit 'em hard! Pile on!"
"Hit 'em hard!"
"Hit and eat!"
"Hit him! Harder!"
"Hit him!"
"Hit {mf|him|her}!"
"Hm-m-m… In that case I… I'll give you my spear! I can make a lot of handy things out of wood. You would call me a woodworker in your tongue." {n}The elf gives you a disarming smile.{/n}
"Hm... Don't you think we made a bad bargain? It's only gold! Don't we already have enough of that? All right, well... I guess some things I just don't understand."

"Hm... I see. I can't say I approve. The bandits will pay handsomely for the right to sell their goods in your harbors – of that I'm quite sure. But soon enough, those who they plundered will come seeking revenge. They'll find your harbor crawling with robbers – any may simply burn the lot to the ground, along with the river pirates too."
"Hm... It's a questionable decision. The gift could be a trap, just as Razmir's Tears were in fact a poison. Magical gifts are often treacherous."

"Hm... This decision will surely please the people, but is it really wise? Sooner or later, the minor kingdoms will fall, and their lands will be taken by Razmir. It would be wiser to support the stronger state, and reap a share of the spoils."

"Hm... To be honest, this is not the best decision. You've let a wolf into your house to get rid of the rats. The Gardeners are fanatics, true, but Goss is a manipulative weasel. He's the more dangerous of the two."
"Hm... Will we pay compensation to all who ever were or will be robbed? Or only the people we like? Only wealthy and influential foreigners perhaps? This doesn't smack of justice at all."
"Hm?"
"Hmm, it's true the capital would end up a bloody mess without the rules."
"Hmm, maybe there's something wrong with your eye that's making it difficult for you to think. Perhaps if we just took that out..."
"Hmm, you just gave me an idea. Maybe I should be called a Smart Guy, not an Honest Guy?"
"Hmm. As you wish, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
"Hmm. Would you please wait..."
"Hmm... Octavia once loved toys like that. Not anymore, though."

"Hmm... This is unwise. You don't have any landed nobles here, as we do in Brevoy. Trade is your kingdom's only tangible source of income. A ban on free trade would have strengthened the powerful class here."
"Hmm... Yes, that's right."
"Hmm... the brew is... all right. Just the bottles are... t-too small..."
"Hmm?"
"Hmmmm?"
"Hmmm… curious examples of pre-historic culture."
"Hold a moment… I didn't have a chance to reward you for your help. Fortunes are best shared, after all. Safe travels."
"Hold it at once!"
"Hold on — let me get you on the books, then you can get your volunteer badges."
"Hold on, we'll help you!"
"Hold on. What's that you have, there? Show me."
"Hold on... This one's a goner anyway — he doesn't just owe money to the boss, he's been borrowing all around town."
"Hold the line! Drive them back!"
"Hold tight if you don't want to get washed away!"
"Hold your tongue, Kressle."
"Hold, Regongar! Your owners are here!"
"Hold, {name}! I'm with you!"
"Holy gods!"
"Home. Breakthrough. Passage."
"Honor and law."
"Hooray! We won!"
"Hope will prevail."
"Horrible day, what a horrible day! {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g}, save my soul."
"Hostess is quite moody today. Folks say she is always that way".
"Hours."
"House Lebeda insulted me gravely. If they want their heir back, they'll have to pay a ransom."
"How about another go right now?"
"How about this? You head toward the road, and I follow. You falter, I'll kick you so hard you make it the rest of the way airborne."
"How am I supposed to work without a forge? Build me a forge – then we'll talk!"
"How are you finding Varnhold?"
"How can I be of assistance?"
"How can I find Tartuk?"
"How can I help you?"
"How can I help?"
"How can anyone have trouble with such a simple thing as getting from one flying island to another?"
"How can this man be a king if he can't even master his own darker impulses?"
"How can you be so merciless? Have you no heart?"
"How can you help my army?"
"How could I get infected?"

"How could I remember you? I'd never met you at the time. That was Kanerah. She was the one who talked to you at the reception, and helped you fight off the assassins. We usually write each other notes, recounting in detail all that happened, and describing any friends that 'Kaessi' had made. But that time we switched right in the middle of a mansion engulfed in fire and filled with assassins. Kanerah didn't have the time to write any notes."
"How could you say such a thing, sir? I'm no charlatan — I even have a license!"
"How could you say that, Your Grace! I couldn't bring myself to harm even an animal! I've chosen this troll because they're a plague, and their numbers need to be thinned."
"How dare she…"
"How dare you?!"
"How dare..."
"How did I let myself get into this..."
"How did the hunt go? To your benefit, I hope?"
"How did you become a justiciar of Abadar?"
"How did you come into possession of gold that had been touched by a demon?"
"How did you get here?"
"How did you meet Linzi?"
"How do I find that balance, teacher?"
"How do you know it's bull? It's not just some bard from a tavern, it's {mf|His|Her} {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}'s own bard! Why would our {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} lie to us?"
"How do you like the Lantern King's joke? Exciting, isn't it?"
"How does all that fit into one gnome?!"
"How long ya going to strut around here?"
"How may I be of assistance?"
"How may I help?"
"How much?! Just where did that price come from?"
"How sad it is to see you whipping your own subjects to rebellion. They will only rise more steadfast against your authority, and soon we'll be sending our military forces to collect your taxes."

"How sad. Everyone is always trying to demolish something, expel someone, banish each other to dark oblivion. The world is full of fragile things, you know. Today you're banishing a harmless coven... And no one will remember it tomorrow. Ripped from their home, they will surely perish. Will we mark their passing, or even care? Do you not see now why our whole world deserves its fate?"
"How terrible! I hope it's not contagious!"
"How to Save Pitax?"
"How unfortunate! Better luck next time."

"How unfortunate." {n}After a short silence, the old man continues in a melancholic tone:{/n} "Well, since this can no longer be considered independent art, I shall pass on another of the young maestro's requests: he wishes to know what themes you would like to see addressed. Do you have a specific lesson you'd like to share with the audience?"
"How would we know anything about Lamashtu?"
"How you know where kobold ambush? Ask: kobold, you ambusssh, yesss?"
"How's your research going?"
"How... how can both of us be here? Is this a dream?"
"How... how should I live now? Where shall I go? Perhaps... home."

"However, I could give you something much more impressive." {n}The old man gives you a wink and a bloodthirsty grin.{/n} "A weapon worthy of {g|Gorum}Gorum's{/g} herald! It's a family relic. Come to my forge, and I'll tell you more."
"However, if you still wish to join us once you come of age, the order could always use such a fine young man."

"However, that is not important now. We can contemplate the wonders of the magical arts once we are out of danger. For now the important thing is that I know how to clear the passage. I only hope I am skilled enough to keep the entire building from collapsing on our heads! Tell me when you are ready, and I will try to move the flower's roots and open that wall."
"How… how beautiful!" {n}The elf reverently accepts the flower.{/n}
"Huh, these were some mighty words! Here's the bard's art for you! Even though you understand she's bullshiting you, the way she does it makes you want to believe!"
"Huh, your noble skin is soft and gentle... You'll make a fine pair of pants."
"Huh? Do I know you?"
"Hundreds of years of lies... You'll pay!"
"Hunt new monsters? Ha! Was born ready!"
"Hunting's sparse around here. We're running low on meat again..."
"Hurrah for {mf|His|Her} {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!"
"Hurray for {mf|His|Her} {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!"
"Hurrraaah!"
"Hurrrayyyy!"
"Hurry up! Get out of the city, it's safe outside!"
"Hurry, girls! Let's hide and wait for the {mf|King|Queen} — {mf|he|she}'ll drive away this pestilence!"
"Hurry, squires! Our little vacation's over. The demons of the Worldwound await!"
"Hurry, {mf|My Baron|My Baroness} , I beg you!"
"Hurry-hurry!"
"Hush, focus! I will cast a spell, and find us something to rob or desecrate!"
"Hydra be so big!"
"Hydra be so strong!"
"Hydra love food!"
"Hydra no eat you?"
"I accept your apology. Please accept this gift as well."
"I accept."
"I accidentally dropped jam on my draft! That jam was really tasty, though."
"I admit, the food is not capital fare. But for a picnic, it will serve..."

"I admit, when you offered me the treasurer's position, this was not how I imagined this job. I knew that it's ungrateful work, that I would have to endure the hatred of the crowd who clutch their purses tightly... But I didn't expect that I'd be stonewalled at every step of the way by my own {mf|baron|baroness|King|Queen}! Are you trying to ruin your country? Well, it's your right, but don't expect me to help you. This is the end. I resign!"
"I agree."
"I already told you, you won't get one coin from me! Now get out of my sight!"
"I always go duck hunting when I'm drunk. With five bows in my hands and the sky full of ducks, there's no chance I'd miss."

"I am an Honest Guy!" {n}The lad strikes his chest proudly with his fist.{/n} "I stand here honestly, welcoming heroes, and seeing them off to their feats of glory. I honestly collect the gear from their breathless corpses. And I honestly sell it to the next heroes."
"I am completely alone in the dominion of a mighty and unpredictable creature. A refusal might cost me my life."
"I am glad to know this nightmare will no longer wander the Tenebrous Depths. She was so reckless and evil, and looked and sounded so innocent, the better to draw her prey into her nets."

"I am guarding the Spawn of {g|Rovagug}Rovagug{/g}, that sleeps in the caves beneath us. I summon heroes to help me defeat it. It is a long and joyless vigil, but I believe that it will one day be over. Perhaps you yourself are the hero who will finally achieve this long-awaited victory?"
"I am her guardian. I am her slave. I am her master!"
"I am hero. Great Hero."
"I am innocent, and I refute your accusations."

"I am master of the school of Conjuration, so sloth has always been my favorite sin... But that was not what ruined me. The seed of my destruction was the same sin it is for most wizards: pride. I summoned a force I could not control, and I discovered my powerlessness too late!"
"I am not keeping up with my responsibilities?! Don't be absurd! You know full well that the disasters that fell upon my lands were the work of Irovetti himself!"
"I am not yet sure what exactly all this greenery does, but one thing is certain – it did not come from our world."
"I am not! It's a very common name! Every third person in {g|Restov}Restov{/g} is a Bragic!"
"I am preparing for the war and gathering my allies in the capital. Can you get yourself there?"
"I am ready for battle. Lead on!"
"I am sorry for what happened here. This massacre was a grievous mistake."
"I am sorry, Verdrin. I have to think of others as well."
"I am still waiting, human. I need a healing artifact from the stash."
"I am the law, the judge, and the executioner."
"I am, Fredero. Let your second start the countdown."
"I and Briar in my hand command you: kill {mf|him|her}!"
"I and my people came to help you, but the damned portal and even more damned fog had us separated from each other."
"I appreciate your intentions, but that 'healing' of yours only harms me."
"I ask a great sacrifice. No one will dare judge you, if you turn around and leave."
"I be scared."
"I be too handsome to die like that!"
"I beg you to have mercy on me! You can't leave me to this horrible fate! Please, help me down!"
"I beg you to leave. Let us mourn our fallen brethren."
"I beg you, {mf|baron|baroness}!"
"I believe I have an idea for the next chapter..."
"I believe in my heart we will overcome this trial, whatever it takes!"
"I believe we should set up a camp for the night."

"I believe with all my heart that justice and prosperity are rooted in the law. I swear before you this day, that I shall rule in accordance with the traditions and laws that serve what is good and right!"
"I believe you. You may continue your experiments."
"I believed in you so much, Stag Lord. And now... now you're just a dead sack of bones."
"I bet I'll kill at least a dozen!"
"I bet they want to take away our loot! They're messing with the wrong men!"
"I bow to no one!"
"I came, just as I promised. I will stand shoulder to shoulder with you against the monster."
"I can hardly believe our fortress stood somewhere nearby."
"I can see you're an experienced trader. Would you consider operating exclusively in my barony?"

"I can sell you various divine spell scrolls. They're quite useful, even if you don't have anyone in your party who can read them! While you're in this settlement — or, indeed, any place with a cleric willing to help — you need only open your bag and choose the scroll you wish to cast. I'll be happy to read it for you. However, take care out there in the wilderness: a scroll is useless without someone who can read it! To use a scroll on your journeys, you'll need a spellcaster whose magical training covers such spells, or someone skilled in magical devices."
"I can stay awake infinitely. You can't. Get some rest before Oleg changes his mind."
"I can still see the face of the guide we hired to take us there!"
"I can tell you're angry, but I'll say it anyway — they're doing the right thing."
"I can understand a broken bed and a crushed candelabra. But what, Desna save me, have you done to the window shutters?!"
"I can't agree to anything before I know what exactly it is you need…"

"I can't agree with this decision. Our weakened position may be too tempting for our less noble neighbors. I'll try to use the remains of your army to organize our defenses, but this may cost us dearly."
"I can't approve of such a decision, but the word of {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness} is the law."
"I can't believe it! That could have been us!"
"I can't believe it! You just slaughtered all of them! I'm never asking you for anything, ever again!"
"I can't believe it! You..."
"I can't believe it! {mf|He|She} just popped the last lock — only one in a million could do such a thing!"
"I can't believe it... I can feel it again – the First World! Our home!"

"I can't believe my ears! You want to insult people who endure curses and spitting every day, at risk to their health and even their lives, that your treasury may remain full? And for who? Ungrateful parasites who despise you and your power, who enjoy your patronage but try to evade their own responsibilities? This is madness. You're digging a hole under your own throne with your very hands!"
"I can't believe those dirty blasphemers pretended to be our brothers!"

"I can't believe we're wasting precious time because you..." {n}Jubilost trails off, then coughs.{/n} "Actually, I know of a place where a fountain of ale flows freely from the stone. I can show you — for a modest fee. Paid in advance, of course."
"I can't fix this. But I can keep others from such a loss."
"I can't move! I carry this much!"
"I can't stay in this city any longer... too many memories..."
"I can't think of anything but tentacles…"
"I can't wait for the banquet!"
"I can't wait to get back to work, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}! I'm so excited to see my new workshop..."
"I can't wait to get to that Eldest and say, 'Guess who's back!'"
"I can't wait to retire and recollect these moments as I sit by the fire, with a cup of mulled wine in my hand!"
"I can't wait to see the ceremony! I've never attended a coronation before."
"I can't wait to talk to my father! I already know what I'm going to tell him... and it'll be a short talk!"
"I can't, I just can't, Your Grace. It would reduce me to poverty!"
"I can't, either..."
"I can't..."
"I cannot believe this..."
"I cannot die like this! I cannot!"
"I cannot lose!"
"I cannot refuse. What is more important than knowledge? Especially the kind that the First World can provide?"

"I caught sight of a certain {g|Cheliax}Chelish{/g} noble, who for a long time been number one on my "kill-on-sight" list. So I challenged him to a duel, and he was too stupid to refuse. I dispatched him, only then to learn that he was a distant relative of Cheliax's crown prince, and besides that, the lord of the surrounding lands. And of course, no one in the area was at all fond of him."
"I changed my mind. Just think of something yourself."
"I come not to kill you. A trial awaits you, trespasser. I shall simply make sure you get there... without getting lost along the way."
"I command you to put the bow down, Ekun." [To trolls] "You better run! If I ever find out that you're attacking people, I will come back and find you."
"I could use the help of a cleric."
"I couldn't sleep last night — I kept thinking about Irovetti. I hope that villain doesn't send assassin's after us!"

"I deeply regret that our people were unable to verify this information. But I would not recommend leaving it unattended. In {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} we know very well how quickly rebel seeds may sprout."
"I did promise, didn't I? Well, I always keep my promises."
"I didn't know you could be so... so wild!"
"I do it for the greater good."
"I do not like that Gunderson. Even if he is not a spy — and mind you, I still have my doubts! — vagabonds like him always bring trouble."
"I don't care about battle scars... But I cherish each scar I get from my nights with you."
"I don't care about the Skjegge and their arguments. But I'm glad you got something out of this."
"I don't care about the nature of your… experiments, so long as no harm comes to my subjects."
"I don't care who you are! You're finished!"
"I don't deserve your help… But as Sarenrae is my witness, I am eternally grateful to you!"
"I don't feel well... No, please... Don't..."
"I don't give a shit about Desna's grace. This is Gorum's district, get me?"
"I don't give an ascetic damn. All vagrants are to be removed from city streets."
"I don't got a plague! I'm just a normal highwayman!"
"I don't have any permits. I'm an herbalist, not an apothecary."
"I don't have enough money right now."
"I don't have it! The taxes cut deep into it, and..."
"I don't have to explain anything to you."
"I don't know if I can save you from death, my friends... but at least we will die at home."
"I don't know much about trade, but I do know that the one who controls the food controls the pack. You've just made a grave mistake, {name}."
"I don't know! I don't know anything!"
"I don't know! Wait... what's that noise?!"
"I don't know. It seems like forever... But finally, my guard will be over."
"I don't know. No way I'm putting that rot in my body."

"I don't know. You saw everything I did! It doesn't seem like we closed it. I thought I heard someone's voice... Maybe it was closed by the same person who opened it... Is that the same person who created this insane fortress?"

"I don't like hiding fugitives from justice, until it's proven that their trial was corrupt. And I'm more troubled by the thought that your decision was guided not by your desire to see justice done, but to befriend the elves."
"I don't like the name 'Stolen Lands'... What if they really are stolen and the rightful owner is coming back?"
"I don't like this silence. Something is surely about to happen."
"I don't like this whole 'tribe' idea. I only helped you, you owe me nothing."
"I don't like those golems around here. You never know what it's... well, thinking."
"I don't like what I'm hearing."
"I don't need your service. I only wanted to know..."
"I don't require your services any longer. You may leave now."
"I don't think your master, {name}, sees anything of the sort. Are you not put aside, laughed at, ridiculed... treated as your tribe treated you?"
"I don't understand why you spared her. You should have let her burn with the house!"
"I don't usually drink... But today's an exception!"
"I don't want to die! Mercy!"
"I don't want to end up one of those undead when I die."
"I don't want to go anywhere. Maybe we can stay here... for a week or two?"
"I don't want to go anywhere..."
"I don't want to hear anything, or see you in my lands again."
"I don't want to let you go."
"I doubt I can tell you anything of interest," {n}Bartholomew mutters without looking you in the eye.{/n}

"I expect he was already insane before he even came here. Nothing else could explain his indifference towards suffering. But he was strong and confident, and managed to get quite close to the spawn – very close – before he met his end."

"I failed to resist temptation, and quickly doused my weary feet in the holy waters of the oasis. I washed my feet off first, for it would never do to desecrate a divine font with the dust of the road.
The sunset danced upon the surface of the water. I closed my eyes as my flesh went numb, in yearning anticipation of a miracle. On the road, pain had gnawed at my heart, but now it melted into the holy water, and my sores seemed to fade away.
I looked into my heart, and questioned the purity of my thought. Was I worthy enough to escape my torment? Would Sarenrae give me a sign? I was prepared to greet the sound of flapping dove wings.
The fever overwhelmed me. I sensed the divine rays, but the sun had set. The light was coming through my eyelids! I witnessed the figures of Sarenrae and her angels. I dared open my eyes, but they were heavy, as if burdened with all the weight of the sun's heat. Sleep dawned upon me."

"I fear it's time I bring my service to an end. There is simply no way for me to continue my work as your Treasurer. Our views on the future of the country are far too divergent. I cannot stand silently by and observe what it's to become."

"I fear that the danger has not yet passed. We have postponed the awakening of the monster for centuries, perhaps thousands of years... But I feel its life pulsating in the desecrated depths. The egg still lives. The larva of another nightmare will someday be born."
"I fear this matter may be more complicated than you expect. Oleg, please explain your situation."
"I feel almost sure that I've just witnessed some sort of a divine intervention..."
"I feel dizzy..."
"I feel for the poor sods living there. It's like sitting on top of a powder keg."
"I feel good when I'm with you. Let's come back here more often."
"I feel the blood of my men on you. Die!"
"I filed all the necessary paperwork, waited for a couple days, and then decided to check on things in person."
"I follow my orders as best I can."
"I fought when alive; I fight while dead. All in the name of our great lord."
"I found it!"
"I found out what I wanted, thank you."
"I found something in the dungeon that makes me doubt your sincerity."
"I found you after all. We will be together..."
"I get the feeling it's going to be a hard day today..."
"I go bring food to Hydra!"
"I go watch. You go chief. Far!"

"I grew up in Molthune. My town entered a contract with the local temple of Abadar: the taxes on the priests' extensive property were waived, and in exchange they raised the city's orphans. I happened to be one such child."
"I guess I have no choice... You're sure you can cure him, right?"
"I guess some just don't learn their lessons."
"I had no doubts about that, {race}. I'll meet you in the sanctuarrry."
"I happy see you, ally. Your visit honor mite."
"I hate these terrible blizzards! This northern weather will be the death of me – mark my words!"
"I hate you! How I hate you all!"
"I have a bad feeling about this. Maybe I'm just tired, but I sense a disaster is coming..."
"I have a fever... Give me some water!"

"I have checked and reinforced all the protective spells I could. They may not be not enough. I remind you again that the criminal is cunning and very strong. I recommend changing the guards every six hours. Wardens should receive a thorough briefing, including recommendations on maintaining the magic barriers, and they should be well-rested and ready for anything. In the case of the prisoner's apparent death, they must remain vigilant: even after death, this creature can find a new incarnation and continue to bring evil into the world."
"I have never defeated such enemies. Well, more is yet to come!"
"I have never seen such an unusual disease..."
"I have no family... But isn't our team family enough?"
"I have no idea what you are talking about."
"I have no idea what you're on about! Just leave me alone!"
"I have no idea."
"I have no time for this."
"I have no time for your taunts and riddles, crow."
"I have nothing more to say about it."

"I have nothing to give as a reward. I never made it to the mage's house, after all. And now I never will! To hell with him!" {n}Waine sighs.{/n} "You'd best find Leksen. He's probably still waiting for me near the cart on the road. Tell him I'm on my way. He'll reward you."
"I have other things that command my attention. Your master will wait."
"I have presented my evidence. Surely now the people can see that I am not guilty."
"I have proof that Irovetti intentionally bred monsters."
"I have to admit — I prefer brawling with the First World to Brevan politics."
"I have to admit, he did teach us magic well enough. I can't wait to see him again so we can thank him for it!"
"I have to find my people. I'll wait for you at the entrance once I find them!"
"I have to go."
"I haven't gotten to kill anyone today... Sad!"
"I haven't tasted fresh blood in so long… Quench my thirst."
"I hear thunder."
"I hear you're not pleased with the way Irovetti rules."
"I hear, moon radish grew sssomewhere near... but where?"
"I heard this custom of the northern tribes isn't just for children. If a man joins the tribe, he has to pass this test as well, right?"
"I highly doubt it. The ancient cyclopes, after all, had far better taste than you."
"I honestly meant to start a peaceful life. Well, it's all right, I can wipe the rust from my axe to help a friend..."
"I hope everyone has enough... Why aren't you eating, Ekun?"
"I hope lightning doesn't strike a building. I'd hate to see something burn down without an enemy in sight!"
"I hope most of the citizens had time to hide before the cyclopes invaded."
"I hope nothing happened?"
"I hope that you won't hold a grudge against the local servants of Shelyn. They are not responsible for the deeds of a bunch of miserable fools."
"I hope the devils gut you in your sleep!"
"I hope the poor thing that owned this boat was not resting on some island when mites stole it…"
"I hope the snow can hide how ugly these lands are."
"I hope there's still work for my sword!"
"I hope they're smart enough to understand who should get the prize..."
"I hope this chaos will end soon. I'm too old for such adventures!"
"I hope we didn't wake up the whole palace... Ha ha ha — at least not the whole city!"
"I hope we'll manage to avoid any duels this year..."
"I hope whatever we find in the fortress is worth all this trouble!"
"I hope you and Irovetti can settle your dispute without bloodshed?"
"I hope you liked the location I suggested for the party?"
"I hope you're ready!"
"I humbly request your protection. As recompense, I'll grant you an enchanted item from my storage. I'll even trade you the other items for only the most modest of prices. Please, follow me."
"I just think you should be more cautious, ma'am."
"I killed her with my own hands."
"I killed the four fallen heroes. The path to the Spawn of the Beast is open!"
"I knew this would happen. Thank you for at least trying..."
"I knew we could come to an understanding!"

"I know Jamandi wants to impose her stepson on you as an emissary of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}. Refuse. Take me instead. Don't look at my age — while they may have trained this half-orc to swing a sword, I've been training to rule since I was a child. I'll be of far greater use to you — both now and in the future, after I have a firm position in my family."
"I know Purple Hide traitor."

"I know a person who will own this whip with pleasure." {n}Regongar bares his teeth in a wide grin.{/n} "Whoo-o-o-shhhhh..." {n}he whispers, flexing his shoulders.{/n} "She and I will have so much fun."
"I know how much power you have, Lady Nyrissa. But do not seek my aid in your war on the Stolen Lands."
"I know nothing!"
"I know what you and your family have gone through, and no one wanted to make things worse over some stupid harness!"
"I know which way he left! It's only been a half-day, we could still catch him!"
"I know you like stories. I have thousands of them, the kind no one else in the whole world can tell you. Be my guest, little robin. I won't hurt you."
"I learn wordsss. Boldnesss! Ssstrengthhh! Sss... sssala... sssalatiousss!"

"I learned today that northern skies
Have a desert sand of their own,
Called 'snow'.
Touched by the sunlight,
It outshines any gem I've ever seen
With my dazzled eyes.
Oh, how can all these people live
With all this beauty, yet pay it no heed,
When skies throw such treasure
To their very feet?
I waited patiently until no one
Was watching,
Then stole a handful of this snow,
And ate it.
Do you laugh?
Now I know the taste of the north.
And I like it.
(Next I will eat an icicle!)"
"I left behind a freshly dressed rabbit — kind of a parting gift."
"I let you down. Forgive me. I brought you here to die..."
"I like Darven very much. Just don't tell him I told you!"
"I like this silence. Soon it will be replaced with the sounds of battle, screams of pain... We should appreciate this while we can."
"I live for fights like these!"
"I look at thisss and think, I'm ssso glad I didn't become a baron!"
"I lost this battle once, because I was alone. But it's different now. And it's going to be different. We will not bow to the Lantern King."
"I love both of you. For you I'll tear anyone in half with my bare hands!"
"I love you too."
"I love you. I do!"
"I love you. The way you smell. The way you taste."
"I mean, I went to hunt some ducks. And each time I missed the fowl, that damn dog bumped out of the bushes, laughed at me, and disappeared!"
"I might be a mere wisp compared to the Eldest, but I'll fight to the end and see the fall of the Lantern King!"
"I miss the mountains back home..."
"I missed you, Maegar."
"I must finish what I've started!"
"I must press on. My family is waiting for me, and they'll be concerned about my safety — I have to get to them, despite the risk. I beg to excuse me, Your Grace, but I must be on my way."
"I need companions. Can you summon more heroes?" [{custom_companion_cost}]
"I need supplies."
"I need to brush my hair, fix my face... This will take a while!"
"I need to find out something else."

"I need to name the golem. If I'm destined to die here with it, I'd like to at least have the illusion that I won't be alone in my hour of death.
It's quiet outside. Maybe the creature left? Or is it just waiting?
It came at night. Its black scales blended in with the starless darkness. No one noticed anything until the darkness moved and brought a cloud of suffocating acid mist down on us. I thought I was the smart one when I ran away and locked myself in the dungeon instead of fighting. This dungeon was built to endure dangerous magical experiments – it can stand up to anything, even a dragon attack. But it looks like I was just fooling myself. I'm locked inside an extremely safe dungeon within the ruins of a building that was destroyed by the dragon lying on top of it. Even with the golem's help, clearing the debris would take at least a month. I'll die of thirst long before that.
We knew there was a powerful female black dragon somewhere in these lands. She used the entirety of the River Kingdoms as her hunting grounds, and she wreaked death wherever she appeared. I even know her name: Ilthuliak. I think the scary stories I was told as a child must have been about her. I'll actually die because of a magical monster — how poetic!
I'm tired of writing. All right, golem, I'll call you Ilth. Let's try to clear out this heap. It's my only chance, I suppose."
"I need to think it over."
"I need to think."
"I never liked those Sisters!"
"I no fear you! Shut up! I will fight, I will!"
"I no talk to strangers. Go talk to Byrk!"
"I nok you left, right, chin, head until that crown fly off, shatshank!"
"I not steal, I swear!"
"I now know how I'll die. Trolls will eat me."
"I only know that the Chanter is more insane than the three other nightmares of the dungeon combined. And the terror she carries with her knows no mercy. She must be defeated."
"I only wanted the best for her! For all of us, the whole family! Boys, I think it's time you dusted this scoundrel's jacket."
"I owned the ironmonger's! The one across the street from your damned store!"
"I paid for my crimes, and I'm ashamed of my old self!"
"I passed. So what?" {n}Amiri grimaces.{/n} "Such a monster downed here, and all you do is rattle on about my old tribe?"
"I poke hollow Old Sycamore and Queen say bad. Me punish now."
"I promised I'd put an end to this. Once and for all."

"I recognize this sharp mind, and his peculiar wit. This joke has an explanation, and I shall give it to you: the heroes who went down into the dungeon to defeat the Spawn have all died, and it fed upon their pain. In the same way, the Captor nourished the daemon, by serving him his own soul. He wishes on me the same fate, just as he wrote on these rings: that I should go down to fight the Spawn, only to vanish and become its food."
"I refuse to go!"
"I regret what I've done. I shouldn't intervene in your affairs. If you agree to stay, I promise to never do so again."
"I remember my pledge. Your army will have something to cover their soft flesh."

"I remember what she was like when she entered the cave. Quiet but resolute. She radiated the light of a noble heart, which had once lost its virtue, but found the strength to regain it. The darkness of insanity, and the power of evil deities, turned this light to darkness... But I am sure, if her former self had met the monster she'd become, she would have slaughtered it without a qualm, just as you have."
"I saw a strong and vibrant forest swept away by fire. Now I see the same happening to a living city."
"I see chaos and desolation, but there is no truth in this. There is no humility, only useless clamor."
"I see no offering worthy of me. You wouldn't summon a daemon without preparing an appropriate sacrifice, would you?"
"I see no reason to reject this opportunity. This meat is ripe. To let it rot is senseless waste."
"I see. I'll move out immediately."
"I see. Let's see your passage documents, then."
"I see. Well... This is quite enough."

"I see. {kingdomname}, a charming remote province, peaceful and serene. No one knows much about it, or cares for that matter. What need do we even have of reputation, relations with major merchants, or interstate trade? That would ruin your whole image of a tranquil picturesque backwater where robbers freely sell each other's stolen livestock!"
"I see."
"I see…"
"I see…" {n}The elf sighs.{/n}
"I serve the {mf|King|Queen}. There is no price that could buy my loyalty!"
"I set off to Brevoy to get help, and met Lady Jamandi halfway."
"I shall carve her image on my chest!"
"I shall pay you an official visit in the nearest future. We will soon meet again, under less chaotic circumstances."
"I shall smite you with the fury of an astral tempest!"
"I share with Valerie the blame for their deaths. Judge us both if you wish."

"I should be clear from the beginning, we're not selling the technology. Your engineers are not permitted to repair the weapons. We'll send our specialists. However, if you're interested in any of our non-weapons technologies, our craftsmen will gladly train your own!"
"I should get some for my father..."
"I should probably fix the nets — riverbed can be treacherous around here. Snags and stones everywhere!"
"I should probably get going... Farewell!"
"I should've never agreed to be a governor. The less you are seen, the better!"
"I shouldn't have left the capital..."
"I smash you into the ground!"
"I sometimes have trouble accepting laws that would protect lowlifes like him, but he is within his rights, unfortunately."
"I speak no lie. In truth, we were not seven that day — we were eight."
"I stab thee with mine own heart... Bitch!"
"I still can't believe we have our own state. It's a good thing we followed Varn!"
"I still can't believe you took me on as your apprentice. You're a legend!"
"I stumbled across this place by pure chance."
"I suppose he was the greatest swordsman of the age? What a joke. Dancing around the battlefield like a tavern act? I have never seen someone dance during combat little one. Sounds made up..."
"I suppose you might have the impulse to hit me. But that can surely wait until the end of the battle!"

"I take a deep breath and stand still. I long to absorb every moment of joy, inhale the evaporation of someone else's soul from their thickening blood. The border between reality and dream fades. It seems that everyone beyond the wall can hear the throbbing in my head, but it's only my fantasy. A ringing silence fills the room.
The fifth sacrifice has been made. My mistress, the most beautiful of goddesses, will be happy. I will take care of everything. Fragrant flowers, cut at the climax of their beauty, are now a part of the masterpiece, which is worthy of Shelyn herself! So what if the narrow-minded priests rejected me and my gift? I serve the Never-Fading Rose herself, not the worms that bite into her stem and suck at her life-giving juices.
It won't be long now before I finish my job. I've already found the material. Her eyes are grey, and hair is dark blond. She is fades into the dirt. I will rewrite her destiny."

"I thank you heartily for your letter. I am happy this little incident was resolved to our mutual satisfaction and didn't cast a lingering shadow over your affairs with Restov. Lord Mayor Sellemius has a very high opinion of your qualities as a ruler, and I agree with him. It's good to know you possess wisdom and the profound mindset of a true politician to be able to avoid hasty decisions and to treasure the ruler's main possession — good affairs with the neighbors. I hope our friendship will remain as deep as ever.
Unfailing ally of yours,
Swordlord Jamandi Aldori"

"I thank you. You've done me a great service. Please, accept this humble gift! I made it myself. Of course, my skill is nothing compared to the beauty of nature… but I think that my spear could still prove useful to you."
"I think I'll wait for the festivities to begin. I'll be around when the Stag Lord appears."
"I think someone is coming!"
"I think something is wrong with Harrim. Should we do something?"
"I think you are teasing me on purpose."
"I think you owe me an explanation."
"I thought you and Octavia were together. Wouldn't she be jealous?"
"I thought... I could... manage... as I took the blade, I had a feeling that I... I was invincible... but this illusion... trick... oh, damn you... Nazrielle!"
"I took you for a hero... for only a hero would be brave enough to come here. Or are you something else? A shabby, tattered bit of comedy, perhaps?"
"I trample you!"

"I travel the country in secret, without servants, so I can see it for myself — not from a carriage window, but face-to-face with the people. My family would never approve, of course — but then, I never asked. I need to know {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} if I'm going to rule a part of it someday."
"I trusted my chieftain... I would have followed him anywhere!"
"I try not to think what is in this stew I ordered".
"I understand. We're all weak. But it's never too late to do the right thing."
"I used to be a library keeper in Mivon. One day, I looked around and found there were no more books to read. And so here I am! New library, new life."
"I used to have ideals like honor, valor, and justice. Wised up eventually, though."
"I vanquished the Captor and his daemon servant."
"I want go alone, got it?"
"I want to go home."
"I want to go somewhere far away. I hope Our Elder forgives us..."
"I want you dead! I want to be strong, to stand over your dead body! And over his dead body! He..."
"I want your people to become the kingdom's ears. Keep an eye on any suspicious foreigners. Never discount a strange rumor. Only united can we stand against our enemy's deceptions."
"I wanted so much to visit the First World! And now it's come to us instead! But somehow I'm still unhappy..."

"I warned you I do not wish to argue. It's not my advice you reject. You dismiss the wisdom of the great goddess, who is far more ancient than all of us. This means you will have to do without my opinion in the future. I will fulfill your order, but then you will find yourself a new advisor."
"I was a father and a husband. I did everything in my power... and failed to protect you."
"I was betrayed by my faithful. Now I seek help from a stranger."

"I was captain of a ship that sailed the {g|Inner Sea}Inner Sea{/g}. We traded with those who were stronger than us, and raided those who were weaker. Just regular life for a man of my profession. One day we stopped at one of the {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g} ports and... that's when it all started."
"I was defeated, but I am unbowed!"
"I was disappointed that I missed battling the cyclops lich who decimated Varnhold. But look – I still have a chance to join the fray!"
"I was just fulfilling my duties."

"I was prepared to condemn you for theft and murder, yet it is no trouble for me to add forgery to the counts against you."{n} Judge Celvoway peers at the page for a moment before adding, {/n}"And even so, it is my sacred duty to protect the people against the foreign pretenders and predators from your lawless land."
"I was reborn. Reborn for glory."
"I was sent by the Eldest."
"I was taken from an important affair! Embarrassed in public! And all because some lady decided she can do whatever she pleases!"
"I welcome you to the House at the Edge of Time, my darling one."

"I went to the old Temple of the Elk again today. Wicked, gloomy place. Just like my soul — it used to shine once, and it is hollow and horrible now.
Did he spy on me? Maybe I should lock him up? No, let him be. What can he do, the useless coward? Just whimper and hide."
"I will bite off your arms and legs!"
"I will come."
"I will destroy the plague sweeping these lands."

"I will do precisely as you say. But after this I will step down from office. Our opinions on the administration of a country are simply too different. Thank you for your trust, but you will simply have to find someone else to fill the Regent's position."
"I will look forward to that meeting, Your Grace, however it unfolds."
"I will make sure that goodness prevails — every time! Nothing will stop us on our way to a life of happiness and prosperity. We'll create a state where there's no room for evil, poverty, or sorrow!"
"I will not fear... I can't anymore! No fear, no fear, no fear!"
"I will pass your words to His Highness... But wouldn't it be wiser to accept a helping hand while your country can yet be saved? Think about it."
"I will respect your wishes."
"I will summon who I can. Let us see which of them will answer my call..."
"I will survive. I have to get back to my family..."

"I will wait for you there, at Sorrowflow. And please, let's explore the ruins together, just the two of us. I don't want to give myself away again in front of your companions. Breaking the Arcanotheign's conditions once was enough. – I have no wish to anger our god. So long!"
"I wish I could disappear like that… when I'm returning home drunk!"
"I wish to unite our powers — and make our enemies tremble at the very mention of our names. Together we will make our nations the greatest allies of Avistan!"
"I won't kill you. Your powers will be of use to me. From now on, you do as I say. You speak when I say. Disobedience leads to punishment. Always!"
"I won't let you escape this time, Valerie!"
"I won't lie, there's still much to be done — years of research. That's no small task for me and for my... assistant. Still, one must be ready to make sacrifices for knowledge!"
"I won't refuse your help, but I don't need any titles."

"I wonder how bad it is that I managed to translate only half of the scroll for the ritual... Unfortunately, time's running out — I'll just have to sort things out on the fly!
These simpletons won't know any better, after all. Oh, Pax Groometra... I'll soon rip your soul from those daemons' paws, I promise!"
"I wonder if any of our centaur allies survived, and where they are now."
"I wonder what a beauty contest between mites and kobolds would look like..."
"I wonder what's more disgusting — this musty dungeon or it's little ugly inhabitants."
"I wonder where I put my belt."
"I wonder who'll win the tournament. My bet's on Daggermark!"
"I would give anything to rip him back from the claws of Pharasma and her minions!"
"I would never! How can you even suggest such a thing?!"
"I wounded it! Come finish it off!"
"I yield! No more!"
"I you know! Greeting!"
"I'd like to be alone. I'll have plenty of time to think about a great many things while my wounds heal up."
"I'd like to use the tutor services of the Pathfinder Society."
"I'd never heard about {mf|him|her} before! Just appeared out of nowhere!"
"I'd never heard of {mf|him|her} before! {mf|He|She} just came outta nowhere!"
"I'd rather fight with demons than talk with fey..."
"I'd say this conversation is pointless and I'd rather leave."
"I'll answer all your questions later, I promise. Just let me feel the warmth of the sunlight on my face first."
"I'll be damned! That beast again?"
"I'll be happy to disappoint you: there's nothing here of the sort! Nothing at all!"
"I'll board this bottle! I don't take prisoners! Beware of Calis, the most dangerous pirate of all the seas!"
"I'll boil your maggots! I'll impale every wriggling piece of you on thorns!"
"I'll buy some!"
"I'll come as well. My magic can make us invisible as we approach them."
"I'll consider it. The boss may not like it, though..."
"I'll cut my hand off! Pass me the knife!"
"I'll definitely succeed next time!"
"I'll double the guard for the night, just as a precaution..."
"I'll fall at his feet, and beg him to take mercy on my young, stupid son. I'll plead for you, since you came clean — even brought everything you stole along with you."

"I'll get to work immediately. {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, when Verex the Blood God asks of me whether my revenge for my family's death was bloody enough, I can tell him the best assassin I've ever met was entrusted with the task."
"I'll give all the necessary orders once we've returned to the capital."
"I'll give the order to pack and call for a carriage immediately!"
"I'll give the order to reinforce the castle guard, and then I'll sail up the river. Don't delay, Your Grace — join me as soon as you're able!"
"I'll hate myself in the morning..."
"I'll have to mend my shirt again... You're so passionate!"
"I'll help you dig the gold up. We'll share the treasure."
"I'll just have to ask Berton to make more traps — he'll put them around the barn. See how the blighters like that!"
"I'll keep that in mind."
"I'll learn the trolls' language, and then I'll befriend one of them!"
"I'll let him continue his experiments, but only because you insist."
"I'll name the child after you!"
"I'll pay... the security tax."
"I'll pound you into the ground!"
"I'll rip your heads off!"
"I'll say! If you decide you'll have another of your disputes, please warn me in advance. I'll hire a carpenter and a roofer to fix the furniture and the holes in the ceiling!"
"I'll show him..."
"I'll stay here and take care of Linnel's body."
"I'll take you down with me!"
"I'll tell you another one! – I usually aim wherever you're yelling. It's the best way to guess where the enemies are!"

"I'll try to keep it short. I come from a long way from here — Daggermark, that is. We've never had too much in the way of law. But we always had order. It just wasn't the guard that looked after it, it was the local bandits. Every village, every quarter, they all had a gang of their own. They never touched anyone except other gangsters that came by. They were just like the guard, you see, even though no one ever gave them any authority. And if you don't have the authority, and you carry a blade — well then you're a bandit."

"I'll try to write down quickly everything that's happened. I awoke in the middle of a burning building. There was no time to look for the diary, let alone read it. I ran towards the voices I heard, and got into a big battle. I'd barely figured out what was going on, when a very strange group appeared. They helped me to fight off the assassins, and then got into a quarrel with each other, right in front of Lady Jamandi. I still hadn't had time to read the diary, so I couldn't understand anything that was happening. I somehow made up an excuse so they'd leave me alone. The strange group split into two parties, and set off for the Stolen Lands. I'm staying in Restov for now. I haven't made any new contacts. And I still haven't figured out your old ones..."
(a hand-drawn cloud weeping drops of rain stands in the place of a signature)
"You silly goat, YOU RUINED EVERYTHING! I ran off my feet trying to find a way to the Stolen Lands, and get my hands on the Disk of the Eclipse. The expeditions organized by Jamandi would have been perfect. I'd hoped to use them to find reliable companions, who could be talked into accompanying 'Kaessi' to Sorrowflow. And now here we are, still stuck in Restov — because of you! Couldn't you have simply asked to go with {name}'s group? You could even have gone with Tartuccio. I'm sure that smug gnome could have been gently steered in the right direction.
But you refused, and now I don't know what we'll do! The Swordlords are running wild looking for spies. I'm just sitting tight, hoping not to arouse suspicion.
But all this inconvenience hasn't been a complete loss. Interrogations! Oh, and it was Captain Kesten who personally came to interrogate me. How could someone punish me so, sending that delicious man to press his questions? I bet myself that I could make him blush in under three minutes – and I won, of course! Ha ha!
Ah, yes, our new contacts. You are unlikely to need them, considering your fecklessness, but still.
Kassil Aldori, a half-orc Swordlord. He accompanied 'Kaessi' when 'she' came to introduce herself to Jamandi. A boring idealist of little interest, but he was friendly enough. He obviously has nothing against tieflings – presumably because he's a half-breed himself.
Kesten Garess, captain of the guard, a tall human male, with dark curly hair. He's looking for spies, and doesn't seem to suspect 'Kaessi'.
Linzi, a halfling bard. Round face, chestnut hair. Kept getting in my way. Unreliable and irritating – you'd get along marvelously, I'm sure. Thankfully, she left with the expedition.
Tartuccio, a gnome wizard, overly fond of the color purple. Funny, I liked something about him – probably his business sense. He's in charge of one of the expeditions.
Jaethal, a pale dark-haired elf. A spook with a scythe. Always turning her nose up as if she's a queen, but elven queens don't go on expeditions in backwaters like this.
Harrim, a dwarf. Shaved head, black beard. Don't come any closer to him than an arrow shot, or you'll die from the gloom.
Valerie, a human. A fighter with a horrible blonde haircut. Mmm, Valerie! I'd gladly pay some dragon or evil wizard to catch her, pluck her out of her armor, and keep her in a cage for six months, taking care that she doesn't abuse her hair. I might just play the dragon or wizard myself!
Amiri, a barbarian with a sword the size of a kitchen table. A funny sort. Left with the expedition, along with everyone else.
{name}, a {mf|male|female} {race}. Forget what I said about Kesten and Valerie. – That's the one to catch and make blush!
Addition: silly goat, we finally got another chance to get to the Stolen Lands and seek the help from my contacts from the above list. If we switch in the meantime, don't ruin everything again — please!"
(a hand-drawn flame stands in the place of a signature)
"I'll write you a beautiful eulogy!"
"I'll... think on your words."
"I'm a fisher, my father was a fisher, his father was a fisher, and his as well. But my great-great-great-grandfather was a scholar and a wizard. Every family has its black sheep, I guess."
"I'm afraid it's not enough to accuse him of anything."
"I'm afraid of Kanerah! She will definitely roast us!"
"I'm afraid they will disappoint you, or worse. You can occasionally come across one or two decent people among them, but most mercenaries are greedy, untrustworthy thugs."
"I'm almost ready! I'm about to head to the capital!"
"I'm always alone. But you can sit here with me. We'll be sitting here alone, together."
"I'm exhausted!"
"I'm gathering my allies at the capital. Can you find the way there?"
"I'm glad it's all over, even if there was a fight. We'll talk tomorrow, once I've finished working."
"I'm glad they left! Now, please excuse me — I have much to do. We'll speak tomorrow."
"I'm glad this little misunderstanding is over!"
"I'm glad to be among your comrades, Your Highness!"
"I'm glad to see you again! Now we'll win without a doubt!"
"I'm going alone, got it?"
"I'm going to fight the great battle with such an, ahem, motley crew..."
"I'm going to knock the hell out of this flying freak if I get to him! 'Lantern King' my spit! Ha!"
"I'm going to primp, and I'm going to do it for at least an hour. Don't even think about distracting me!"
"I'm guessing you're Hargulka."
"I'm happy to answer to the best of my humble knowledge."
"I'm having fun today!"
"I'm here, my darling, to teach you another lesson."
"I'm holding it!"
"I'm honored you consider me a part of your new tribe. You're a strong and valiant warrior."
"I'm inclined to agree. You're taking on a heavy burden — but you've already proven yourself a highly capable person."
"I'm innocent! It's... a mistake! A terrible mistake! I haven't taken anything from anyone!"
"I'm just an old, lonely pilgrim, living out the rest of my days. Please, just leave me alone."
"I'm no vagrant! I'm an ascetic monk!"
"I'm not convinced. As the ruler of these lands, I order you to immediately cease all dangerous experiments and terminate that troll."
"I'm not doing anything!"
"I'm not going to waste any effort remembering your name, {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}. You {mf|barons|baronesses|kings|queens} change every six months anyway."
"I'm not here to pry or to judge. I'm just glad I could help you."
"I'm not in the mood to talk."
"I'm not interested."
"I'm not judging you. I can see you are an honest person. Just like me!"
"I'm not moving an inch until I get what's mine!"
"I'm not some boozer! That moose really said howdy to me!"
"I'm not some tenderling, but we should take on Oleg's offer. Don't know when we'll be sleeping in proper beds next time."
"I'm on the mission from Shyka the Many. Please stand aside."
"I'm only jealous of you because I love you."
"I'm pleased our... minor ideological differences are respected. We might prove extremely useful to each other!"
"I'm ready for anything, and we'll do whatever it takes."
"I'm repaying the debt. One ruler to another."

"I'm simply a humble researcher in the field of esoteric sciences, and I've chosen this location to work in peace, away from the noise of the city. When the environment is quiet and the air is fresh, ink just begs to be set to paper!"
"I'm simply a humble servant of my {mf|baron|baroness}," {n}the wizard answers coldly.{/n}
"I'm so glad Thomas and I moved here! A welcome change from the Narlmarches!"
"I'm so glad you've returned! A land without a {mf|king|queen} is like a house without a roof."
"I'm so happy you are mine!"
"I'm so scared..."
"I'm sorry I overreacted. You know I love you."

"I'm sorry, but we regard caring for your subjects very differently. I cannot countenance the way you exercise power. I am an unwilling participant in this, and I cannot be a part of it any longer. Your order will be carried out, but after this I will resign, and leave my position vacant for another candidate."
"I'm sorry, teacher, but how are we supposed to just wait and stay patient with the knowledge sitting right at our fingertips?"
"I'm sorry, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, but it's not very easy to do this sort of business out in the open. I need some kind of office – even a small one would do!"
"I'm starting to miss that tentacle thing…"
"I'm sure you have your trade permit with you, of course."
"I'm surprised, Baron{mf||ess}."
"I'm telling you, Jamandi's cache has to be here somewhere!"
"I'm telling you, he just snapped his fingers, and half of the city turned to dust! As if he disintegrated all of them at once... Is that even possible?"
"I'm the baron{mf||ess} of these lands. Your words are fair — I'll do what I can to make the roads safer."
"I'm the local baron{mf||ess} — I have every right to be here. And who are you?"
"I'm told you're an expert on local monsters. Do you know anything about the local trolls that are resistant to fire?"
"I'm too young to die!"
"I'm undead. You can't heal me with spells meant for living beings."
"I'm waiting, {mf|king|queen}. Bring Evindra to me if you want Lamashtu's blessing!"
"I'm... defeated? But I still have strength enough to take the boy with me!"
"I've already agreed to help you…"
"I've been trying to get permission to build my stables for three weeks now! Can you believe it?!"
"I've changed my mind. Just make whatever you think will come out best."

"I've completed my work, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. Obliterationr has been reforged and hardened! And I swear, it is now even more deadly than before. Please, accept this glorious weapon as a token of my gratitude for avenging me. Let your enemies fear for their empty skulls! This hammer will make you invincible."

"I've described the plant and the wound it caused as soon as I could. I hope in the future I'll be able to show these notes to some druid, to learn more about this stuff. I should have known better than go into a bush thicket — the slope was steep, and it was dangerous to climb here anyway – even if these lights-creatures won't bother us. Rismel started to behave strangely early this morning, he acted like a real madman: made me search for the shortcut to the ruins, then refused to heal me when I got wounded by the thorn. Damned priest constantly pushes us ahead — supposedly he had a message from Nethys himself, and while his god is waiting for him in the tower, the cleric has no time for petty matters. I'm starting to believe all those rumors about the followers of Nethys and their unreliability were true.
I wanted to turn back and leave the gold where it belongs, but Bryt persuaded me to keep moving forward. According to him, this Gunderson guy has got the wrong meaning of the word "treasure". The paladin is convinced that the treasure, which really is hidden in the tower, is some priceless magic knowledge left there by ancient dwellers of the island, but he's not sure he can get to the place through the thickets without my help. If I had it my way, I'd just leave this mess as it is — I seriously doubt our client is interested in some dusty old books. But this argument won't work for the cleric, who worships a god of magic, and the paladin, who serves a god of knowledge.
Bryt tried to heal my wound by himself. As a result, it is almost closed, but still stings bitterly. I hope it's a passing side-effect. Because, at least for now, I have no way back."
"I've encountered a strange obstacle in the caves. It is made of a swirling darkness. Do you know anything about it?"
"I've given peace to the Wicked Chanter."

"I've got bad news for the elf. I'll have to tell him that his wife was still alive when he blocked that passage and fled the dungeon.
Our expedition is the third one he gathered to recover his wife's remains from the caves. The first two didn't even reach the rubble. We were the 'lucky' ones. We've been wandering these halls and passages for over a month. We fell back when we encountered groups of monsters that were simply too powerful to face, then crept back to pick them off one by one, or look for ways around them. Finally we made it. I don't know how the elf even found this place. – So much time has passed, a few dozen years I believe. But he managed it. He cried out for our kineticist, and nodded to the pile of boulders blocking the passage. "Clear the path," he said, then stepped aside and turned his back. I suppose he was remembering the monsters dragging his wife into the darkness, as he crawled away and blew the passage with his last remaining bomb.
Once they'd opened a small hole in the rubble, I crawled in to see what was on the other side, as I'm the party's scout. When I reached the other side, I knew right away that something was wrong. Someone had clearly tried to clear the rubble from the other side. I kept exploring, and found signs of an old battle. There were scorch marks on the rocks from alchemical bombs, and the walls were scarred with sword strikes. And then I found it – an abandoned camp with makeshift tools, where whoever had tried to clear the rubble once lived. After exploring the camp and collecting a few things, I'd become almost certain that this was the elf's friend.
I'm telling you, it's a curse to be a scout. You take the greatest risks, and you're most often the one who delivers bad news to the party. Shame on you, dragon. You might have warned me about this. Or maybe you didn't know...
***
The elf seemed to take the news calmly. You can't tell whether he's devastated. – He's just pale and silent. Scarcely says a word. But his black eyes flare from time to time. I call him 'Grandpa', though the elf looks younger than me. He pays me back by calling me 'Red'. Well, at least he talks to me sometimes. He hardly acknowledges the rest of the party. I have a feeling that he's decided to find his wife's bones and then just lie down and die there beside her. He paid us up front, so it shouldn't bother me, I suppose. Should it? We've done clearing the rubble, and we're making our way forward again.
***
I found a second camp. I think the woman withdrew here once she realized that she was never going to be able to clear that rubble. This place is situated beside an underground lake, and it's much more comfortable: there's a hearth made of stone, rough shelves, a sleeping nook made to keep away the cold that creeps in from the water. The cave walls are covered with mosaics made of pebbles. The woman made all sorts of things: flowers and figures of animals, the sun and the moon. I looked at it all, and didn't know how I'd ever bring the elf here. Everything here suggested that she survived, and never gave up. She was waiting – and waiting for a long time at that. But the camp was abandoned a very long time. I found many footprints of monsters running through it. And something else, which looked very much like... no, I should banish the thought from my mind.
When I returned to the others, I heard the scariest sound that one can imagine in these dungeons. A soft, sweet song echoing down the tunnel. I couldn't make out any words at that distance. I ran, glad of my escape. I will tell them I found an empty camp, but we should avoid the place. It's far too dangerous. We don't want to encounter the Wicked Chanter, do we? No, we don't! Even the dragon warned us what a terrible monster it was.
And if we will stay well away from the underground lake, the elf will never have to see the mosaic on the wall."
"I've got goose bumps. Let's be careful, all right? Better to fight the bandits one at a time, if we can."
"I've got no money, and I'm too old, but... I have a son! He's strong, and healthy..."
"I've got three mouths to feed! How am I to raise them all alone, with no one to go to?!"
"I've grown tired of our arguments. You should find a more obedient and less sophisticated master of espionage. I will fulfill the order, but then I will attend to other matters."
"I've had enough! Die!"

"I've had enough. I've tried my best to make your job easier, but you have an opinion about everything! I think you need another Regent – someone who cares less about her work than I do!" {n}Octavia sighs.{/n} "I'm sorry, but you really will have to find another advisor to fill my post."
"I've handled the Weary Traveler."
"I've heard our baron{mf||ess} is tall as a troll, has hair of pure gold and can breath fire!"
"I've heard that some wizards can stop time. I dream about that when I'm with you."
"I've heard you're not exactly happy with Irovetti's reign."
"I've killed the Fallen Priestess."
"I've never even heard of Sarenrae... Tell me about her. What's she like?"
"I've never heard anything like it! I hope none of the beasts survived, otherwise I'll have to revise my defenses..." {n}Bartholomew quickly goes silent, frowns, and closes his eyes.{/n}
"I've never heard anything like it! If this is true, I'll have to revise my defenses..." {n}Bartholomew quickly goes silent, frowns, and closes his eyes.{/n}
"I've never seen anything more gruesome than the chaos that the Lantern King has created here."
"I've never seen such a huge temple of Erastil. Once we restore it, the whole world will know of it!"
"I've no doubt of that." {n}Bartholomew sneers.{/n} "But I'm afraid you'll have to find someone else for your magical needs."
"I've no need of your company right now."
"I've promised for many years that I would lead you to victory. And now I have!"
"I've seen the cub!"
"I've told you a dozen times now, you nitwit — you pay the fee, I register your complaint. If you don't have the money, then get lost."
"I've waited for this moment for long. How comforting it will be to close my eyes and know there is no need to open them again..."
"I've wanted to meet you for a while. Perhaps you could also host a tournament sometime?"
"I... Hmm."
"I... I don't know what to say! I'm sure he'll agree! I'll ask him today!"
"I... I obey the word of the victor. Farewell, Valerie."
"I... I want to be a paladin, too! To act in the face of danger and defend the light!"
"I... I'll try. Just... stay near, please. Maybe hold my hand. Or... could you carry me? Please? Could you?"

"I... I... can't! I can't do it, you understand? What if I fall, or stumble, or bump my head on a branch? Anything here could be a trap! No, everything could be!" {n}The panic returns to Waine's eyes.{/n}
"I... don't feel well today."
"I... need some time alone... Sorry."
"I... well maybe... just for a little bit... I'd like to hear your own story! To learn first-hand, and put it to paper... a book such as that would surely be the only one in the world!"
"I... well... yes! Because I'm not a traitor and I don't abandon my friends!"

"INTERIOR OF CASTLE'S HALL — NIGHT
The fat DUKE paces and frets, looking with concern toward a window. A crowd JEERS outside. FOOL sits upon the floor and watches DUKE with concern. FOOL opens his mouth to speak consoling words but then recoils when the DUKE looks at the FOOL irritably.
Duke:	Rage, hatred, wrath, and spite they shout below
	What villain must I be to earn such ire?
Fool:	Your Grace, protests this humble fool, I swear.
	The folk, they praise your acts w'out lev'ty
	For's not your deeds that draw to eyes their tears.
	Nay, you they honor with bright confetti.
	Why ask, your Grace, whose policies they loathe?
	One name, oh Duke, that King-
Duke:				-Aha! Send word
	To my finest knight, with blade like blazing
	Justice, so burning with red righteousness!
Fool:	Your Grace, if one so humble might protest?
Duke:	Speak, Fool.
Fool:		That warrior man you deem your best?
	Has all the noble heart of drunken wolves
	Who chase the shepherd's flock while licking lips
	And claim they drool for want of the sheep's safety.
Duke:	Fool, of what know you of laws, lands, and ships?
	Our king's word has this knight of his esteem,
	And yet now here you judge a soldier's worth?
DUKE raises a hand to strike the FOOL.
Fool:	No hon'r claims he when innocent heads roll
	And your knight hears anguish yet laughs with mirth.
Duke:	No crime is humor.
Fool:			Aye, no crime ‘cept when
	Sir knight snorts mead at jokes of your Grace's girth
Duke:	Forsooth! Fetch me my blade and cuirass, Fool
	And serve as squire to my thirsty vengeance!
DUKE angrily grabs his sword to find the KNIGHT as the FOOL chases after him with a breastplate in hand."
"Idiot. Your pup's of no use to us."
"Idiots! Halfwits! Another breastplate ruined! Even a goblin has more brains than a troll!"
"If Ancestor say go cut your tail, you go do it too?"
"If I am found guilty, what happens?"
"If I ever get my hands on that arsonist..."
"If I father, call daughter Bdaah. And son too..."
"If I had such power and influence, I wouldn't waste my time with such shoddy venues."
"If I knew back then, at the ressseption in Ressstov, how it would all end..."
"If I survive, I'll hold an entirely ignoble revelry..."
"If I throw the rake into the well, Mom won't know I broke it, right?"

"If I were you, I'd start looking for a new Warden. I'm not doing this any more. All I ever do here is get angry and run pointless errands. It's not like you need me here either. – You make all the calls yourself anyway. Long story short, if you wanna go stomp some goblins or fry a troll or two, just whistle. But as for being a warden, you can count me out."

"If Your Grace is willing to resolve the matter, I know a mage living nearby. I visit him from time to time to sell him reagents for his spells. He's an expert on trolls — might know why they've suddenly become bolder. And fire proof."
"If it ever comes to that, their future shall be decided by the court."
"If it means profit, then I agree."
"If only I were a sorceress! I would've invented magic that makes cauldrons clean themselves then."
"If only Xae made it... she will get us back home, she will!"

"If someone asks me
The saddest things I've seen,
I'll name a trampled rose,
A child at a mother's grave,
And two one-winged birds, locked in the same cage.
Beauty without future,
A last goodbye, and freedom lost,
Wings meant to lift you to the sky,
Now halved and useless,
What are they now – the final sadness?
And yet there's something stronger, deeper,
That lives despite it.
Hope."
"If someone did to our lake what they've done to your city, I'd skin them alive!"
"If someone slipped me a fake coin, I had no idea!"
"If the Sister brought us here, she must have had a good reason."

"If the public learns of this, there'll be no stopping the panic. I recommend we keep this incident quiet for the time being. I'll conduct an investigation without drawing anyone's attention, and in a month's time, I'll inform you of the results."
"If they let everyone build whatever they wanted, there'd be no streets left within the year."
"If this Vordakai truly wishes to meet with me, then he can come to me!"
"If this can help, then I agree."
"If those flying islands didn't come with a horde of monsters, I'd put a house on one and live there."
"If we allowed the cult of an Apocalypse Rider to flourish here, we would have frightened off far more settlers than we killed today. Think of these deaths not as a waste, but an investment."
"If we don't do him in, someone else will. Why not let the young one pay off the debt?"
"If we had a Brevan envoy with us, they'd be spying out the road to Varnhold for Jamandi."
"If we make it today, first round's on me!"
"If we meet a kobold, we hit him hard. If we meet a wolf, we climb a tree. And if a troll comes around, we run as fast as we can."
"If we share the money with the rest of the gang, maybe. But if we keep the split between just you and me..."
"If we've dealt with this challenge, we need to deal with other matters."
"If you agree to work for me, I'll build you a house here."
"If you don't know yet — you will soon. Unless you seal up your ears with dirt when we set a camp next time, hehe."
"If you let this monster go now, it will simply sow death and terror somewhere else. Do not make this mistake."
"If you lose, my heart stops along with yours."
"If you turn to the right from the square — you'll end up straight in our tavern. The food tastes good, and the lady who owns it is a gem."
"If you turn to the right from the square — you'll end up straight in our tavern."
"If you want to get anywhere, you have to grease the wheels. And you seem to be all out of grease!"
"If you're a friend, you may pass."
"If you're digging for fun, the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} can have your share instead."
