"If you've got money you don't need lying around — then sure, give it to them. Just don't say I never mentioned what sort of bastards you have serving in your guard. I should know – I picked 'em myself, ha ha. Cut-throats and cold-blooded killers send prayers to their gods when they see my guys crossing the street. Just thought I should mention what kind of guys you're pampering, and what might be in store for you."
"If your soul is in turmoil, if your mind wanders, then your knowledge and skill shall yet fail you."
"Ignorance?! I'll show you ignorance!"
"Ill omen everywhere... There will be trouble."
"Ilora? So what? I've dealt with her from time to time myself. The girl is very competent in her trade."

"Imagine this: A girl (whose name I shall not disclose) comes to town and immediately purchases the most expensive suburban villa. This newcomer spends unfathomable amounts on charity, even returning several tragically perished citizens to life at her own expense. She's very young; her rough speech and manners indicate that she's not of noble birth. This leaves the whole town wondering: how did this young lady come into possession of such a huge fortune, and why does she spend it so eagerly?
Those secrets were revealed to me when I was invited to the mysterious girl's house to provide healing services. The young lady reluctantly displayed something she'd been hiding from everyone — terrible acid burns. She forestalled any questions with a single word: 'Ilthuliak.'
The monstrous black dragon's name was well known in the River Kingdoms. She'd lived in the region for hundreds of years, inspiring terror and emptying settlements. Many experienced dragon hunters attempted to put a stop to her — and all perished. No one knew where Ilthuliak's lair was, or where she would strike next. The wounds Ilthuliak's acid breath left on my patient's body were terrible, but her soul was hurt much worse. The girl and her friends had found the lair of the dragon. They could have gathered hunters to destroy the monster, but they instead kept silent in search of profit. When the lair's mistress was absent, they would carry treasure out, little by little. Ilthuliak suspected something was happening, so she set an ambush for the thieves, and they were dealt with cruelly. My patient pretended to be dead, surviving while the dragon devoured the bodies of her friends.
She had much gold left at her disposal, but it came with the burden of memories that recalled devastated cities and countless people burned by acid. Unable to tolerate the guilt, the girl tried to atone for ill-gotten gains with good deeds.
I was able to heal her physical wounds. When we parted, she told me she planned to spend the rest of her wealth organizing an expedition to Ilthuliak's lair to end the beast.
I recently heard rumor that the villa has been abandoned for quite some time now. It's possible the owner left for other lands, but my heart tells me her bones lie in the lair of Ilthuliak — that winged terror and plague to the River Kingdoms..."
"Impossible! This must be a cyclops trick! Let's push forward and dispel this devilry!"
"Impudence! I'll see you groveling in the mud like your worm-lord!"
"In Search of Joy. Confessions of a Heretic."
"In Taldor, the streets are paved in gold! And roofs are thatched with cow patties!"
"In a place worthy of you, inquisitor."

"In ancient times, before the Earthfall, a great cyclopes empire ruled these lands. But they were unworthy of the power granted them by the Master. Their emperor took his gift to his grave, and guards it there still, in the depths of his tomb. Now the emperor has awakened, and his cyclopes have arisen. It is time to open his tomb. Go down there and accept the god's gift from his cold fingers."

"In any case, you should find yourself another curator, {name}. It doesn't make sense to me to continue as your advisor. Apparently, you already know how to spend money, what to do in every situation, and how to solve every problem. You know where to find me when you want to talk."

"In early spring, willows' leaves are the same color as her eyes.
His, too. I barely hold myself from burning them out with acid. It is his fault. Despicable, weak. If it was not for him, she would still be alive."
"Does not talk to me, looks away. Plans something, I know, I know. I have to gather forest herbs and make a hiding place, hide my charms. He is a coward, but he can steal and run away. I will punch it out of him."
"Everything hurts. I can barely walk. How could he? How? He would never bring himself to confront me on his own. ...He says his name is now Stag Lord. He says he will not let me die or let me go. He says I should not be calling him my son. Like I ever did..."
"He told me to pack my things, we are leaving soon. He now has his people and his own fortress. I'm hiding the charms in the herb cache. I probably should not. I will not be able to escape. He will not let me."

"In every scream of 'unlife is disgusting!' I hear an unsaid 'given a reason, I'd give everything for the opportunities it provides.' And this is material evidence. If you want to see a hypocrite, just look for a {g|Pharasma}Pharasmin{/g}."
"In praise of the Goddess!"
"In that case I recommend you to make haste to the nearest garrison… if you can find one. The roads are thick with trolls."
"In that case, I shall leave it up to you to decide the fate of your children — just as long as your behavior doesn't become a threat to them, that is."
"In that case, I'll complain about you!"
"In that case, you won't mind if we carry out a brief inspection of your personal effects, would you?"
"In the cage you wanted to escape so desperately, my little skylark!"
"In the game of espionage, money is dust. Are you that fond of trading dust? You shouldn't be selling something so valuable for gold."
"In the name of the goddess!"
"In your faces, jerks!"
"Indeed. And the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} pays me to perform my duties."
"Independence" Magazine
"Infidelity is the parents' sin, not the child's! Consider how kind the gods are to you — even in your dishonor, you're granted a gift of joy!"
"Insolence! Keep clinging to yourrr pitiful beliefs that yourrr deeds matterrr. When you finally accept yourrr fate, come to the Valley. I'll come forrr you therrrre."
"Interesting architecture. I should visit the cities of the Material Plane more often..."
"Interrogation?"
"Intruders! Kill them!"
"Iomedae, I am the sword of your justice!"
"Irovetti brought a whole army of bards to Littletown, and used them to crush his enemies."
"Irovetti scared off all the best teachers. He's probably blaming everyone but himself, of course."
"Irovetti sends his regards!"
"Irovetti! Now you're going to pay for everything!"
"Irovetti... Confetti... Damn it all, why does he have such a difficult name?!"
"Is everyone here? Jamel's about to announce the winner!"
"Is everyone taken care of?"
"Is he some kind of maniac or something?"
"Is it just me, or are you really sad?"
"Is it not insane to be faced with death and stop to question whether you may be breaking some law or rule? {Name} acted wisely."
"Is it your army?"
"Is it... over? The beast that overthrew me lies breathless at our feet. Come now, my spring — the Eldest awaits!"
"Is that how you speak to your {mf|baron|baroness}? Face {mf|him|her} directly and say a proper farewell!"
"Is that so? Ha, ha, hmmm..." {n}Regongar measures you with an openly lustful look.{/n} "I will... think about it."

"Is that so? I hope you will rule your lands with the same resolve you show today. When I decided to ally with the mayor of {g|Restov}Restov{/g}, I was confident in my resolution. In time I grew to question my decision, but of course we must look always forward. Never let doubt shake your determination!"
"Is that so? Two dirty vagabonds leeched themselves onto my caravan, and now they're asking to be paid. Did we forge a binding contract of some sort?"
"Is that the sound of your knees shaking in fear?"
"Is there not virtue in lending a merciful hand to someone who's been damned by all? Just as I now lend mercy to you, who lost yourself to anger?"
"Is this the flower you were looking for?"
"Is {Name} here? Is {mf|he|she} drinking with {mf|his|her} people?"
"Is {mf|he|she} here?!"
"Isn't it time to take them off the fire?"
"Isn't such a verdict too strict? It's only money, after all. Can we blame him for living so long in an evil, lawless country that he eventually acquired something of a bandit's mentality?"
"Isn't... isn't that your throne?"
"It appears that the restless old man started preaching again..."
"It appears that they are connected to that flower... I think I know how to use them to clear our path."
"It burns!"
"It can't… it can't be! Thank you, {name}!"
"It clean here, and air fresh. I fix that!"
"It didn't work out… Sorry, Kimo."

"It disgusts Kurgess when people cripple themselves, so we reject alcohol and stupefying potions. I shall prohibit these among your soldiers. The spirit grows stronger in a mighty body! Kurgess dislikes foul play, so cheating is also illegal."

"It doesn't seem you care much for your pack, allowing a bunch of moneybags merchants to entertain themselves in a place that might instead have fed your starving people... not to mention the children of {g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu{/g}!"
"It doesn't smell at all! And even if it did, how's that my fault? This is a pub, for gods' sake — we get all sorts here!"
"It feels like someone is watching us all the time..."

"It has many squads joined together: my fighters, other {g|Swordlords}Swordlords'{/g} forces, {g|Restov}Restov{/g} militia, mercenaries. Restov is surely a free city, but it always relied on us Aldori to protect it."
"It is all in the radiant Sarenrae's power! She teaches us to show mercy to all — even the most terrible of criminals."

"It is an open secret that things are not going too well for your kingdom of late. Bandits and monsters, which you supposedly exterminated, are swarming your countryside once more. You are losing the trust and respect of your subjects. Everyone sees that you are failing to meet the responsibilities of a proper ruler. – It's just that not everyone dares to say this out loud."
"It is becoming more and more interesting..."
"It is high time that Varn and his people were rewarded for their many feats. I'm glad the moment has finally come!"

"It is insane when faced with death to stop and question whether you may be breaking some law or rule. Even more insane would be to ask forgiveness for making the right decision. Sorry, {Name}, but your words display a lack of wisdom."
"It is just rain. Let us push onward."
"It is not an impossible task. After all, what use is an apology if it cannot ever be given?"
"It is not my decision. But they do not deserve such treatment."

"It is perhaps Avistan's most popular dish. In the capital of Cheliax, it is baked in a cheese crust and sprinkled with lemon juice. The local fishermen use a different cooking method in Qadira, which is on the opposite end of Avistan. There you will find it finely chopped and mixed cold ingredients. The exact origin of the dish remains unknown, but it is generally believed to have been invented in Andoran, and spread around the globe by seafarers and pilgrims.
It's served as plain pâté in its most basic version. To prepare it, soak the herring in spiced marinade, then mince it into a spreadable paste. Add a mashed tart green apple, hard-boiled quail eggs, the freshest butter you can find, and half an onion. The list of ingredients may vary in the inland regions. In the region of Nirmathas, beef or lamb is used for this snack. I once tasted a highly original and equally highly disgusting version cooked with milk and mushrooms on the border of Druma..."
"It is ridiculous!"

"It is the oldest, biggest, and the most prestigious arcane academy in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}. It's very influential. Students come from all over the world to master the art of magic. Mind you, the school is tuition-free."
"It is time for the sacrament. The First Faithful will bless us!"
"It is true. Your time has come, Harrim."
"It is with the greatest joy that I announce the founding of my barony in Dunsward. It shall be called... Varnhold!"
"It looks like Remus has returned from his exile..."
"It looks like we're done here – and looks like we scattered another potential threat to the kingdom."
"It may be difficult, but at least it won't be boring!"

"It might be hard to believe, but I was once a goblin. I died and was reincarnated into a nice elven lass. But I then got bored and was reincarnated as an android. Next was a hill giant. Then a merfolk. Then a kobold. I'm not even sure who I am anymore without looking in a mirror."
"It might sound surprising, but I like goblins. They're fun to be around."

"It seems like a bad idea. I have little doubt that the first thing these newcomers will do is use threats and blackmail to suppress the local merchants. The very merchants who rely on our support and protection!"
"It seems the tavern keep is pouring us what's left of the former owner's brew."
"It seems the winds are changing. The winds, and perhaps more."
"It should be an easy transition, though — after all, he already purchased your former property from the crown."
"It sounds like your son's not the one dreaming of working in the mines. You seem to be the one invested in that 'good money,' lady!"
"It was a good fight today. Glory for fighters, peace for the fallen."
"It was a great hunt! This will make a nice story to tell at home!"
"It was a scandal! The judge had to leave his post after that, of course. How can someone who was caught cheating on his own wife be trusted to judge others?"
"It was arson! You orchestrated the whole thing! It had to be magic — no ordinary flame could burn so hot!"

"It was brought here by Taldans from the Fifth Army of Exploration. {g|Taldor}Taldor{/g} and {g|Qadira}Qadira{/g} were enemies for ages. Thousands of years ago, a soldier broke into the temple of Nethys and stole the relic, to sell it, or secretly hoard it as an heirloom. Hundreds of years later, his own kin, or the kin of its hundredth buyer, brought the Disk to these strange lands, where the Taldans had come – uninvited, as usual – and which they finally vanished from with little trace. Sometimes, history is as intricate lace – you'd never guess where it begins, and where it ends."

"It was called Sorrowflow in the chronicle we read. It was once a Taldan town, founded by the veterans of the the Fifth Army of Exploration. It stood on the shores of a turbulent river – and that was what destroyed it. One night, a terrible flood devastated the settlement, killing many and driving the rest to flee. Only the tower on the cliff remained, which was too high for the flood to reach. Water covered the ruins for a long time, but last year it receded. My friends found a chronicle, which recounted the destruction of the city, and spoke of the Disk of the Eclipse which was kept there. They managed to track down the ruins, but were frightened away by the monsters and beasts that roam the area."
"It was half that price last week!"
"It was not {mf|his|her} fault,"{n} declares Eimar as he steps forward. {/n}"I accept responsibility for-"
"It was perfectly reasonable. Just the way a leader should think."
"It was so gratifying to assume my true form again. It's a pity I had to return to the mask…"
"It was time to end the carnage between us and the two-legged. I am glad to see this day."
"It wasn't a massacre — it was justice! Everyone knows that judge always ruled in favor of the rich!"
"It will be a lengthy task, and this is how it shall be measured."
"It will be done. All your neighbors will hear how your people support you. That will make them respect you!"
"It's a brave choice. We'll see what this risky cooperation brings us."

"It's a dark and sordid story — and I swear I'd give my life to learn the full truth of it. {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} was founded by four families and ruled by their four trade houses for centuries. We quarreled from time to time, of course, and property didn't always change hands peacefully, but none of us would dream of impinging on another family's lawful rights."
"It's a good day to test our fate. Are you ready?"
"It's a good thing you got rid of those monsters and bandits, Your Grace!"
"It's a little bare here for now... But it's all right! If we work hard, in a few years this will be a great town!"
"It's a long story, but the Horned Hunter, that monster who toyed with us in Lostlarn Keep, is the very same creature that now torments the kingdom."
"It's a miracle we escaped Pitax with our lives!"
"It's a pity the hunt you held was ruined. I do hope it wasn't the last one!"
"It's a pity we had to fight the centaurs. They live in my lands, so they're my subjects too!"

"It's a pity you've done so. You've deprived me of my pleasure. And I hate it when someone deprives me of my pleasure." {n}He stares in your eyes for several moments, then turns away.{/n} "Move, nothing to do here," {n}he drops behind his back.{/n}

"It's a pity." {n}The elf whispers a spell and boundless peace and tranquility descend upon you. Unable to even reach for your weapon, you watch Kamala leave with dignity, the fey running after her, laughing.{/n}
"It's a shame — all these years, and they still can't come to terms. They're in the same country! What if they get attacked?"
"It's a shame. Think what life in Brevoy would be like if they could just stop all the infighting!"
"It's all alone and scared! We need to look for it!"
"It's all because of you! Die! DIE!"
"It's an honor to greet you, Your Grace."

"It's an unusual relic, called the Disk of the Eclipse. I once heard a beautiful story that it was created from the shadow that hides the sun and the moon. But I don't think that could be the truth. {g|Nethys}Nethys{/g} is the god of magic, who was once a mortal wizard, and relics from his temples are usually very powerful. There are many among his followers who think that solving the mysteries of magic – even rivaling their deity – is the best way to serve him. One such follower created the Disk, long ago in the distant past."
"It's been a long, long joke... And you're the punchline! Laugh it up!"
"It's breaking the roof!"

"It's done," I said.
Miliken studied me with narrowed eyes.
"You look awfully clean," he said. "Where's the knife?"
In answer, the first shouts went up from the inn.
"Fire!" screamed Ilna, and then other voices joined hers.
In an instant, Milikin's entrepreneurial instincts took over, and he sprang for the door, tossing the crossbow aside. Outside, the roof of the inn was already smoking oily black against the sunset, ﬂame licking through the thatching in places. With a scream of pain, Milikin ran for the creek. I looked to Phargas. Needing no further cue, we each grabbed up armfuls of supplies and sprinted off in the opposite direction.
After ten minutes of leaped brambles and ducked branches, we stopped to catch our breath. Back the way we'd come, the smoke was still visible, though the sounds had faded to just the faint and frantic pealing of a church bell.
"That was close," Phargas said, leaning against a tree and breathing hard.
"Agreed," I puffed, staring down at the cloak full of bread that now made up our sole possessions. Then the sound of the bell reminded me of something.
"About what you said back there," I asked. "You said Shelyn. I thought you were a priest of Desna?"
Phargas grunted.
"A man's faith is a personal thing," he said, tying up the cloak. "Now shut up and keep running."
And we did."
"It's getting disgustingly humid..."
"It's getting out of control! The ceiling is barely holding!"
"It's good my sister was away when all this started. On the other hand, I'm worried about her..."
"It's good to take a respite from the city life and have a party in the wild..."
"It's hard to find forgiveness for any creature that does such horrific things… but I doubt forgiveness would mean anything to a monster like him."
"It's how I learned my craft. That's what the Thorn Scar used to say: 'Big thumbs up to Varrask's hands! Big thumbs up to Varrask's head!' Which meant they respected me."
"It's just a fever! I am not dan... khe... ger... kha... khaaaaAAAAAAARRGH!"
"It's just not right. What if my son feels drawn to mining? He's a halfling, so he won't be allowed — what do I tell him?"
"It's just old rubbish here! Pots, axes, spinning wheels... Couldn't you find something valuable?!"
"It's like a blizzard, but hot!"
"It's niccce... calm..."
"It's nice to see the beginning of a future noble family..."
"It's not for me, it's for the hungry! I'm collecting donations for those who can't make it on their own. It's for Desna's grace!"
"It's not just them, either — none of Brevoy's noble houses are particularly friendly with each other at the moment."
"It's not that the money's fake — it bears traces of another world."
"It's not the first time I've heard that, and I'm sure it won't be the last."
"It's not the first troubles to fall upon our heads. We'll survive this too, Your Highness!"
"It's not the same!" {n}Octavia turns to you for support.{/n} "Would you allow cruelty like this in your lands? Order him to set the troll free!"
"It's raining again! Oh, how I love the unforgettable sensation of wet clothes sticking to my back."
"It's smart. Now shut your trap and bring me something to eat, dear apprentice."
"It's so easy to trick you, silly {mf|boy|girl}..."
"It's so good to breathe the open air and see the sky again! Being locked in a dungeon almost drove me insane."

"It's so long, I don't even know where to begin." {n}Darven grins.{/n} "Although, I guess, you're only interested in the things I've been accused of. I... I did, in fact, kill a {g|Cheliax}Chelish{/g} noble, and I participated in a rebellion. But all of this happened by total accident!"
"It's so quiet here… I can't even hear my own heartbeat. Is my heart still beating in my chest, or have they taken that from me too?"
"It's so refreshing to work for someone with an open mind! Believe me, Your Grace, I'll prove to be a valuable ally!"
"It's still too early for the official proceedings. Go, speak with the guests."
"It's such a relief to finally start working on something new… I think this time it will be a tract on the philosophy of ogres. With autobiographical remarks."
"It's the end for you rats!"
"It's the natural order of things. It's how the world has been since it was born, and how it will continue to be until it, too, makes that final journey."
"It's the {mf|King|Queen}! Attack {mf|him|her}!"
"It's them again!"
"It's time to leave. Farewell."
"It's time we had a rest."
"It's time we keep our promise. We award you with the secret weapon of our order. It is a spell that quells all wrath, pacifies berserkers and binds evil. We are sure you will use it wisely."
"It's time we turn from prey to hunters!"
"It's true, I could help you with your plight. It is within my power to cure your husband's ailment. However, I cannot do so for free."
"It's true, life's gotten better for everyone with the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} on the throne!"
"It's true,"{n} Eimar proclaims, eliciting a gasp from Talwyn.{/n} "I concocted a story to get {name} in trouble. We would not be here now were it not for my deception."
"It's undead again!"
"It's warmer here than in Brevoy... But is the soil fertile?"
"It's wet near the lake and windy up here on the hill. A fine place to throw garbage at your neighbors' heads though. Ouch!"
"It's you! Good day, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!"
"It's your life, and your decision — I'm not here to judge. I'm just glad I could help you."
"It's... it's medicine, sir."
"It's... perfect!"
"Item four, the most important one: the participant must assume the shape of a giant frog."
"Item four, the most important one: the participant must routinely enter desperate fits of screaming."
"Item four, the most important one: the participant must say TENTACLES at least once every ten words."
"I… I won't let you!"
"I… I… I'm… Wa… Waine," {n}he manages at last. His eyes are wide, so wide they look like they might fall out of his sockets.{/n}
"I…" {n}Dalton frowns.{/n} "Don't get me wrong, Your Grace, but I've family in {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, so my road always must take me there. No matter how dangerous the journey."
"Jaethal, no! Stop!'
"Jarmuld, down there! Please help him!"
"Jealous mediocrity! Get out of my sight!"
"Join me! The food, is good!"
"Join your ancessstorsss... Valerie..."
"Joke bad! Hit joker!"
"Joyous day!"
"Jubilossst... your time... hasss come..."
"Judging by the discolorations on his pants, I'd say he spots rabbits regularly."
"Judging by the odor, I can tell exactly what the main ingredient in this 'paint' is."
"Jump mice my friendsss. Good have friendsss!"
"Just as a farmer tends his land, providing shade to spots with too much sun or water to soil that is too dry, you must be attentive to the movements and condition of your heart and soul."

"Just because someone asks me to do something doesn't mean I actually do it," {n}Bartholomew says as he shrugs.{/n} "Though to be honest, in these parts, you can't really tell a local bandit from a peaceful hunter based on looks alone."
"Just close your mouth."

"Just do what you consider right and let others discuss it. You know, not everyone gets a chance to become a baron, so discussing a baron's actions is actually all the unlucky ones can do."
— Jubilost Narthropple

"Just don't start this... that..." {n}Amiri stops, trying to choose the right words.{/n} "Don't talk me about honor and valor. I know already!" {n} She frowns and turns away.{/n} "Still, I owe you thanks. You have the heart of a true chief," {n}she adds a moment later.{/n}
"Just hang on, Verdrin! We're almost there!"
"Just let me... Damn, where are they..."
"Just like a garden cannot flourish on dry rocks, an artisan's talent yields no fruit without a workshop..."
"Just like that. Took 'em down nice and easy. Whoa, pal — you sure you wanna be walking around in a dead man's clothes?"
"Just look at this place... Well, at least we don't have to deal with metal monsters like in Numeria."
"Just move, will you?! No messing around."
"Just one more question! I really need this for my book!"
"Just simple bandits? We'll deal with them in no time!"
"Just spit it out already! What'd you find when you got back?"

"Just stand lookout like you were told." {n}The man's voice carries the weight of command; he seems to be the leader of these bandits. His bushy beard is matted, and remnants of the last day's meals are still evident in it.{/n}
"Just think of it, I'm in the First World, and wasting my time just standing around waiting!"
"Just what do you think you're doing?"
"Just yesterday, you took the book I was studying from — it seemed to have some powerful spells!"
"Justice will prevail."
"Kabron, calm down!"
"Kagar not know. Damage too big. We stay in village, not survive long. Need go somewhere away from Thickskins, look for new place to live."
"Kanerah..."
"Karasssk!"
"Keep going, {race}. I will finish... this. And follow."
"Keep moving if you would rather not freeze to death!"
"Keep talking... I don't believe your tales!"
"Keep your dogs away from me! I'm a man of the arts!"
"Keep your eyes peeled."
"Keep your position! Do not fall back!"
"Kha... Kha..."
"Khh, khh... Something's... wrong with me... Feels like..."
"Khhh... Help..."
"Kill 'em!"
"Kill borba!"
"Kill me, torture me if you want, Nyrissa. But I will serve you no more."
"Kill slimy kobolds! Kill!"
"Kill that toad!"
"Killed by a tree. One less fledgling woodcutter"
"King Nok-Nok kicked me once. So strong! Good King!"

"King Tartuk wants to make deals with borba. King Tartuk teaches us to not eat borba. Hargulka disagrees. Borba sly. Borba not respect trolls, want to fool trolls, make trolls weak. Trolls will not be borba's dogs! Hargulka will conquer you, destroy your homes. Then, Hargulka and Tartuk will start to make deals with you."
"Kneel, servant! Kiss the ground before a living god!"
"Kneel, worm! The herald of Nethys will smite those who won't submit to the great god!"
"Knees or neck first...?"
"Kobold asssault! Kobold attacksss! Kobold victory!"
"Kobold go past bush. See scale tail. Poke it knife! It one more kobold!!"
"Kobold go tunnel... and fall his own trap! Ha-ha-ha-ha!"
"Kobold ressst now. Ssso tired."
"Kobold sssilent sssneak, then big asssault!"
"Kobold ssstong, fierccce! All run from kobold!"
"Kobold steal catapult. Not know what do. Shoot himself in wall!"
"Kobold think — they little dragon. Dragon think — they little food. Ha-ha-ha-ha!"
"Kobold victory! Glory! Glory!"
"Kobolds are so sweet! I'm so glad you were able to make friends with him!"
"Kobolds eat me alive! What is this?!"
"Koboldsss! Glory! Glory!"

"Kressle, a task. As soon as you're done with the taxes, find an old hut in the woods upstream of the Thorn River — and burn it to the ground. This is the Stag Lord's wish. He literally said, 'Burn! Burn!'
It was originally going to be Dovan, but he grew upset when he learned nobody lived in the hut. Said burning houses with no one in them was 'boring.' So I said I'd send someone more reliable. It's a strange task, but try to finish it quickly. And no asking 'What the-?!' or 'Why bother with this trifle instead of preparing for war with Restov?!' We'll get to that.
A."

"Kurgess was a {g|Taldor}Taldan{/g} villager of remarkable figure! He traveled around towns, visited trade fairs, took part in every competition and show, and always won. It's only natural that everybody was jealous."
"L-l-lied how? Why...?"
"Lady Aldori doesn't have guests very often, but today's occasion warrants a celebration!"
"Lake Silverstep, my lord. I bring fresh fish for sale!"
"Lamashtu be our mother. Nok-Nok be our father."
"Lamashtu be pleased!"
"Lamashtu can't be stopped... Bloom... be... soon..."
"Lamashtu favors us! She blessed the pack with a new cub! A beautiful female cub, marked by the goddess sacred touch!"
"Lamashtu herself protects me! You don't dare even touch me!"
"Lamashtu is watching you. As do we. Remember that."
"Lamashtu, have mercy!"
"Lamashtu-serving be killing, be burning!"
"Lantern enemy make bad lantern ghosts. Maybe he send unreal Ancestor in our village?"
"Larzio should write of commitment to duty. Of loyalty and honor."
"Last group of idiots who paid me to escort them was planning to raid a wyvern's nest. When they got there, I kept to a corner and didn't lift a finger."
"Lately these dismal lands are much more fun! Mortals running around, screaming, fussing... What's happened?"

"Law is the gateway to civilization — and many are the sacrifices we shall gladly make in its name. From now on, the state is your {mf|father|mother} and your god. Serve the law — and it will protect you. Reject the law — and your life will be as smoke in the wind."
"Lay down your weapons, apostate."
"Lead on, chief. Let's show those bandits a good time."
"Lead, and I will follow."
"Learn."
"Leave me alone! I'll deal with my problems myself!"
"Leave the poor sod alone, you hear?"
"Leave these lands immediately. And leave your loot as well. If ever we meet again, I'll kill you."
"Leave! Now!"
"Leave, or I'll call the guards!"
"Leaving them to die bought you mere minutes. Believe me, I would have held on until your arrival."
"Leg it!"
"Leg it, leg it!"
"Legacy... Can't... Unworthy... Rightfully ours..."
"Legend of the Archknights of Avistan", Vol. 1
"Legend of the Archknights of Avistan", Vol. 2
"Let go of me, you imbeciles!"
"Let me ask you about something else."

"Let me be frank, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. I've been in this position for too long, and each day I feel more worthless. You should find yourself another High Priest – someone more flexible. As for me, I am too old to argue, or play your tutor now and again." {n}The priest bows and turns away.{/n}

"Let me remind you that while the trading post in question is situated on the land which now belongs to you, its owners, Oleg Leveton and his spouse Svetlana, are of Restov origin. They have been paying their taxes to Restov for many years, and enjoyed the benefits of the city's protection. Restov is not accustomed to tossing away its subjects. However, as Oleg and Svetlana have expressed the desire to go under your jurisdiction, Lord Mayor Sellemius is inclined to act benevolently and let it happen, but not without a precondition.
Some debts are owed by the Levetons' post. I suggest it's only fair if you, as its new patron, would compensate the city for this sum. Besides, the road connecting the post with the rest of the world is in a deplorable condition and needs urgent repairs. Since the bigger section of this road runs through your lands, you should show some care for your subjects and make all repairs, helping to establish trade connections and proving your intention to do more for your citizens than mere tax-collecting. Until the repairs are finished, the trading post stays under Restov's protection.
Waiting for your swift reply in words as well as in actions,
Swordlord Jamandi Aldori"
"Let me show you a trick. I need a sword, four candles, an apple and a monkey. Hey, Babarm, bring in the monkey!"
"Let me whisper to the flowers. I think I'll be able to help!"
"Let the battle commence!"
"Let us begin! Your sleight of hand against our most sophisticated devices! Who'll win?"
"Let us go before they take us up there!"
"Let us put an end to this madness. Peace will be restored — with iron and blood, as circumstances require."
"Let us settle this... diplomatic misunderstanding with the First World, and return to matters of court."
"Let us through! The road should be free for all!"
"Let's begin!"
"Let's go look in the pantry!"
"Let's go with us, beastie… You'll like it there!"
"Let's go, everyone! If we survive, drinks are on me!"
"Let's go. For Varnhold!"
"Let's go. Let it burn. There's nothing more to do here."
"Let's have one more! And then two more!"
"Let's leave this place, I beg you. I can't stay here any longer."
"Let's look at your wares."
"Let's put them back to rest!"
"Let's see — he's smart, he's handsome, and he loves your daughter with all his heart. That seems like a good start!"
"Let's see... Well, what do we have here? A book? A literature fan, huh?"
"Let's send Linxia to hell!"
"Let's settle it with a fight! Yes!"
"Liacenza family! Today is the day of our reckoning! Destroy Irovetti! For {mf|King|Queen} {Name}!"
"Liar! We've been to south, it's no better than here!"

"Liars!" The ghost's face twisted with fury. "It's not enough that you keep me imprisoned, but you lie to me as well?!" He screamed, the sound tearing at our sanity. "Make your demands and begone!"
So we...

"Lies and slander!"{n} explodes the magistrate. {/n}"How easy it must be for a playwright to spin such a web of falsehoods to confuse the listener and betray his neighbors! No, good people of {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, Eimar Deschamp was born not in our fair nation but in {g|Taldor}Taldor{/g}, where intrigue and backstabbing are second nature. It should come as no surprise that he would find a kindred spirit in {name}."
"Lies, all of it! Some sins can't be forgiven. What's the point if a murderer repents? It won't bring back the dead!"
"Life for life!"
"Life is fleeting, but law is forever."
"Like it or not, I'm turning you in to the guard! After what you've done, you're no son of mine!"
"Like it, borba? You like it?"
"Linzi... welcome your end..."
"Listen close, now. I don't give a damn how much you had to pay for that piece of paper."
"Listen to me! It's wrong to cling to your dishonorable behavior!"
"Listen to me, students! Today we'll be rid of that old buzzard! For {mf|King|Queen} {Name}!"
"Listen to me, trespasser. You sought a kingdom, I seek something simpler — an apology."

"Listen to me... I see you're no ordinary folk. Probably in the service of some rich merchant? Or maybe even the local ruler? We don't need to be enemies. Let me keep guarding this fortress — in return, I'll give my best golems to serve your lord! Well, you've already broken the best ones... But I'll make new ones!"
"Listen to yourself, dear! One should never risk angering the Lady of Graves, even if out of grief!"
"Listen, dear citizen, do you want this fine nation to become another Galt? Do you want everyone to live like THEY do? Do you want your children to starve?"
"Listen, good lady... Forgive me, what is your name?"
"Listen, good sir... Perhaps we could... strike an agreement? I can be very generous!"
"Listen, hon. You wanted a magic rod — I sold you a magic rod. If you wanted a magic rod that still had charges left, you should've said so."
"Listen."
"Lived a long life, but this mess is something new. Thank you for sorting everything out, {mf|baron|baroness}."
"Lizardfolk aren't real people! – There's nothing to be sorry about! They're only good for making boots!"
"Lockpicking Contest"

"Long ago, {g|Mivon}Mivon{/g} was founded by the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g}, who refused to bow before the new ruler and fled {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}. While not Brevans anymore, our people and the people here have a lot in common, as I've heard the barony here was founded by people from {g|Restov}Restov{/g}. We look upon them as distant cousins, I suppose." {n}Dalton smiles.{/n} "Welcome cousins, that is, not family you'd rather forget."
"Long live the {mf|King|Queen}!"
"Long live the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}!"
"Long story short, we've got our ways. So that's why I'm asking for your permission and your help — we want to bring a few brave and quick-witted folks together, and do everything by the book."
"Longshanks get in shaman's way — bring them low and make them pay!"
"Longshanks scary!"
"Longtail have past again. Have future again."
"Longtail ready to travel."
"Look again at the testaments of those you sent to die. They all blame you! Enough excuses! Who are you lying to? – Me or yourself?"
"Look around. This fortress belongs to you now."
"Look at me, Irovetti! I do this in the name of our love!"
"Look at me. Don't turn away. Why so silent all of a sudden?"
"Look at our master! A true example of knighthood, he is!"
"Look at these rings. The Captor thought that you serve the Spawn of Rovagug, just like his pet daemon served him."
"Look at this picture. The lines! The colors!"
"Look at this shield. The Weary Traveler believed that you are just another victim of self-delusion, much as he was."
"Look at this temple! What proportions, what harmony! It truly was built by a genius!"
"Look at this! These books are newer than the ones on the other shelves. Is this someone's idea of a joke?"
"Look at those clouds... Might start raining any minute."
"Look at {mf|his|her} favorites!"
"Look away, boy! You keep away from them, hear? Those are bandits."
"Look out lads!"
"Look who's here!"
"Look! I have blue paint! We can paint your faces, you hair, your clothes!"
"Look! It's the chosen one!"
"Look! It's {mf|King|Queen} {Name}!"
"Look! Look!"
"Look! Someone's coming, coming! Right here!"
"Look, I meant no disrespect, all right? Just... try to avoid killing anyone this time — please. Cleaning up corpses is a real hassle."
"Look, Irovetti, it's {Name}! {mf|He|She} defeated you once — {mf|he|she}'ll do it again!"
"Look, Your Grace! The cultists!"
"Look, a trail! They must have dragged it along the road. Let's go — no way they made it far with something so heavy!"
"Look, a way to the surface! Great! I was feeling like a prisoner in these caves."
"Look, as if you're looking in a mirror. This is what I can make of you. A perfect face. A perfect spirit. A perfect warrior."
"Look, it's Regongar! Get him!"
"Look, it's pouring again! When the weather gets like this, all I want is to dance."
"Look, it's the {mf|King|Queen} of {kingdomname}!"
"Look, it's the {mf|king|queen} of {kingdomname}! It's an honor to meet you!"
"Look, it's {mf|King|Queen} {Name}! Have you heard what they've been saying about {mf|him|her}?"
"Look, look! Help has arrived! Hurrah!"
"Look, there are children's books here!"
"Look, there go warmblood! Why come in village?"
"Look, there {mf|he|she} is!"
"Look, they're running! Get them!"
"Look, this is the rune of the Langebukk clan."
"Looks like a storm's coming!"

"Looks like an act of magical sabotage to me. And guess who the prime suspect is! Our dear western neighbor! Now that our wastelands have been turned into farmlands, Dunsward has become a tasty pie, and everyone wants a piece!"
"Looks like it's worse here than we thought."
"Looks like we got their attention. Well, the thicker the rye, the easier the harvesting."
"Lords and ladies! Today, we are here to honor three brave people who have done the impossible — they've tamed the Stolen Lands!"

"Lords often consider us nothing but milk cows for the state. We appreciate that you have let us go about our business. You didn't rob us as you grew in power. We're not used to such decent treatment, and your good faith and understanding have been a great boon. My friends and I discussed it, and decided that we'd return the favor. Tell us, what can we do for you, Your Highness?"
"Lose your ways, lose your minds, lose your lives..."
"Lost."
"Lotslegs! Lotslegs! Leg it while they still there!"

"Love!
The caravan to the Five Kings Mountains will leave tomorrow, me and kids have to go with it. It's been days since we've heard anything from you. I hope your hunt went well, and you'll catch up with us on the road or will meet us in the Langebukk quarters in the mountains.
The Road of Shields nowadays is safe for a caravan, but might be dangerous for a lonely traveler. Our scouts spot trolls all over the region. I'm leaving behind my favorite bow. It will protect you against those cruel giants.
I'll be praying to Desna day and night with one wish: to see you again."
The poor condition of the paper suggests that the letter was written centuries ago.
"Lower than vermin," {n}Valerie says with a grimace.{/n} "With your permission, I would happily cleanse the world of this trash."
"Lucky day for you, vagrant. You get to keep begging another day — but somewhere else, got it?"

"Ludriggan Vanderlapius and Daughters" Publishing house
"I spent half of my life in a temple of Sarenrae. I served the goddess loyally and blindly, never considering that no one, not even an immortal deity, can walk your path for you. I carried out Sarenrae's will, but never stopped to think about what it was exactly, or what lay behind it, the source of the kind goddess' kindness. Then an unknown preacher came to town, and challenged the senior priests of all the great temples to debates. Some laughed at him, others defamed him, but many, like me, saw the truth in his words. We followed him into the Arthfell forest, where he'd meditated for seven years, gaining insights into truth. The teacher opened my eyes to the Wise Way – the path that the kind gods follow, and the common thread that unifies all their teachings and makes them worthy of veneration. Some understand it through the Phoenix, in burning instincts and a fiery will. Others go the way of the Unicorn or Chameleon, achieving peace in silence. Those who have a powerful voice go the Lion's way, and preach the Wise Way to others. I found enlightenment on the way of the Wolf – in cutting wood, carrying water, and working without thought of thanks..."
"Lying does not befit a ruler, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
"MORTALS ARE PATHETIC. ONLY THE DEAD BECOME CLOSER TO GOD."
"Maaaaegaaarrr..."

"Madness, mortal. Darkness and madness are the monster's sword and shield, its food and the material that its shell is made of. The heroes I summoned here descended into madness. They lost their minds, and the Spawn of the {g|Rovagug}Beast{/g} fed upon their insanity. Somehow, I avoided the same fate. They went down into the darkness, driven by the noblest of intentions – and were rewarded only with eternal torment."
"Maegar" seeks to increase the {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom}'s arcane might, no matter the cost.
"Maegar's" training is complete.

"Maestro Janush,
The problem is finally solved, and we have an incident report on all damages sustained by our organization. The company of technomancers and their robotic escort, deployed at your command, have finally eliminated this nuisance.
I regret to inform you that very few of our men have survived the assault. The Myrmidon and lower class robots have been reduced to parts, and only one of our two precious Annihilators is still in service, although heavily damaged and beyond our capabilities to repair.
At least, the case of this "Disaster on Numeria" is finally closed for good, and the complete reports will be sent to you as soon as possible. In the meantime I can shed some light on the main lines of inquiry at play here.
For the moment, this seems to have been the work of a small group of powerful and well organized individuals, referred to as the Five Disasters until further information is recovered:
-One android, unregistered, with four arms and heavily customized cyberware, which is what allowed it to cause such heavy damage with crippling and often fatal explosives. We have not been able to repair it and put it to use, all that we have able to extract is a chunk of strange nanite cloud that settles into a tangible form, and some largely corrupted data. For now, our restoration efforts have only succeeded in extracting a self-identification of "Gears" and several recurring names — "Eloniel", "Sayeh", "Shindra", "Elfrieda", "Maks", "Byllee" and "Sandalee". We are hopeful that the names of the Disasters are among them, as this is the only promising starting point for our investigation.
-What seemed to be a female angel (possessing wings and the powerful holy aura), who greatly delayed the execution of the Disasters through her sustained curative powers. With her support the Disasters seemed to heal faster than they could be damaged, and with each heal one of our men seemed to suffer a backlash and spontaneously combust.
-A female devil or similar beast (horns, tail, small pointed fangs, extremely nimble). She was the last to fall, even though her damage output did not seem to match that of her peers. She seemed untouchable, until the Annihilator obliterated the general region she was last seen in.
-A human female, with very strange powers. Attacking our troops with the combination of a bow and mysterious singing, she seems to have caused sporadic mutations and a burst of aggression in her allies during battle. No traces of her or mutations remained afterwards, though we are still investigating.
-The last case is quite unusual, and resists easy classification. An elven male or possibly half-elf in appearance, he threw himself into the fray drooling with rage and unleashing a storm of steel and lead with a blade and a handgun. Between two assaults, the android scratched him and he changed into a massive six-armed creature made of water – wreaking havoc among our ranks with claws, fangs and weapons. There is clearly still much to investigate.
The aforementioned Disasters seem to be behind the deaths of our agents that lead to the end of our activity at the Scar of the Spider, on the Felldale side, forcing us to return to our headquarters at Starfall.
Their true intentions and the motivation behind their hostilities are still unknown, our teams have always been assaulted without a word.
Despite this hard blow you will be happy to know that our activity in Numeria should have been resumed by the time this message will have reached you.
Kalannah
PS. I attach to this letter a box containing the remains of the android, the nanites take form and fuse, but seem practically inert and unresponsive to our experts and analysis machines. Maybe you can find some use for them."
"Maestro Janush, where are you? We need backup!"
"Maestro Janush?!"
"Maintain order! Watch for looters!"
"Make haste if you can. It's west of here, not far. You can't miss the spot."
"Make ruins of kingdoms. When each is dust, the grains shall gather in this vessel. When a thousand grains are gathered, bring it before us as an offering so that an Eldest may sip from it."
"Make way, make way! All right, what's going on here?"
"Make yourself scarce!"
"Makes sense. Heh, look at this — I look just like one of them nobles! Just yesterday we were tramping through mud, and now we're all dressed up!"
"Manticore gland oil, sir! A wondrous tincture, and much cheaper than a mage's services. Try it — I guarantee you won't regret your purchase!"
"Mary is beautiful, any Nyta is kind. So how can I decide which to buy a goat from?"
"Master protection mode activated."
"Master, do not leave your loyal servants!"
"Master, watch over us!"
"Master... I let you down..."

"Mathian, my beloved brother,
Read this and heed my words: This expedition to Iobaria is the stupidest idea I've ever heard of. This is pure madness. If you are lucky, you'll come back empty-handed, a fool in eyes of all Gralton. But if unlucky, you won't come back at all, leaving your wife a widow, your children orphans, and me — Aroden forbid — the heir and head of our insane family.
I beg you by every god and their mother — forget this expedition of yours! Come home!
Your brother,
Penrod Hanvaki"
"May Calistria bless the King! Temple guard, to battle! For His Highness Irovetti!"
"May Calistria damn Irovetti, the blasphemous usurper! Temple guards, to battle! For {mf|King|Queen} {Name}!"
"May Erastil protect you!"
"May I use your comb?"
"May the Goddess save you!"
"May the blaze of the Hells consume my foes!"
"May the cleansing commence!"
"May the gods bless your rule!"
"May {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} spare me from ever having to make such a choice... But {Name} behaved decently, as a true leader!"
"Maya's Charm" Necklace
"Maybe I should've washed those plums before eating them. Or not even stole them in the first place."
"Maybe I shouldn't have doubted you."
"Maybe we should help you after all?"
"Maybe, maybe not... Let me see your other papers — everything you've got."
"Me be baron, chest be mine! No touching baron's treasure!"
"Me be your friend now! Hail be to baron{mf||ess} and {mf|his|her} goblin friend!"
"Me eat no borba today!"
"Me hungry..."
"Me learn cooking at tavern!"
"Me like it in your kingdom. Good for goblins!"
"Me no hit! Hit others!"
"Me open it for you, Baron Yergrace!"
"Me run tests now!"
"Me too. But there's no helping that now. We'll just have to get drunk for the peace of his soul sometime!"
"Me? Cheating you?"
"Medicine, huh? And were you the one that gave it to him? I'm sure you have a license to sell that, right?"
"Meeting the {mf|king|queen} {mf|him|her}self! What a lucky day!"
"Melianse... What a beautiful name..."
"Melisandra? You are Melisandra Daveon, aren't you?"
"Merciful Sarenrae, heed my prayer… burn my heart, purify me by your fire, save me from evil…"
"Merciful Shelyn, save us!"
"Merciful gods, the baron{mf||ess} is here!"
"Mercy before law."
"Mercy! This is needless cruelty!"
"Mercy, I beg you!"
"Mercy, Lamashtu!"

"Mhm. I see…" {n}The elf furrows his brow in concentration.{/n} "I do not fully understand the laws of these lands… I just want to say I am very glad I met you. And I'm sad that I have to leave. But, if that is what I must do… Farewell, {name}!"
"Mighty army mite go attack!"
"Millennia."
"Mine! All mine!"
"Minstrels will sing about this battle!"
"Miserable scumbag! You rotten, rotten little man!"
"Miss old rattler! Want hear his song once again!"
"Misty chamber in the underground floor... misty chamber in the underground floor... you can get where the final key is stored, from there... oh!"
"Mmm. You're rude..."
"Mmm... Enough traveling and fighting, let's stay here forever!"
"Mmm... Try the eclairs — they're delicious!"
"Mmm? I'm sorry, I got distracted by the reflections playing on the wall. Did you want something?"
"Mmm… You're interested too? I'd never guess!" {n}Octavia laughs seductively.{/n} "I'll think about it. But mind the handle will always stay in my, and only my hands."
"Money first. This ain't a charity."
"Monster! We knew that you would always thirst for blood!"
"Monsters? Again?!"
"More corpses on the floor here! It's not easy to wash out blood, you know..."
"More green cuties? Nice! And you all should stop yelling at Nok-Nok! — Can't you see how hard he's trying to be a good advisor?!"
"More! Give us more! I haven't laughed so hard in a long time!"

"Mortals are stupid, ridiculous and pathetic. This is true for the Skjegge, and for me and you as well. But sometimes a lesson can be learned from their swarming. A shadow of a higher truth in earthly dust."
"Mortals, challenging a fey lord and his godlike powers... Victory seems impossible, and yet we have no choice but to march on."

"Most Honorable {mf|Baron|Baroness} {name}!
This is Maegar Varn, the ruler of the neighboring city of Varnhold, writing. You might remember meeting me at the reception — our encounter had a powerful effect on me. You are a brave warrior and a wise ruler, which is why I hope to enlist your support and, in the future, form a firm friendship. No matter whether the gods or the Swordlords have contributed to us becoming neighbors, I believe that our alliance will be as steadfast as a rock.
To signify the formation of our alliance, I invite you to visit Varnhold and see for yourself that my intentions are good. The city is still young, but we have a lot to show our guests. Our cellars are full of wine barrels, and our storehouses of grain and cheese. It is easy to reach my city: the path to Varnhold lies in the east, past Lake Silverstep, and over the ridge of the Tors of Levenies. Hard to get lost in these parts.
Whether you accept my invitation or not, I ask of you one more thing: consider building a route and developing trade between our lands. I am convinced that both of us would only benefit from this union.
I anxiously await your visit.
Respectfully yours,
Baron Maegar Varn"

"Most Honorable {mf|Baron|Baroness} {name}!
This is your good neighbor Maegar Varn, the ruler of Varnhold, writing. The terrible news that your lands are being swarmed by loathsome monsters has just reached me. Without wishing to cast any doubt on your valor and combat prowess, I nevertheless dare suggest my help in these dark times.
Unfortunately, I cannot lend you my sword: all my warriors are busy protecting our roads — there have just been too many bandits in Dunsward. But as a sign of my utmost respect, I send some valuable resources along with this letter. Let them serve you and your people well in these harsh days.
I am sure that you would do the same in my place and would never leave Varnhold without help. Therefore, do not perceive this as an attempt to indebt you to myself. My help is free — I offer it of my own volition. Baronies like ours need to stick together, in a steadfast alliance. If one falls, the other will follow. Together, we can withstand any menace — even the likes that the Stolen Lands are famed for.
P.S.: I dare not insist, knowing of your hardship, but I do remind you that I would be delighted to welcome you in Varnhold at any time.
Respectfully yours,
Baron Maegar Varn"
"Most disheartening. A new ally stretches out his hand to share his knowledge in friendship, and we push him away. Why?"

"Most honorable {mf|Baron|Baroness} {name}!
I am Baron Maegar Varn of Varnhold, and I am writing to inquire about the current state of affairs in your realm. I hope that no trouble or pestilence have found their way to your lands. Perhaps we could arrange a neighborly meeting soon to discuss things — at your leisure, of course.
I would also like to request your aid in a small matter. A few days back, an adventurer by the name of Willas Gunderson retrieved a mysterious bracelet from one of the ancient ruins scattered across Dunsward. Gunderson kindly turned it over to my court wizard, Cephal, who continues to examine it as it lies on the table before me. It may be the most peculiar thing I have ever laid eyes on. The bracelet is covered in angular patterns that resemble a labyrinth, and it is adorned with an inscription in an unknown language. No learned man in Varnhold has been able to read this writing or deduce which culture the artifact belongs to. So, I ask for your aid: please, if you have an archivist with deep knowledge of the history of this region, send them along to aid us in solving this mystery. I am sure that your capital has plenty of such learned men and women. Perhaps one of them will succeed in reading this inscription. Of course, I will return the VORDAKAI VORDAKAI VORDAKAI VORDA"

"Most wise sovereign of the most thriving kingdom!
I hasten to inform my King that the secret mission with which you graciously entrusted me has reached its destination. This place's name sounds far from the music of heavenly spheres, and never would I dare risk insulting your eyes with the image of ignoble syllables, but for the sake of accuracy, I must inform you of our location. The settlement is called Littletown (and rightly so, I must add).
The inn we have settled in for the night in is located at the edge of the forest. In the morning, feathered minstrels delight my ears and the ears of my less talented brethren in pen and rhyme, and I am imbued with the grace of loyalty to my King. Though, the same cannot be said of some of the above-mentioned brethren, whose unworthy mouths have the audacity to express dissatisfaction with their fate. As for me, if it be the royal will, I would kneel before you and read my most refined sonnet, inspired by the local nature, which I enjoy at your command.
I humbly assure you that my King will never be affected by the shadow of doubt over the fairness of the decision to send your obedient servant on such an important mission, which all of us, by the way — and me most of all — are ready to start immediately!
With my lowest bow to Your Highness,
Trebricent of Cordelon"
"Mother Lamashtu! Accept blood that will be now shed, as sacrifice!"
"Mother of Monsters, give me the strength to free your lands of this filth!"
"Mother, they're protecting all of us. Don't you see?"
"Move away, stringbeans!"
"Move it, lads, ain't worth it".
"Move it, will ya!"
"Must be, real great ancestor send you!"

"My Dear Kennoth Plamer,
With your desire to pursue a new archaeological mission in mind, I spent a few hours in my library today and identified a location worthy of your research. In the northeastern part of the River Kingdoms lies a region called the Stolen Lands. Many antiquities can be found in such places. No doubt an inquisitive researcher would be able to find old coins, significant cultural remnants, and even pieces of artifacts that might be restored. Naturally, you shall require the services of a specialist to evaluate your findings during your travels. I've no doubt of your ability to recruit such a specialist once you arrive in the Stolen Lands. Such contacts can typically be made in large cities or settlements. You would not want your return journey encumbered with items of scant value or interest, after all.
Before you set off, it is my obligation to warn you that this place is untamed and can be perilous. Watch not only for bandits and monsters, but also impassable swamps and dangerous open plains. Should you decide to visit the Stolen Lands, I strongly urge you, Kennoth, to hire a professional guide, and better yet — guards. It is wise to take precautions.
I should appreciate it greatly if you return with a few amusing curiosities for me, as a token of our friendship.
Your true friend,
Agneth Bregan"
"My Dream, my Queen... grant me power!"
"My advisor referred to you as the 'Golden Shields', yet you say 'Golden Shield'. Which one is it?"
"My beautiful fey... How did I live without you?"

"My beloved Callitropsia,
Every day I spend without you seems to drag on forever! The only thing left to do is to think of our coming wedding. Only you know how I long for this day to finally come. Each time I close my eyes, I see us, together. I see happy guests and tables set out for a feast, I smell the fragrance of flowers and fine cuisine, I hear cheerful music, I feel your touch as we whirl in dance. But even these dreams pale in comparison to the mere thought of the eternity we'll spend together. I shall love you forever, even after death, in every life after this one and across all of creation.
Only one thing disturbs my happiness. Do you know that someone tried to interfere with our wedding? My former groom, Dorsy, has talked father into trying to disrupt the ceremony. Picture this: father took it into his head that since he is a headman of our village, he can decide my fate! But don't you worry, my love — their plot has fallen apart. No gods could prevent our union, for a higher force is standing behind us. A few nights ago I dreamt of a mesmerizing maiden, who told me how to free myself out of my father's grip. I did everything as she told — I was so angry with him! Now, of course, I am beset with doubt — was it the right thing to do? Still, I hardly think any of this is more than pure superstition: such silliness cannot change how things are, and I could have dreamt up absolutely anything.
Think nothing of this, my love. Think only of me. I love you.
I cannot wait for our day!
Your Nyta"
"My brother met him once. He was out on patrol, and a group of bandits ambushed them!"
"My brother's just stupid! We're educated frogs, ha ha!"
"My brothers are long gone, but today of all days I miss their advice and support..."
"My cart! It's sinking!"
"My child will live!"

"My darling! I'm writing this while taking a rest stop in the Glenebon wilderness. Don't be surprised, but I finally decided to get out of Pitax. I'll miss the 'magical' potion dear Kharne Vereel sells, but that's fine – I brought a supply of it with me! It'll come in handy when we celebrate our reunion.
As for my homeland... things are getting worse and worse there. Irovetti's appetites grow, the guards are fighting with the thieves' guild, the old Trade Houses keep making new schemes, and even the Academy of the Arts has been said to have some new free-thinkers appearing from time to time. I'm sure that pot will boil over sooner or later, and I'd prefer not to be there when it does. I also look forward to seeing you! In the meantime..."
The letter cuts off here.

"My dear Elga!
I'm sure you don't remember my face, but I hope you do know my name. In case you don't, I'll introduce myself — my name is Settrex. I am your father. I deeply regret that I never had a chance to watch you grow up, that I didn't help you at times of hardship and didn't share your moments of happiness and your sorrows, that you never knew how much I love you. It is unknown to me what Isabel, your mother, has told you about me — whether you ever found out that I'm a satyr, whether you've heard of the extraordinary place you were born or of my fate after your disappearance. In this letter, however, I'll try to tell you everything.
You were born in a village where humans and fey have lived in peace for centuries. We were more than good neighbors – it was a close union. A union so close that fey and humans built families together. Your mother and I fell in love with each other, and you were the fruit of our love — the child of two peoples. There wasn't a single human or fey in the village who didn't like our little Elga. From early on, you knew how to conquer hearts. And I loved you as well — more than anyone else in the world. Every day I would look at you and admire your features, and I would feel like the happiest creature in all of creation.
But my happiness wasn't meant to last. Isabel took you to far-off lands. Why she did this, I do not know. Perhaps, I offended her in some way, or maybe she foresaw the coming disaster. A few months later, a horrid creature attacked the village and razed it to the ground. A lot of fey and humans died, hundreds of houses were laid to waste, and soon those lands were void of life. I looked for both of you for a long, long time, but I never found you. Finally, I had nothing left to do but to return to our ruined home, and live out my days in solitude.
I am grieved that Isabel didn't allow me to be with you, but I'm glad she took you away and saved your life. Nowadays, I'm one of the few who still live in the village ruins, hoping desperately that one day you will return to your homeland. I'm too old and too lonely to leave. If I don't live to see you come back, then this letter will tell you of my fate.
Forgive me, my little girl. I love you.
Settrex, your father."

"My dearest neighbor!
Now I have every right to call you so. Brineheart is located on the riverbank in the southern Kamelands — right near the border of your lands. So you can congratulate me now, my dream has finally come true, and I've become a legitimate ruler of my own little kingdom. I strongly recommend you come and congratulate me in person — for our dearest Linxia will most definitely do the same in the nearest future. And I'd love it so much if all three of us could gather near the fireplace and share the latest gossip over a bottle of good wine. Without you, this gathering would be incomplete.
I'll be happy to cover all your travel expenses.
Your friend,
Darven."

"My dearest sister, do you remember Tiltaren, who these three years ago I had the misfortune of meeting along the pass over the Tors of Levenies? He'd gotten himself into a jam – run straight into a band of thieves that waylaid travelers on mountain roads. His bombs were his only weapon, and he couldn't use them in the snowy mountains without bringing an avalanche down on his own head. By chance I was climbing up the pass from the other side, fleeing a pack of werewolves... and then there was that horrible blizzard... It all ended in quite a mess, ha ha!
Me and an elf, stuck for three days in that cramped cave, afraid to peek out. Bandits and werewolves stalked the blizzard outside. The occasional sharp cry rang out, and then silence fell again. When we finally escaped that stone hole, we were sick enough of each other to say goodbye through gritted teeth, and parted ways silently hoping that we'd never meet again. Well, that hope's been dashed: we managed to run into each other in the middle of some backwater in the Stolen Lands, only to discover that we were on our way to the same place! Someday I will tell you more of our quest, and the manner of our meeting. But know that it began with 'You again!', and in turn we discovered – what a coincidence! – that we'd been having the same dream, sent to us by a dragon. As you know, everything happens... more quickly in parties of adventurers living from one dangerous expedition to the next. It was like that between me and Till too. On the fifth day of our journey, his blank face began to seem sweet, and the jingle-jangle of his alchemist vials grew soothing.
Today is the thirty-seventh evening since we reunited, and we're camping inside the cave where the dragon called us. Today Till gave me a special seashell – a protective charm. He said it will help me survive in the most dangerous places, and that it remembers the last words said at the end of the day. You can hear them when you hold the seashell to your ear.
He gave me this gift, and went out on patrol. It's his turn today. At first I didn't think to listen what the shell had to say; and when I did...
'Marry me.'
I know you'll call me a careless fool, sister dear. But I know what my answer will be.
It's a good thing that Xelliren, the dragon who called us here, is also a priest, though he follows a strange god. You can't have a wedding without a boring speech and a priest's ritual, right?"
"My deepest regards, Your Highness!"
"My dream... I will await your return."
"My family's been thrown out into the streets! My children have to beg on the corners!"
"My farm's a long way from here, and they still got their greedy mitts on it... Had to flee in the night so they wouldn't notice. We left everything, hoping they wouldn't come looking for us..."
"My farm's far from here, and they got their greedy paws on it... Had to escape at night so they wouldn't notice. Left everything, hoping they wouldn't come looking for us!"
"My favorite pastime at parties is to stand silently in the darkest corner, and watch friends and strangers dancing and having fun."
"My flea joke better you!"
"My friends went ahead, but I stayed to chat with the heroes of the Varnling Host. Who would have imagined that you've accomplished so many feats! I hope someone makes a song about you too!"
"My goat is such a dog, he puts the moves on the headman's mare!"

"My goddess sees a darkness upon the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}. Such evil must not cast its shadow on {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}. It must be turned to nothingness, by mercy or deliverance. I am {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae's{/g} warrior, and will do my duty — and then... then I will be returned to her light."
"My goddess, give me strength!"

"My grandfather got obsessed with all the tales about Desna and wished to fly to the moon. I hired two wizards to cast an illusion of a trip to the moon for him. Let the old man have his dream fulfilled. These are his last days, after all."
"My grumpy cousin…"
"My head hurts after last night... someone give me some wine!"
"My lady, I'm the wife of Gurt, who serves as groom for your beloved husband!"
"My lady, there's nothing we can do. The power of those who've hidden Briar exceed our own in many ways."
"My lady, you saved us! Your dear husband forgave my husband's debt over the ruined harness gear. And it was expensive — had brasses and everything!"
"My lady, your order frightens me."
"My lady? I was just going to give it to you..."
"My legs are killing me... when's supper?"
"My life will cost you dearly!"
"My limbs grow cold... Pharasma opens her doors to me, ready to place a laurel on the poet's bloody brow... Oh, cruel fate..."
"My little girl has grown so much..."
"My love! I will devour all your enemies!"
"My love... Why did you leave me...? How could this have happened..."
"My name is Kimo. Kimo Tavon." {n} With a wide smile, the elf slowly nods at you.{/n}

"My name is Xelliren. I am a loyal servant of {g|Apsu}Apsu{/g}. Thousands of years ago, my god appointed me to watch over this place, where deep in the depths there hides a great evil. I knew at once the repulsive smell of the {g|Rovagug}Beast{/g}, but it took me centuries to locate the egg that he left. All this time, I've stood guard here, looking for a way to destroy the Spawn before it hatched and brought immeasurable sufferings to those who dwell upon the land."

"My name, as I mentioned, is Offeld Skjegge. I was once a famous master. The golems I made were unrivaled, either here in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}, or in our homeland, {g|Five Kings Mountains}the Five Kings Mountains{/g}! I created this throne and scepter to control a whole army of golems, ordering them to make more and more new ones... Yes, it was a glorious time..."
"My new toys, you are so much fun! I will toy with you until you break!"
"My nose is itching."
"My patience is at an end. Where's our money?"
"My prayers have been answered! Save us!"
"My protection costs much. But refusing it costs a hundredfold more!"
"My regards, {mf|Baron|Baroness|King|Queen}!"
"My respects, Your Grace!"
"My respects, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."

"My return... was not a gift, but a curse. I became the one I pretended to be. Kobold Tartuk, not gnome Tartuccio. And I ssstarted to forget. Who I was. How I lived. Sssometimes I have pictures in my head. I thought they were visionsss. Until I met you, my executioner."
"My revenge shall make you tremble!"
"My second husband loved hunting. That's how he died: he was chasing a deer, but instead found a bear. Poor soul!"
"My self-assured peacock. Did you think you could hide from me something that used to be a part of me?"
"My service... is over. Farewell, Mother..."
"My sight… My Eye! My gift from the depth of Abaddon! It's gone! Stolen!"

"My sister and I often snuck in to hear these stories, hiding in the shadows just beyond the circle of light and warmth. We are hellspawn, you see. Tieflings are unwelcome guests in {g|Qadira}Qadira{/g}, unblessed by the light of merciful {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g}. We grew up sleeping in a common tent, scavenging food here and there like orphans, all but outcast and disowned. We were thirteen when we left, and set off to find happiness in the cities – and everyone we left behind sighed with relief."

"My sister and I... we are twins, but as different as the sun and moon. Her name is Kanerah, which means 'Silent Flame'. She is fire – a cold fire, but one that turns everything to ash. I am a river. It brings me joy to give water to tired travelers, and nurture green shoots. But when I flood, I am bound to bring death..." {n}The girl's eyes are full of sorrow.{/n} "Despite our differences, we are one. Our lives belong to divine {g|Nethys}Nethys{/g}, and by his mercy we now live... in turns. While one of us is here, the other sleeps in another plane, and when she wakes up, we switch places. Just as you just witnessed..."
"My skylark, your song is sad today. What has happened?"
"My skylark. Your song is so sad today. What troubles you?"
"My son's quick, thinks on his feet — and miners make good money!"
"My songs and ballads are more popular than your money, here!"
"My stomach is on fire! I'm pretty sure the plums are responsible."
"My strength is running out, but I will not die today — no!"
"My subjects! Servants of the Kingdom of the Cleansed! Today is a special day. The day we have long prayed for!"

"My sweet Leksen!
I just received a letter from you and rushed immediately to answer — I want you to get word from me as soon as you arrive in New Stetven. With all these endless travels of yours I've become an expert on roads and settlements myself. Little Ketri asks about his father's whereabouts every night instead of a bedtime story. Then I get a map and show him: here's our Galt, and these are the Stolen Lands, there's Brevoy, and this is the road our father is riding on right now. Then we wish you goodnight and go to sleep.
Everything is all right here. The workers you've hired finally finished painting the walls and fixing the roof. Now sitting at the very top of our house is that marvelous forged weathercock you brought from Numeria. It's perching up there and watching around — what's there behind the horizon? Maybe the master is on his way home?
Ron the Baldhead returned recently — you'd somehow missed each other in Mivon. He told a bunch of tall stories about his adventures, as he usually does. Told us there is a hodag living in the woods in the southern Stolen Lands. I almost fainted on the spot — that's the forest you pass by every time! Maybe Ron just lies — gods know he usually does — but I beg you to take care and choose the other road to skip coming near that damned forest!
I'm writing this now and can't keep my tears from running. I'm just not myself without you. The only joy I have is watching little Ketri. His face and yours are as like as two peas, he even frowns just like you! You always bring me some presents — dresses, or shoes, now this turquoise brooch you promised last time — but I need none of that! The only thing I need is you by my side, safe and sound. Take care of yourself! Be back soon!
Your beloved,
Olika and Ketri"
"My victory was foretold in the stars!"
"My {mf|Baron|Baroness}, I… I just don't know how to thank you!"
"My {mf|king|queen}!"
"My... Head..."
"N-nothing, sir. I was just leaving."
"NO!"
"NOOOOOOO! AAAAAAAHG!"

"Name's Urtenea. I'm an alchemist from Vyre. Irovetti contracted me to work for {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, promised me my own laboratory, access to rare ingredients... The conditions aren't quite what he promised, but it's better than working as an apprentice till my hair goes gray! Do you know how hard it is to save up for your own glassware set?"
"Nay, wasn't nothing, just thought I did. Damned stump!" {n}The man hits the trunk of the tree with his fist, then winces and massages his hand.{/n}

"Neither alive nor dead, but tormented eternally by their worst nightmares, these brave heroes still wander the labyrinth. Find and destroy four of their strongest, and the power of the Beast's madness will weaken. – Then I'll be able to crack open the shell. We must destroy the monster before it hatches and grows strong!"

"Nethys' followers should never condemn achievements in magical research, but I do so wish to find the crafty fool who did this to the trolls. – And tear him apart! Fire-resistant trolls, can you believe it? The very thought insults me!"
"Never back down in the face of danger, {mf|king|queen}! — And we will be happy to help you!"

"Never before have so many troubles beset our lands. Robbers rule the roads. Peasants flee, leaving everything they own behind. And now this terrible sickness: I saw with my own eyes how people got a fever, and then monsters clawed their way out of them. And our most honorable baron{mf||ess} is sitting on {mf|his|her} hands as {mf|he|she} wants nothing to do with this. If this goes on any longer, {mf|he|she}'ll have to collect tax from monsters and robbers, because there will be nobody else left.
Since no one is helping us, neither the gods nor the baron{mf||ess}, I've firmly decided to rescue our lands myself. Destroying all the robbers and monsters is beyond me, but at least I can restore justice.
Yesterday, grandmother Elsa lost her only hen. How did the simple folk deserve all of this? Take Garald, that clueless bully: he's got a full hen house, he always has enough eggs and meat. Is that at all fair? That's why I decided to sneak into Garald's hen house at night and take one of his hens. It won't hurt him. I put the bird in Elsa's hen house, the grandmother will jump of joy in the morning. Garald's hens look nothing like the one Elsa lost, but is that so important? All eggs taste the same. The important thing is that justice has been restored. And our {mf|baron|baroness} can sit in the castle and twirl {mf|his|her} thumbs all {mf|he|she} wants.
I never liked that grumpy Ralph was so prosperous, especially in times as harsh as these. He must have at least 20 heads of cattle. He's gloating in his neighbors misery, glad that their livestock didn't make it back from the pastures, and sells milk to them for an arm and a leg. So I came at night and took his herd to the old hut. There are meadows nearby, they won't starve, and I'll take their milk to the village and give it to those in need. Who knows where I'm getting it?
I successfully hid the herd, but I couldn't find it anywhere the next morning. Well, I did find the horns, skins and tails. Bad luck. Well, at least Ralph isn't having such a good time anymore.
Yesterday, I saw a wonderful stallion on the road, with a rare coat. It was all white, with beautiful spots on its sides and so many shiny badges on its saddle it hurt my eyes! I reckoned, it must be some money bag who stopped to take a leak. I wouldn't have won if I were to fight him, but taking his stallion — sure thing. Untied it, sprung on its back and galloped all the way to the village. I quietly led the stallion into uncle Frey's shed — his old mare might die ploughing the field any day now. Came by to check on him today, and there was nothing but ashes left of his hut, and a lot of horse tracks on the ground around it, as if from a cavalry unit. Odd.
Greedy Rickman has stuffed his barns full of grain and refuses to share it with the needy. At night, I snuck into one of his barns and pulled out a sack of grain. Decided to take it to aunt Lucy.
