The sack was heavy, but my sense of justice gave me strength. I hid the sack in her barn. But come next morning, that damned Rickman went all the way from his barn straight to Lucy's barn, as if by smell, and made an awful scene! The scoundrel.
I am positive that once the peasants find out who's been helping them, they'll write songs about me. But my heart desires even more heroic deeds. I cannot stand watching the people's misery. It is time to give them back their happy lives. Tomorrow I am planning to travel to the hideout of the Stag Lord himself and steal all the treasure he has accrued by robbing poor peasants and refugees from neighboring lands. The truth shall triumph. And after that we'll get to the gold of our baron{mf||ess}. We'll see what {mf|he|she} hides in those coffers."
"Never sure whom to bow to and whom to spit at..."
"Never thought these burrows have chasms like that!"
"Never. It wouldn't be polite to visit Pharasma without bringing some company!"
"New toys to sharpen my talons? At last!"
"Next time you want to throw a party, ask me to arrange it!"
"Next time, things will definitely go as planned!"
"Nice meeting you, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!"
"Nice timing, Your Highness! I don't think we could have defended the trading post without you!"
"Nice wine, nice company... What else could we wish for?"
"Nice! I hope you'll fly away to your goddess now, and stop annoying me with your happy idiot's face, winged boy."
"Nights in Katapesh"
"No can do this!"
"No doubt."
"No forgive! No mercy!"
"No more fight. We tired. We go!"
"No music is more pleasing to a man's ear than the sounds of fierce battle!"
"No need for two-faced hospitality. Toxic intent is no less poisonous when phrased politely."
"No need to thank me. It's not your fault you got sick."
"No one knows! That's why he's got that nickname."
"No one will be left unpunished."
"No one will ever see my tears again. Neither mortals of Golarion, nor the one who cursed me!"
"No one will move while you're looking for evidence. I promise you that."
"No one's coming to help you. No one cares."

"No place to work, no place to sleep... What should I do – live in a forest under a bush? {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, please, build me a workshop. – I promise I'll return the favor!"
"No time to surround them! Attack!"
"No way am I trying this sludge. You're nothing but a charlatan!"

"No way out."
In place of a signature, the note is signed with the image of a comet, curled into a spiral.
"No way!"
"No wonder barely a handful of freaks worship him in all Golarion. What kind of a god sits on his ass in some remote corner of the universe? Gorum's much better! His children bring thunder and fun!"
"No worries. I ain't superstitious. Just gotta think on your feet, that's all. Look at these two — they weren't paying attention, and now they're dead."

"No! I must not doubt! I must be strong in my faith. Father! I do not sit here in vain, do I? I am fulfilling your will, am I not? I beg you! Send me a sign!" {n}The dragon's eyes search the sky. His words sound like thunder, and pound on the rocks... And fade into a depressing silence.{/n}
"No! Please help!"
"No! Please!"
"No! That's her! She's found us!"
"No! That's the monster and her henchmen!"
"No! These are new strangers!"
"No! Wait! I know!"
"No! Whoever you are, leave the poor thing alone!"
"No! {name} is a hero, and so I am. Am I. Me. Hero! And I will stop you."
"No, Kimo… it was a joke."
"No, Your Grace! Stop!"
"No, but… Well, he… To hells with you and your babble! Ugh! No sense arguing with a cleric!"
"No, his arrows strike their pride, not their hearts. A while back, the judge's wife got a note from a secret well-wisher telling her she should go out for dinner at a local tavern."
"No, just look at her! Walking around the enemy's lair, enjoying the scenery!"
"No, let him go. I'll make sure this wimp doesn't cause any more trouble!"
"No, no resurrection for him. I won't forgive Lander for his betrayal. Let him stay dead."
"No, no, let them boil a bit more!"
"No, no, no. Engelidis, my love... Don't!"
"No, no. Don't judge us so hastily... We're already..."
"No, none of that! We're not beggars, and we're not out for charity!" {n}The barbarian woman forces several coins into your hand.{/n}
"No, not work. Wits spill out. No can pick up. We examine."
"No, of course not! I'm a patriot! I wholeheartedly support our government! Please don't hurt my children!"
"No, there is no need to be afraid of my Octavia's jealousy. But beware of her tenderness! Ha, ha... Not every one can handle her!"
"No, this is not the end. We have to believe! We will open this door!"

"No, we can't. They happen at random, most often while we're sleeping, but sometimes in broad daylight. That's why we can never stay in one place for long. When someone witnesses us switch, we usually tell them tales of 'a special magical way of traveling', but people start noticing strange things and begin to figure things out. Truth be told, I'm so tired of having to pretend. We knew this couldn't last forever, and now the truth is finally out. Ah, what's the point in all this..."
"No. I refuse."
"No. I've had enough of following you like a dog. I'm here for blood, Stag Lord. One of us won't see the end of this day!"
"No. Pass-word?"
"No. You shall not touch her."
"No. You're on your own."
"No? Then get lost, you panhandlers!"
"Nobody else is guilty here. I accept full responsibility for what has happened."
"Nobody made me leave." {n}Kimo glances at you sideways.{/n} "I just woke up one day, looked out the window... and the road called. And I went."
"Nok-Nok be beating up! This place, he know! Now the others smash-to-bits!"
"Nok-Nok be great hero!"
"Nok-Nok be true Hero!"
"Nok-Nok new King!"
"Nok-Nok no hero! Can't protect Lamashtu shrines!"
"Nok-Nok our hero! And you — you make good sidekick!"
"Nok-Nok! Nok-Nok! Nok-Nok!"
"Nok-Nok... today... you perish..."
"Nok-Nok...?"
"Nok... Nok-Nok."

"None can challenge his charm or wisdom,
The Sage of Pitax should rule this kingdom!"

"None can rival his wit or might!
King Irovetti shall end our plight!"
"None of which include sorting out your petty problems!"
"Nonsense! How does such daubery compare to the complexity of chess? To the energy of tag?"
"Normal cyclopes weren't enough, no, now we have zombie cyclopes, too! What's next? Ghost cyclopes? Maybe vampire cyclopes?"
"Northern architecture is beautiful, but very heavy. In my native land of Qadira, palaces are furnished quite differently..."
"Not a chance. In fact, my brother just shook his hand and thanked him!"
"Not even departed, and we already won our first battle! Seems like a good omen, right?"
"Not even one monster! They fear us and run!"
"Not every man could accomplish such a feat!"
"Not from these parts, huh? He's a local hero! Protector of the people."
"Not here, you stupid animal! Take your muzzle off me!"
"Not in body, of course. But I felt her presence — she was near, and her divine aura protected me."
"Not kids. Trolls. Monsters," {n}Ekun objects through the clenched teeth, without putting the bow down.{/n}
"Not the kind of battle I'm accustomed to, but it could be worse."
"Not to mention the ones who get thrown out before they're even seen, just because they smell? Did you know that, Mr. 'unlicensed medicinal trade'?"
"Not yet, but if nothing's done, they're on track to have a civil war on their hands soon."
"Not your son!"
"Not your toy!"
"Nothing but your husband's life. What's worth more to you?"
"Nothing gets him!"
"Nothing here is what it seems! You see those vases? They look suspicious – like they're watching us!"
"Nothing here," {n}the villager says, perplexed.{/n} "What happened? Did the bard lie to us?"
"Nothing to report, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. A pity."
"Nothing's left. Agai's going to get mad."
"Now I bid you to leave me. I need to perform some rather... unattractive procedures."
"Now I would like to introduce my right hand – a hero without whose help I wouldn't be standing here now. {Name}, please, step forward!"
"Now easy to breath, like air cleans from smoke!"
"Now is the best time to surprise them. Onwards!"
"Now she demands another sacrifice."
"Now that's a downpour!"
"Now that's what I call revelry!"
"Now they want to know how I plan to dispose of all the manure the stables are expected to produce!"
"Now we look like rich losers. – The perfect victim. Now all our other neighbors will want to sink their teeth into us. You shouldn't make your own weaknesses so obvious to others."
"Now we're afraid of nothing! Look out, Lantern King..."
"Now what should I do with you, friends of the betrayer? You've outlived your usefulness. Neither {mf|he|she} nor I have any need of you."
"Now you turn... GRRRAARGH!"
"Now, let's try this again. Where's our money?"
"Now, now, child..." {n}Bartholomew answers slowly.{/n} "I would never do anything like this with humans. This is a troll. A mindless man-eater. Your company kills them in the dozens."
"Now, where is the cyclopes king? Maybe over there? Or right here? Or maybe he doesn't exist at all!"
"Now... Continue the battle. Armag must leave... No one dares object! It's important — the most important thing in the world!"
"Nuisssanssse. Bad ssshaman. I sorrow."

"Numbers will help you on your way,
One of them is fifth in ten,
It will be easy to find if you read
Who opened the road for the ancient dead man
And his black-feathered messenger.
The second is a dozen times in a dozen
And is thrice the number of those who lost their faces.
Don't try to guess it now – it's not yet time.
Wait until he who is born twice,
Will twice be defeated.
Put the two numbers together.
When the Moon leaves her path,
Near the waters of the {g|Candlemere}Candlemere{/g}
Find the one who will open the secret."
"Numerous books around, and very few people. That's what I call a perfect job!"
"Nunuk the hunter told me that he saw an incredibly beautiful flower growing in the swamp! I would go and pick it myself, but I fear I would become lost. Also, there are monsters there..."
"Nunuk the hunter told me that he saw an incredibly beautiful flower growing in the swamp! I'd go and pick it myself, but I'm afraid I'd get lost... And there are monsters there…"

"Nwan Quant peeped through a slit in the window shutter. The visitor was staggering at the porch. Nwan had promised himself many centuries ago that he'd never have to deal with halflings again, after the case of the Clockwork Head. Even the Bleaching is better than some adventures!
However, there was something disturbing in the visitor's appearance. Something was wrong.
– What do you say, Kexy?
His assistant sat at the next window with yarn and knitting needles in her hands.
– Look at his clothes. They're second-hand. He's a hobo.
– He is, but you're not quite right. Look at his feet.
Kexy looked, trying to make out at least something in faint light of the lantern above the door.
– Are those... he was shackled?
Rather than answering, the gnome stepped toward the door.
– We shall need a doctor.
As if to prove his words, the guest faltered and collapsed onto the knees, and fell head first onto the doorstep."
"Nyrissa is no more. Your dusty Eldest is no more."

"Nyrissa knows that you are here. It was she who made you leave the portal last. She has taken your companions. And not only them, but everyone she thought was connected to you, those she could reach. Nyrissa has a... peculiar sense of justice, if you can call it that. You've taken so many toys from her — her 'skylark', me, Armag, Irovetti... And now she's taken your toys."

"Nyrissa knows you are here. And she has gathered many — ones she thought were connected to you, those she could reach. All your companions are here — there, inside, trapped by her spell. She seems to enjoy taking from others something that is useful or precious to them..."

"Nyrissa!" The ghost snarled, and if we didn't already know he was a ghost, we would have then, his face contorting in ways that would have broken a real elf's skull. Behind him, the fog swirled, forming an image of a beautiful elven city. He jabbed a finger at it. "Look! See my kingdom? See what she destroyed? All of it, gone! And why? Just to add one more grain of dust to the Nymph Queen's chalice!" He shrieked, a sound full of madness and sorrow that seemed to stab through our ears and into our brains. "And now she binds me here, as a bauble for her servants to squabble over!"
So then we...
"O Sarenrae, give me the strength to overcome evil. Give me the fire to burn the disgusting undead, servant of the fallen goddess!"
"O lovely followers of Abadar... when I was a thousand years younger, your souls were like a tempting dessert to me."
"O, mASTer! tHAnk yOU for The prECIOUS Gift of maDNESs!!!"
"Oblivion and d-death... unconsciousness and... al-co-holic lethargy. Is it not all the same?"
"Oblivion awaitsss... Jaethal..."

"Octavia and I are connected, and this connection cannot be broken. We grew into each other, you know? Jealousy is for weak cowards, who don't trust each other and are scared of being tricked. If a night on the side threatens your love – that just means there was no real love there to begin with!"
"Octavia's right, Reg. Leave him be."
"Octavia, my dear child, don't! Aaaah!"
"Octavia, you should be ashamed! You're out of line!"
"Odd business, trying to intimidate a troll. We ARE food for them. Imagine if something you eat, let's say a chicken, attempted to intimidate you. Would you take its threats seriously?"
"Of Transmutations and Bodily Poisons", Part I
"Of Transmutations and Bodily Poisons", Part II
"Of Transmutations and Bodily Poisons", Part III

"Of course I warned against pirates," {n}Judge Celvoway responds indignantly.{/n} "King Irovetti's soldiers patrol our territory to ensure the safety of all, yet there are those who would exploit the River Freedoms to attack our merchants." {n}He looks at you for a moment before turning to crowd.{/n} "Clearly, our king was right to worry about foreign powers preying upon our people!"
"Of course! I'll remember that place till the day I die!"
"Of course! It's more fun when there are three of us!"
"Of course! My table is set for everyone! Eat and rest as much as you like. Down below, in the darkness, you will have to be at your best."
"Of course, I'm ready and willing to cover all the expenses for Kyt's education — in return for ensuring that Ronald will be under the watchful eye of an older peer."
"Of course, my illusions are the art of the highest order. Those cyclopes... Oh, I do love them so much!"
"Of course, please ask! I'd be happy to chat all day!"
"Of course, they took our cattle, but the house still stood! I guess they gave up on it — too far from the Stag Lord's fort!"

"Of course. But forgive me, my treasures are not endless, and I cannot provide you with free supplies. If you require the aid of a priest, select a scroll, and I will read it for you. But be careful. – Down in the labyrinth, you're on your own! Do not go into the depths without a servant to the higher forces in your party!"
"Of course. Here you are. Is something going on?"
"Of course. I will help you in any way I can."
"Of course. If the merchants learn that some rascal is planning to cause trouble, the guards will be informed of it right away."
"Oh damn, we're busted. Let's put 'em down! – We'll bury the bodies in the swamp."
"Oh gods... I should have stayed out of this battle..."
"Oh mighty beast! Deadly be your poison!"
"Oh mighty beast! Sharp be your claws!"
"Oh mighty beast! Strong be your wings!"
"Oh no, not another Jubilost joke!"
"Oh no..."

"Oh really? So she sacrificed both her life and her soul for her friends? She compelled an evil goddess to perform a good deed, but in return submitted herself to the power of evil?" {n}The dragon shakes his scaly head.{/n} "Oh, mortals... your lives are ephemeral, but capable of holding such nobleness that is hardly imaginable to transcendent beings."
"Oh yes, the time has come. The time of fate and curses."
"Oh! Of course, I..."
"Oh, Goddess, cleanse me in a righteous death!"
"Oh, I can imagine what the servants will be whispering after tonight!"
"Oh, I don't think that will work. We risk breeding an arrogant lot. They'll consider the power they hold over other people's lives some kind of birth right..."
"Oh, I just thought of something..."
"Oh, I love this tune! Linzi plays so well!"
"Oh, I see! Rest assured, the merchants of the neighboring lands will be green with envy. We will spread the greater glory of your name from here to {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}!"
"Oh, I was long gone. See, that night I collected all the loot — and their weapons and money."

"Oh, I was taught magic by Janush of {g|Starfall}Starfall{/g}, one of the most famous wizards in {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}. 'Maestro' Janush as he insisted on calling himself." {n}Octavia's voice overflows with contemptuous sarcasm.{/n} "Anyone would be happy to learn from such a great master, and only a talentless bitch like me would dare to reject his teachings and indulge in her laziness."
"Oh, I'll be happy to spend some time with you, Restov bootlicker. I'll even make some time for your funeral."

"Oh, Waine... Frankly, I wonder what was going on in his brain that he'd just rush into the forest, being perfectly aware of the danger. Obviously, if you hadn't rescued him, I would... just a bit later. After he'd learned his lesson."
"Oh, brotherhood, sure. Got nothing better to do than prowl the wilds, huh? Could've had a normal life, earning your bread with honest work like us!"
"Oh, come on! What happened next?"
"Oh, dear... I must have put something heavy on it."
"Oh, dear... This is going to take a while..."
"Oh, gods... I'm so happy to see my daughter again!"
"Oh, great. Now we're gonna get drenched."
"Oh, hello, Your-r-r — Hic! — ...ness..."
"Oh, it's you! So, how are those ugly things enjoying their cave? Is it cozy?"
"Oh, it's you! What an honor!"
"Oh, it's you! You remember good old Dovan, don't you? Spared my life back at the Stag Lord's place... but I won't be making the same mistake! Ha ha ha!"
"Oh, it's you!"
"Oh, look — {race}!"
"Oh, my dear boy..."
"Oh, my poor heart can't take it anymore... Run home, you fool. I'm going to the captain of the guard to beg on your behalf."
"Oh, no, no! Not my daughter!"
"Oh, no... Is everyone dead?"
"Oh, oh, oh! They raised the alarm! It's starting!"
"Oh, right! I can't remember his name..."
"Oh, screw you...."

"Oh, she's not bad, all right. But would ya even know what to do with her? It's all ya can do to lay with me once a week, and I barely get a yawn in before ya finish. I doubt ya could sit the saddle to ride her kind."
"Oh, sure, you do what you want — unless you want to say some choice words to that wretch who bosses you around!"
"Oh, thank you my lady! Thank you so much! Is there anything I can do for you? Please, I want to thank your family, any way I can!"

"Oh, that is the saddest and scariest part. The Spawn of the {g|Rovagug}Beast{/g} feeds on nightmares, and its very shell is made of madness. The caves around are filled with insanity. It has flooded them with an ocean of darkness, which distorts the very nature of the multiverse. Heroes who approach grow mad or perish in great suffering... This gives the egg its strength: the monster feeds on their terror and pain."
"Oh, that was YOUR miserable hut that went up in flames the other day?"
"Oh, that's all nonsense. Well, except for the part about breathing fire. All barons can breathe fire, trust me."
"Oh, the rulers of the mortal realms are so smug and careless!"
"Oh, these young heroes... Such bravery, such spirit! Why, I remember when I was your age..."
"Oh, we tore my shirt again... Enough is enough — it's not funny any more!"
"Oh, we'll straighten out, don't you worry! We'll turn a new leaf for sure!" {n}The bandit leader smiles, his blackened teeth showing behind his beard.{/n}
"Oh, yes, my love... I won't let anyone harm you. Anyone!"

"Oh, yes. I'm quite proud of that one, actually. You see, trolls rarely perish in traps. If they manage to break free from one, their animal cunning usually helps them avoid further traps. But that rock troll was trapped just before dawn, so he had no way to avoid the sunrise. Now he just stands there, serving as a demonstration of sorts... It's useful both for my research and as a ward against unwelcome guests."
"Oh, you contemptuous little thing. You cannot stop me — but if you truly are a hero come to challenge me, then you may join the others who came before — in death."
"Oh, you do have so much faith! Too bad you don't have the brains to match!"

"Oh, you think you're smart? I suppose those fellows must have been geniuses to trick a smart guy like you! Or maybe you're not that smart, and you're just being disrespectful. Do I need to call the guards?"
"Oh. He really vanished! Hooray!"
"Oh. Is that a scratch on your neck? Forgive me! I'll be more careful!"
"Oh. Oh. I am unused to lies, they are just wrong. But yes, I knew it was a secret, we all did — yes?"

"Prologue
Numeria is a stern land in northwestern Avistan, full of unsolved mysteries. It's a fruitless wasteland, almost untouched by civilization, but it's not without a particular somber beauty. Throughout these lands in which only the strongest survive, cold rivers rush from the north to the south, veritable arteries of water for several nomadic tribes, and at the northeastern border, the waters of the Lake of Mists and Veils sparkle.
Numeria is encompassed by dangerous regions. Ustalav lies to the west, swarming with undead; the black Worldwound lies to the north, filled with demons; and the endless internal wars of the River Kingdoms seethe to the east. The noble families of Brevoy and the daring defenders of Mendev would give a much to be rid of their Kellid neighbors. You, dear reader, can learn about these various lands and regions from other scientific works — on these pages, I will teach you about Numeria. Let us begin our journey with its greatest legends.
Starfall
Barbarians have lived in the territory of Numeria dating back to ancient times, long before it received its name — even before the dwarves' Quest for Sky. From generation to generation, the legend of Starfall has passed down among the Kellids — an immense calamity that struck Golarion in the distant past. Their oral traditions brought us vivid descriptions of this catastrophe. One night, a huge flaming ball appeared in the sky, radiating waves of heat as it plummeted toward the ground. On the way, it split into many fragments that fell across various areas of Numeria, wreaking terror and destruction. The largest fragment that fell kicked up a huge cloud of dust and dirt when it hit. Once the cloud settled, the surviving nomads saw a huge, strange mountain in the impact zone. A city later grew near it, eventually becoming the country's capital. It was named Starfall in commemoration the legendary event. The Silver Mountain itself became sacred to the Kellids, and to this day scientists and explorers are entranced by the mystery of its origin, not to mention the secrets stored inside.
The Great Warlord Armag
Among the ancient Kellid barbarians, there lived a warlord named Armag, unmatched in battle. A huge tribe known as the Tiger Lords followed him, defeating any enemies the encountered along their way. Like a ruthless force of nature, this horde crossed Numeria, bringing war to the south and the east in regions such as Rostland and Iobaria. The power and valor of Armag were so great that mighty Gorum, the god of war himself, bestowed the hero with his attention and benevolence. But the pride of the great warlord failed him: blinded by victories, Armag said he would live forever and death itself had no power over him. The boast reached Pharasma, the goddess of birth and death, who deemed it an insult. She sent her servants to help Armag's mortal adversaries accomplish a single goal — kill the impudent man and send his soul to Pharasma's Boneyard. Becoming a pawn in the feud between Gorum and Pharasma, Armag fought to his last drop of blood, but he fell while battling a great red dragon. His soul still didn't go to the Boneyard, however — Gorum took it and fused it into Armag's own sword. That is how Armag's boast came true: his soul never left this world, and the fame of his victories endured throughout the ages, making the Tiger Lord's name immortal.
Armag, defeated only by the goddess Pharasma, plays a special role in the myths of Numerian barbarians. According to legends, Armag's sword has great power, and he who finds it will bring the world to its knees. Not only Numerian priests, but historians from all over the world argue over exactly where his remains and his soul, trapped in steel, rest. According to stories and research, Armag's tomb is hidden somewhere in Numeria or the adjacent lands — an unassailable crypt guarded not only by barbarians, but by myriad traps and even immortal guardians placed there by Gorum himself. The tomb has been sought by many honored scientists, such as Curtis Corvarraum and Tonahold Arintan, but their findings didn't provide any exact locations. Ancient chronicles describe a place between two dried rivers; the Silver Mount and the bed of the Sellen River are named among possible matching locations.
You can learn more about these famous explorers' expeditions and where they think the grave is hidden in the extensive and comprehensive works of Corvarraum, Arintan, and their colleagues — "The Legend of Armag," "Lost Artifacts of Avistan," and "The History of Numerian Barbarian Tribes."

"So, this is it. The magic chunk of wood that N. needs so much. Out of everyone I sent to procure it, that lame Tartuccio was the one to get lucky. The rascal politely died, sparing me the need of paying... But to hells with him. This odd piece of wood is what's important. E. said it was called 'Briar'. What's so special about it? Why's it so important for N. – and more importantly, what's in it for me?
***
Started with the basics: tried to examine the piece of wood using magical detection. Simple, right? My eyes nearly popped out. This thing has a stunning aura. It's a major artifact – maybe even belonged to one of the gods. Or an Eldest perhaps? N. is a fey – probably swiped it from someone in the First World. Congratulations, Irovetti, you've hit the jackpot! Just figure out fast what to do with it, before they take it away!
***
Artifacts, especially major ones, are deceptive. Hold it by the wrong end, and a shitbucket of curses will shower down upon you. So before experimenting with it myself, I gave it to my Engie-girl and told her to poke Drelev with it. Nobody's ransom for him, and he's too proud to either serve me or warm my bed – so let him be a test subject. It ended badly – the poor fellow lost his mind. Well… That's a result too!
***
Engie-girl is like a totally different creature. She used to hiss at me and threaten to bite something off unless I soothed her with a few spells. And now she coaxes me, assumes the most seductive poses, whispers tender things. She's fallen in love with me head over heels, and I haven't used any spells on her for days! Looks like I somehow activated the wooden thing's witchery… But how? Why wasn't it Drelev who fell in love with her, but she with me? I need to continue these experiments...
***
I've got it! Touching the Briar causes the subject to fall in love with its owner – that's me! Drelev's insanity doesn't fit into this, but we'll deal with that later. As for now, I should try this artifact on… Hmm, whom? There are so many opportunities – I don't know where to begin!
***
I used the Briar on A. B. – I couldn't lure that column of ice into bed without divine intervention! At first I thought she went mad too. That foolish woman started screaming, throwing plates, splashed wine on me – acting more like a stallkeeper than a bard! But in a couple days my people reported that she came to her senses – and was seeking revenge! Ha, ha, ha. But still, what does it mean? How does this Briar work? There must be some purpose!
***
I tested it on I. N. – same result, an ugly tantrum out of the blue. Ha, Irovetti! You have everything – talent, wealth, power, but no luck in love – none whatsoever!
***
Fun is fun, but I need to do something with the Briar, and soon. If N. finds out I've been hiding her toy all this time, I'll be in trouble. But what tragic comedy. – I hold this incredible power in my hands, but don't have the key to use it! And I've no one to ask for advice – there's not a single intelligent spellcaster nearby. I should have opened a school of magic instead of an Academy of Grand Arts!"

"That Armag! Son of a witch!"

"That arrogant dwarf is going to train our soldiers?! I wonder what he can offer them! Real battle isn't a time to show off, and I've never seen a Kurgess priest on a battlefield. I've never heard anything of their victories, either."

"That bard was too generous. If it was me, I'd have thrown them in the debt-pen, but I would have managed ten gold at least." {n}Jubilost turns his gaze to you.{/n} "Wait, don't tell me you believe this wash about a hidden treasure?"
"That damned ghost sent its monsters again!"
"That doesn't concern me, but since this is so important to you — Bartholomew, I order you to free the troll and cease your experiments."
"That is exactly why I am the Honest Guy, and not you!"

"That is most generous. But we should focus on the murdered caravan escort, who will never need gold again, rather than consoling the merchant for his lost goods. We need to capture those cutthroats!"
"That is precisely why I am here."
"That is... that's not what I meant..."
"That lout insulted my mother!"
"That one, with the mop of red hair, see? He takin' others' tools!"
"That so? If anyone's gonna be pushing up daisies, it won't be me!" {n}Kressle sets her stance and attacks.{/n}
"That so? Seems our friend here wants to play a game with fate."
"That sounds awful. Please accept my condolences and sympathy."
"That sounds horrible! How could you even think-"
"That was a sound decision. Sometimes one must act at one's own risk and peril. Until crossing the boundaries of what is allowed, showing initiative is no crime."
"That was smart, what Hargulka did! Only true king can do!"
"That was you, sweetheart. You said in the job description, and I quote, 'No witnesses.'"
"That will be all. Thank you, Roham."
"That won't help. We are bleaching on the inside, not the outside."
"That'll teach you!"
"That's a crazy idea. When your new 'soldiers' get homesick enough to put you on the rack, don't cry for my help."
"That's a ridiculously low price for a piece like this! It's dwarven made, you know! My grandfather used to wear it!"
"That's a strange thing to say! But it's true, in times like these, all our neighbors envy us. Don't you worry. If any trouble stirs up, your guards will be the first to know!"
"That's a very wise demand! An educated youth could come in handy, especially now that trade in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} is flourishing!"

"That's actually what I wanted to talk to you about. Kanerah was supposed to tell you of an ancient treasury that we've been looking for. Gold isn't the only thing of value in this place. It may contain an ancient relic, taken by the {g|Taldor}Taldan{/g} raiders from a respected Qadiran temple of Nethys."

"That's because you're smart, Your Highness. First, our 'toys' are far safer, and their failure far less dangerous than magic cast awry. Secondly, anyone with an eye and two hands can use our weapons. That makes things a bit simpler for you, doesn't it?"
"That's disgusting!"
"That's exactly what I need. He wanted to see kingdoms in ruins? He will!"
"That's exactly what everyone always says. Every prisoner says they're innocent if you ask them."
"That's great! These mites are worthy folk! I wouldn't risk eating their delicacies, though, heh."
"That's his lunch? Good borba, must be tasty... Can I have a bite?!"
"That's insane! I won't let you kill them, brother!"
"That's it! Only trolls will rule this lands! Death to kobolds! Death to borba!"
"That's it! Trial done! Now no one dares say Amiri is weak!" {n}She grins complacenly and thrusts her chest out.{/n}
"That's it. Time to count our losses, I suppose."
"That's it... I have enough trouble already."
"That's more like it."
"That's none of my concern. It looks broken. Can't give you a coin more."
"That's not mine! You planted it on me! This is a blatant abuse of power!"
"That's not the way I wanted to get to the First World..."
"That's right! This is how we deal with the Stag Lord's bandits!"
"That's robbery!"
"That's the alarm! Close ranks — we're in for a tough battle!"
"That's the law."
"That's the spirit of a true soldier. Allow me to fight by your side!"
"That's the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}! The Maestro promised a reward for {mf|his|her} head!"
"That's what they all say, citizen. Looks like we're going to have to have a little chat about loyalty and patriotism after all."
"That… that's the secret!" {n}After some hesitation, the elf decides to add,{/n} "But it's not hard. Not at all! You have my word."
"The Academy of Infamy"
"The Adventures of Captain Ellena: In Search of the Cyclops Lord's Scepter"
"The Baron himself – and his comrades! I never thought I'd meet someone so important."
"The Book of Bitterness"
"The Book of Blind Revenge"
"The Book of Joyless Triumph"
"The Book of Never Saying Goodbye"
"The Book of Nourishing Rage"
"The Book of Shackles"
"The Book of the Journey"
"The Book of the New Beginning"
"The Captor is the greatest wizard I ever managed to talk into visiting this gloomy place. I had high hopes for him, and so I turned a blind eye to the darkness in his soul."
"The Categories of Space and Time in the Classical Numerian Saga"
"The Chains of Conscience: Memoirs of Those Arrested for Sedition"

"The Codex"
This mysterious book, written in an unknown language, is thought to be the codex of some secret society. The abbreviation "RPG" on its cover does nothing to illuminate this mystery.
"The Complete Collection of Useless Writings"
"The Curse of Ancient Iobaria" by Hastef Umme

"The End Times are nigh."
— Harrim
"The Fallen Priestess. The Weary Traveler. The Wicked Chanter. The Captor and his horrifying slave. Deliver them into peace, and the path to the enemy will be opened!"
"The First Crown has been broken. You do know who was confined inside? The spirit of the first ruler whose kingdom Nyrissa ruined."
"The First Crown is mine! Nyrissa gave it to me!"
"The First Faithful abandoned us!"
"The First Faithful is dead! Run!"
"The Flower contains immense power — power from which immense evil can be born. Monsters, erupting on Golarion by the hundreds... in a crowded street, a busy tavern, near a baby's crib…"
"The Generous Patron of Arts." A play in 2 acts.
"The Great Debates" by Veylira Illio
"The Great Patron"
"The Hellknights are scary. What if they found out... Oh, uh, never mind!"
"The Kingdom of the Cleansed grants salvation!"

"The Koloran Empire once encompassed all of Casmaron, and its influence even spread to the neighboring lands of Avistan and Garund. This vast territory was inhabited by a multitude of wild tribes, all of which lived in the shadow of the great cyclopean civilization. Even at that time the human tribes tried to forge alliances, settle new lands and build large settlements. However, this growth was stunted by the aggressive Koloran overlords and their ever increasing demand for new slaves. The clash of these two cultures gave birth to legends and myths, one of which tells of a great warrior who challenged the opressors. The unnamed hero united the tribes and led an uprising. Many took up arms and followed him into battle. Alas, the fight was uneven, and human armies suffered a crushing defeat. Since humans did not disappear without trace from Casmaron, Avistan and Garund, it is evident that cyclopes decided against wiping out the whole race for its defiance. Nevertheless, the casualties were enormous, as evidenced by archaeological finds related to this dark period in history. According to legend, cyclopes even succeeded in capturing the leader of the rebellion, and he met "a fate worse then death". What exactly happened to him, what punishment he faced for his bold challenge, remains unknown. The dream of the unnamed warrior — the destruction of the cyclopean civilization — came true during the Earthfall. The cataclysm allowed the human civilization to rise out of the dust. Soon, the younger races forged new great empires, but the memory of proud cyclopean cities of Koloran survived through the ages."

"The Labyrinth tricked Tioko's mind, and stole from her Desna's protections. When next her reason failed, she returned to Lamashtu, and sacrificed her friends to her cruel mistress, one by one. Ever since, she has lurked in the depths, seeking new gifts for her mistress. Alas, the last embers of good in her soul have long faded. She has become a monster. The Beast has consumed her utterly."

"The Lady of Graves", "Mother of Souls", "Gray Lady", Pharasma is the goddess of birth, death, and prophecy. She shepherds Golarion's recently departed souls to their final reward. Upon death, souls migrate via the River of Souls to Pharasma's Boneyard in the Outer Sphere, which sits atop an impossibly tall spire that pierces the Astral Plane. She is among the most ancient deities in the multiverse, but keeps her knowledge of the fate of all souls closely guarded.

"The Lady of Graves", "Mother of Souls", "Gray Lady", Pharasma is the goddess of birth, death, and prophecy. She shepherds Golarion's recently departed souls to their final reward. Upon death, souls migrate via the River of Souls to Pharasma's Boneyard in the Outer Sphere, which sits atop an impossibly tall spire that pierces the Astral Plane. Domains: Death, Healing, Knowledge, Repose, Water.
Favored Weapon: Dagger
"The Lantern King. He failed to trick me, but he managed to cast me into the depths of the First World. It's not so easy to find one's way out."
"The Legend of the Pathfinder" by Aren Roarvie
"The Lyre and the Sword: An Anthology of Heroic Pitaxian Poetry"

"The Master of Death will call out those who are buried under his feet. Those who rejected Vordakai will become servants to Him. Great Vordakai will unite sworn enemies with a common after-life goal — implementing His will."

"The Master would be angry if we reached out for his gift before the time was right. Even if we reached the tomb, its doors would be closed to us. This staff is the key. It has slumbered for ages, but now..." {n}The tiefling shows you his staff, crowned with a metal skull. A greenish flame dances in the single eye socket.{/n} "The dead eye has opened, the dead fingers move. The gift awaits the worthy!"
"The Nomen tribe is with you, people of Varnhold!"
"The Notes of a Traveling Priest: Ilthuliak" by Tyrin Dean
"The Path of Splendid Glory"
"The River Blades are at your service, Your Highness!"
"The River Freedoms"
"The River Kiravoy — it flows down the mountains and north, all the way to Brevoy."
"The Savored Sting will execute you!"
"The Sisters put a spell on Armag to doom us all!"
"The Sisters who went to the hills in search of truth {d|c31 Tomb Murder}never returned{/d}. They perished, and {mf|he|she} is the killer!" {n}The woman points a trembling finger at you.{/n}
"The Six Bears never give up!"
"The Stag Lord has nothing on this bastard! Razed whole towns to the ground, killed hundreds of folks! They even say he once scooped one poor sod's eyes out with a spoon. A handsome story, eh?"

"The Stolen Lands are a region located between Brevoy and the River Kingdoms, a realm so disgusting that it makes both its neighbors look almost cozy. Miles and miles of impassable woods, putrid swamps, muddy lakes and barren wastes, infested by various monsters and bandits — this so-called "treasure" is still contested only because neither of its neighboring countries wishes to concede before its rival. For the last several years, the Restov Swordlords have been promising the title of Baron to any person who proves capable of curbing the chaos of this patch of land. One by one, adventurers and knights of fortune have gone there in search of action, and must have found more than they expected, for no one has returned. Recently, though, one of those challengers managed to succeed, and received the grand prize. And since {mf|His|Her} Grace has promised me a session of decapitation for backbiting, I'm going to remain positive in my review from now on.
The newly-made Baron{mf||ess} of the Stolen Lands has managed to resolve the issue of banditry in {mf|his|her} domain completely — now if a traveler encounters a group of people with sharp swords and earnest faces, they may be sure that these are not just mere robbers, but rightful law enforcers. Though "the road" is a hyperbolic definition, of course: except for an overgrown and ancient dwarven tract, there are no other roads here. The brave traveler who comes here submerges knee-deep in their first steps into a marvelous world of local wild nature and gets a refreshing mud bath. And next comes acquaintance with the local flora and fauna: various centipedes, trolls, owlbeasts and giant spiders roam around freely without any interference from forestry officers, and all this wildlife is eager to take food right out of your hands.
While I was approaching to the capital, the first thing I noticed was the smell. Then I heard hammers thumping, handsaws squealing and builders cursing. And finally, the settlement itself appeared before my eyes. Its splendor can be matched only by your average Brevic village. If you are a carpenter, a stonecutter, or — especially — a janitor, you'll be embraced here gladly, though I doubt they can offer you any other payment besides the embraces. Anyway, I am convinced that a great future lies before this young barony, so I've decided to stay here a bit longer, to record all of the Baron{mf||ess}'s great exploits and deeds in glorious detail — for their descendants' education and for your entertainment. If I don't become a head shorter after this review gets published, wait for the updates in the next issue!"
"The Technic League always gets what's theirs!"
"The Tiger Lords never abandon their own! I'll keep on living and serving the tribe!"
"The Tiger Lords never retreat. Fear is not our way!"
"The Tragic Love Story of the Noble Maid Rosalinta and Ginratti Badbassor, the Night Bloodsucker"
"The Vascaris have long been a thorn in your side. You stood to gain from their fear, especially if you got someone else to do your dirty work."
"The Written Word on the Execution Block"

"The abominable embodiment of greed! He has no shame. He plunders the corpses of fallen heroes and sells his prizes. But I cannot forbid him from doing it. He does some good. – He sometimes travels around the area, delivering supplies."
"The armies of Taldor are invincible! Innumerable! Imbecilic!"
"The art of weaving spells, more so than any other, requires maintaining a strict internal balance."
"The assassins are already here! Follow me, quickly!"

"The bandits had greater numbers. They must have tracked us and timed their strike carefully. You see, our outpost was isolated. They waited for me to leave, then slew everyone else. And then they waited to ambush me. I was lucky to escape. I took the hammer from my elder son's hands, fought them off, and fled into the woods. After that, once my head cooled, I started hunting them. Eventually I lost them in the swamps by the {g|Kamelands}Kamelands{/g}. You know what happened next. I heard things turned out badly for the bandits. They're all dead except their leader. The fingerless wretch is still alive."
"The barbarians are still a way off, but I can smell them already!"
"The bard lied to you; the treasure's not here. I know where it really is." [Point at a random location on the map] "I'm too busy to dig it out myself..."
"The baron isn't mad at us, is he? We didn't mean any harm!"
"The baron{mf||ess} is here! Hang on! Help is on the way!"
"The baron{mf||ess}!"
"The battle is over! Mysteriado wins!"
"The battle is over! Zynmyrgya wins!"
"The beasts are everywhere!"
"The best locks from Highhelm! Don't miss your chance to get one!"

"The blazing sun overhead, a salty taste on your lips, the squawk of seagulls, calling you forwards. Ropes squeaking in the storm, as you fight against the sea itself — winning in the end. And, of course, the line of the land on the horizon, when you know that tonight you'll have a mug of rum in one hand and a smiling girl to share it with." {n}Darven gives you a sly smile.{/n}
"The blizzard is coming. It's so scary – but beautiful at the same time!"
"The blood of an innocent is on your hands, {mf|baron|baroness}!"
"The bonfire was great! Look what I found among the ashes."
"The building in front of us is your residence. That's where we'll head to now."
"The captain has ordered to guard tripled... what use is it now?"
"The centaurs, those mad beasts! Will we ever be safe so long as they roam these lands?"
"The chief always takes the best stuff. Even I recognize this as a law." {n}Regongar utters a guttural sound, clearing his throat.{/n}
"The city's chock full of you lot. Can't take a step without someone tugging your sleeve!"
"The civilized world ends at the river to the south. Beyond that are miles upon miles of impassable wilderness. What a relief it is that people will be settling there at last!"
"The climate in our land leaves much to be desired."
"The craft has no place for codes or other trade lies that limit your options."

"The danger has passed. The monster is destroyed. The great shell of its egg still lies under the ground, but its wicked seed will sprout no more. I feel the evil evaporating even now. The darkness lifts with each passing moment."
"The dark stalker fled across the Osirian desert, and the gunslinger followed."
"The day was long. Shall we rest for a while?"
"The debates, the fey, and their mysteries! And most importantly — we don't have to fight anyone! I like this adventure!"
"The debt of blood is paid in full. No one can call Amiri a pariah no more."
"The divine fire accepts any sin — and burns it away! There is hope for everyone!"

"The door flung open. The three chaps sharing adventure stories fell silent.
"Hail, friend!" said the visitor in a deep voice. "Have you got a room for me, master?"
The bored half-elf behind the counter peered into the visitor's face and whistled.
"Blimey! If it isn't Gregas Jeffs! Hail, friend! Let me give you a room – your gold is no good here!"
"No, I'll pay for it in full. That's what the Society is for. Helping and sharing!" Gregas nods at the three chaps. "So there's my replacement... Have you held the Confirmation yet?"
"We've got one last trial to go!" The youngest blurted out and popped up from his chair. "It's such an honor! I've read all the Chronicles! All about your adventures!"
"I heard you joined the Decemvirate, Gregas," another uttered.
"Oh, did you? You should cut off your ears then, they deceive you! Am I wearing a mask?"
"You ain't."
"Good for you. A Pathfinder with no eyes is no good. I'm not interested in politics. I'm interested in seeking. So, are you going to pour me beer? And I'll tell you a couple of tales..."
"The dweomercat does not forget those who help her. We shall meet again... Perhaps. Who knows!"
"The dweomercat has helped enough. Now you'll manage for yourself!"
"The elders were right – we're cursed, our whole bloodline. We're dumb. And unlucky."
"The farmers in the south will be slaughtered while these nobles are making up their minds! They'd better send more soldiers, and soon."
"The feat I ask of you is most dangerous, almost certainly suicidal. If you agree, I want you to understand what you're getting into."
"The ferrymen have increased the fee for transporting goods across the river — again. I had to raise prices to compensate."
"The fey are no match to my ingenuity."
"The first lock is open! Congratulations! But can you open the second?"

"The first of the River Freedoms — 'Say What you Will, I Live Free.' It doesn't mean you won't get beaten up for what you say, though!"
— Elina the innkeeper
"The first reasonable words in all this... this... this circus!"
"The fog, the silence... and then I heard this 'clip-clop, clip-clop, clip-clop, clip...'"
"The fool was begging on our turf. 'For Desna's grace!' Ha ha!"
"The gates of the ninety-nine hells open! Behold, for it comes! ...I said, it comes!"
"The goddess took cub mother's life as a payment. What a worthless female she was, only able to bear a single child! Goddess grants, her daughter will be more fertile."
"The gods deemed your husband's time had come. You should thank {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} for the happiness he bestowed upon your family all these years."
"The great lord awaits."
"The grimoire that will open this word's gates to devils! – It must belong to me! Give me the book and perhaps I'll spare your life!"
"The guards were losing pretty badly, then — bam! Sharp-eye. He saved their skins that day."
"The guards!"
"The heart of every city is its main square. We plan to hold street festivities and fairs here. Look — we already have our first vendor."
"The heart of every town is its main square. We plan to hold street festivities and fairs here. Look — we already have our first vendor."
"The help has arrived! Quick, we need to save Lady Jamandi!"

"The history of Rostland is known for its many mysteries. One of them is the story of Baron Sirian the First.
Sirian was a furious fighter, although not highly skilled. There were malicious rumors that he fled to Rostland, to hide from the sneering public after he'd lost dozens of duels in his homeland. But his new home greeted him with yet more misfortune. He waged not a fistful of coins, but a whole settlement in a duel with a gang chieftain – but the baron was broken again, and left Rostland in shame. He dropped off the map for several long years, and quiet anonymity changed him completely. Not only did he return home bearing a new name, Sirian Aldori, but he had also acquired a new gift! He no longer had any equal in swordfighting. Sirian challenged the chieftain who had once disgraced the young baron, and slew him in the blink of an eye. Afterwards he announced a reward of one hundred thousand gold coins to anyone strong enough to defeat him in battle..."
"The huntsmen have told me about their homeland. I pray that this place doesn't become like the Embeth Forest!"
"The king of the first kingdom destroyed by Nyrissa? But that happened millennia ago! The poor soul must have suffered so much..."
"The kingdom is in ruin. All is lost."
"The lady was within her rights — it's not a crime to fool an idiot!"
"The last lock remains undefeated!"
"The law says differently. You still owe that merchant, by the way. You'll have to work off your debt on his farm."

"The left one is for normal work. I use it to kill bandits and thieves spying on our secrets. It's loaded with ordinary bullets. The right one is for special occasions. Each of its bolts bears the name of a rascal who wronged me or my family from the times we languished in {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g}. When the right one is empty, my travels on {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} will end, and I will return to Alkenstar and find myself something else to do."
"The legend is... Immortal!"
"The lich seems even more dead than before, although that scarcely seems possible..."
"The life of an adventurer is full of surprises. Even a war with a First World deity doesn't seem so unlikely."
"The locals are kind and warm-hearted. But also impatient."
"The main course – hero cutlets. Served with an ally ragout..."
"The marchioness was not just a terrible mother, she was a criminal. For slave trading, I should be sending her to the gallows!"
"The marquise is so sweet, and her husband is very charming!"
"The marquise sends her regards!"
"The matter's settled!"

"The merchants became wealthy because they know how to read and write, and they studied history and geography. Let the people send their children to schools, temples, and sages, so they may learn and grow wiser."
"The miller is like this, the smith is like this, but the headman isn't like this. Though he can be like this, if he does like that."
"The miners know best on matters of who and what's safe in the tunnels — they don't need us harping on them about it."
"The mistress ordered me to get the book and to kill the pathetic mage! Get out of my way, I'm not going to a punishment cell!"
"The monster was invisible — he hunted and killed us one by one. We were on the marches, and he almost took me... but then a man emerged from the quagmire and killed the bloody thing!"
"The oath is sacred."
"The past seems to haunt me. I didn't expect to see a shrine to Shelyn in these dungeon depths."
"The performance is over. Let us thank the actors. Reckless mortal heroes — and you, my toy. You have all done precisely what I wanted, how I wanted."
"The playwright Eimar Deschamps asked me to attack the Vascari convoy, though he misinformed me about my targets' identity."
"The poor people of the city and the kingdom! It seems they haven't lived a day of peace since the moment it was founded."
"The portal has opened again! Help me!"
"The priest seems eager to speak with you!"
"The problem's solved. There was a monster in the box — a cyclops — but he's dead now.
"The return here, where it all began, the prototype, the precursor of all that is known to mortals... and it lies open before you."
"The ritual is over. Brother... I'm coming."
"The road's clear! We can move at last!"
"The roads are unsafe. I would suggest you go no further than the capital, and wait until the roads can be garrisoned properly — there's still plenty of trade to be had elsewhere in the region."
"The robbers took everything from me. Even my vestigial arm! But at least I have a story to tell. There aren't many people around here who've been robbed by a treant and a talking raccoon!"
"The rock troll in the woods nearby — is it real?"
"The ruler returned to his subjects. The kingdom survived. One grain of dust escaped from the cup."
"The scoundrel! That rotgut must've gone foul ages ago!"
"The second lock's defeated! Only the hardest remains!"
"The settlers aren't hurrying to join the militia. Everyone wants to live in a warm house, but who's going to protect those houses?"
"The seven paladins, and their lady Iomedae. She herself was there among us."
"The shadows! They're coming!"
"The skies tear open... It is as though the End of Days has come!"
"The story won't be complete until we gather all the characters, right?"
"The tail makes everything better, doesn't it?"
"The tamer of the Shrike Hills, who put an end to the atrocities of the Stag Lord's bandits!"
"The tavern's ale is blessed by Cayden Cailean himself, I swear! — And the lady who owns it is a gem."
"The things in this pile must be five times heavier than those mites!"
"The thunder subsides and those having fun pass away… What do they leave behind? Just ashes and bones... So in the end your Gorum doesn't differ much from my Groetus."
"The time for laughter has passed. It's the hour of hunting and chaos."
"The time has come! Your lives in exchange for the mercy of my sister!"
"The time has come. You are a stag now, not some defenseless fawn. Go. Go and fight!"
"The trade is booming, the taxes are bearable. Darven is a fine ruler."
"The traitor god… Torag priests used to set hiding places in statues like that. Look closer, if you wish. You might find something."
"The traitorous poet should be escorted to the gallows, with a loop in the noose for every lie. That's the sort of show I'd gladly watch from the front row!"
"The trolls tread here no longer. Good."
"The truth is the least I can give you for your feat."
"The truth is this bard lied to you."
"The truth will be revealed to those who seek it..."
"The undead are loyal, reliable, quiet... Everything one could wish of a servant."
"The verdict is out. You are doomed. Bow your head and humbly await your execution."
"The very sight of these low-life scoundrels offends me."
"The villagers say the souls of those who once lived here haunt their houses still. It is hard to dispel my congregation of such superstitions."
"The water is gone… completely gone… Do I really have to go to the neighbor's well now?"
"The way back to the road is free of traps, Waine. We just came from there after we heard you screaming. Come on, we'll make sure you get back safely."
"The will of Abraxas will be fulfilled at last!"
"The will of Lamashtu is done. Farewell."
"The {mf|Baron|Baroness|King|Queen} {mf|him|her}self! Greetings, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!"
"The {mf|King's|Queen's} wills the way."
"The {mf|king|queen}'s alive! I told you!"
"Their wine is all right, nice and strong! But the appetizers — pff! Barely a mouthful!"

"Theirs is a bear, and ours — a teddy!
Just hand the crown to Irovetti already!"

"Then I settled in Lastwall. A godforsaken place. Orcs are treated like scum. – It's understandable, I guess. Orcs kill many more people than you can count. I moved in near the Thorn Scar's territory, out of harm's way. They're a tribe, or what's left of one. They worship {g|Lamashtu}Mother Lamashtu{/g}, so they stay busy. They needed new armor and weapons every year. And so I worked my force in return for their protection."
"Then call me a bandit chief if you will. Some things simply mustn't be allowed, law or no law."
"Then came the land surveyor, to make sure my extension wouldn't 'impede street movement.'"
"Then go to Vordakai, and make haste... your presence offends me."
"Then let her go. Stop clinging to something that doesn't exist anymore — you only hurt everyone involved. Free the one suffering from your indifference, and care for your child and its mother."

"Then my fellows — worms and lice, unworthy of even wearing beards, let alone the glorious name of Skjegge! — betrayed everything we lived for. They decided to abandon the road, abandon the fortress, and return home with those Woradash cowards and Langebukk morons! They even had the nerve to accuse ME of betrayal! They spread rumors that my experiments had emptied the treasury... What a ridiculous excuse! A true dwarf will find his own way, even without gold! He would sooner eat stones than give up his life's work!"
"Then why do you keep bleating about Torag? It's sickening! You whine about him, like a lad about the girl who dumped him! And nothing about your Groetus!"
"Then you'll vanish. Even the most beautiful flowers die. Such is life."
"Then, all of a sudden, you get stabbed in a dark alley one evening."

"There are many goblin tribes in Avistan. These militant creatures do not construct cities, instead they build their settlements in forests, ancient ruins or in caves. Goblins do not farm: they collect waste, rob and loot, in other words — parasitize on more developed civilizations who avoid any diplomatic relations with these dangerous pests.
Goblins experience pathological fear of horses and dogs. Despite this, they do not disdain the company of wolves, which they use as mounts. In battle, goblin riders are terrifying: they are a striking force that breaks into the enemy's formation and carries horror and death to all who happen to be caught on the way.
Goblins are often accompanied by worgs — these creatures are larger than ordinary wolves and have even more ferocious temper. Although worgs allow goblins to ride on their backs, it's highly questionable who is the master and who is the pet among those two.
Another beast, which should be known to the curious explorer of the wolves and goblin tribes is a barghest. Scientists consider these monstrous creatures to be related to goblins, but in appearance they are very similar to wolves. Barghests are very dangerous: they are able to shape-shift, to instill a feeling of boundless despair in their victims, and tear them apart while they are in helpless state. For the goblins, barghests are sacred creatures: they believe these monsters once initiated the goblin race."
"There are more here. Look sharp — no one escapes!"
"There are no goods in his cart, only empty chests. I suspect he came to collect the loot from the chests in the attic and sell it!"
"There are prisoners here! But hold on — who are they? Careless victims who stumbled here? Or servants of Vordakai?"
"There are rules hanging on the poles. Go read them quickly or you can't participate."

"There are tons of diseases in {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g} that you won't find anywhere else. I guess they came along with those falling stars. Fungi, mechanical parasites, brain-eating worms... Fun to be had at every step!"

"There are two kinds of issues that the ruler must address: boring ones and amusing ones. The bright side: you have servants and advisors to handle all the boring problems!"
— Lander Lebeda
"There is a difference between taking initiative in battle and blatant arrogation. How can one who disregards authority be a leader {mf|him|her}self?"
"There is a secret door… there, in the corner…"
"There is no limit to your kindness, my lady!"
"There is no way we can dispel this barrier. We need to find a way to disable it. I suggest searching around these portals — they clearly have a common power source."
"There is room in this world for all sorts of different birds. Some sing sweetly, while others screech proudly. But the peacock displays bright feathers to outshine them all."
"There isss icssse on my scalesss!"
"There may be a lot of ruins here, but they were probably looted centuries ago..."
"There they are! The assassins!"
"There was a time when I would have found such toys entertaining. Not anymore, though."
"There was no water in the well yesterday. There is no water in the well today. But my hope is strong. I'll come to check tomorrow!"
"There was nowhere to go, really... rough times. But then, one day, I come to the market, and what do I hear? The Stag Lord's no more, and now a real baron{mf||ess} has the crown!"
"There were complaints about merchants disappearing in this area — along with their goods. We should look into this."
"There were two mastodons in the glade, but the lightning struck a tiny frog. That's what I call misfortune!"
"There will be no mutiny!"
"There's a certain dark poetry in the silence that fills me."
"There's a little chest full of bottles of sleeping potion in his cart –- the very same sort of bottles as there are here in the kitchen!"
"There's bandits and monsters all over the place. We'll need to double the patrols!"
"There's monsters everywhere!"
"There's no battle I can't handle!"
"There's no need for that. I actually liked those particular times. At least in that state my masters weren't able to beat me."
"There's no place for bandits in my {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom}."
"There's no time to save your junk! Run! — Run!"
"There's no way I'm putting my name on this! Label it as a folk song!"
"There's nothing but trouble waiting for us at home – and it's not much better here."

"There's nothing to tell. It's a traditional orc thing. Any decent battle gear must be big, heavy, and tough. Fragile and brittle materials don't last. The orcs' strength rages and storms! Small and light objects get lost all the time. That's why orcs need a weapon that can't be broken in half on the enemy's head. Orc armor must be even sturdier, because they fight each other far more often than they fight their enemies. Thin armor would result in many deaths among the tribe."
"There's nowhere to sleep in this stupid hole! My back aches for the fourth day in a row because of the cold…"
"There's only one thing I hate about libraries. The visitors... Uh, except for educated patrons of scholarship like yourself, of course."

"There's something else, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}… I've thought about this for a long time, and I must give up my position. I cannot guarantee the safety of those whose lives have been entrusted to me, if I don't understand the decisions of my superiors." {n}Shuffling his feet, Kesten adds:{/n} "I am sorry, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}."
"There's still so much to do..."
"There's unrest in the north. They say the Surtovans and the Swordlords are at it again."
"There, serves them right! Why talk to jerks?"
"There, there..."
"These Six Bears have frostbite in their brains!"
"These are the kinds of heroes we've needed!"
"These caves could be so calm and empty without kobolds fussing around."
"These creatures are much different than the other minions of Nyrissa. They display loyalty to their fallen friends and to their mistress. It would be sad to see them as our enemies."
"These huntsmen are exceptionally interesting people. It seems to me, they know much more than they tell."
"These lands are mine or soon will be. Go ahead and fell the tree. I'll wait to see what's hidden beneath it."
"These lands are mine! I won't let you take them from me!"
"These people are not just celebrating. It seems your feat has given them new hope."
"These people need help. Find some food and blankets for them. And keep your eyes open!"
"These roots are woven through the entire castle. They keep the walls from crashing down."
"These ruins… So calm and tranquil... Reconciles you with the future."
"These slaves need food, and we're still a long way from Numeria."
"These woods are swarming with faeries and other monsters..."
"These {mf|barons|barons|kings|queens} always think so high of themselves." {n}Shortie spits on the ground.{/n}
"They are both guards of this place and tokens of the druid's evil magic. Please, be careful!"
"They are, they're coming!"
"They both think only of themselves — not a thought for those who toil under them!"
"They call this a feast? I'd show them some real festivities, if they'd let me."
"They called us 'traitors,' but I think 'pragmatists' is more fitting."
"They come, they come! Come on!"
"They got someone! We have to help!"
"They got what they deserved."
"They had a rocky past, but so what? All their bickering is tearing their country apart!"
"They hoped you'd cry and run away. Yes, I remember."
"They invented their pathetic toys because they had no magic. Why stoop to their level? After all, we do have magic."
"They mustn't reach the lake!"
"They say repetitive activity wears you down. Well, I've discovered an interesting way to recover from palace intrigue..."
"They say there is unrest in the north. Barbarians are raiding distant villages."
"They say there's a secret treasury under one of the capital's wells. All lies, I think. All the gold would've been scooped up in buckets long ago if that were true."
"They should have been back already... I hope they're all right."
"They shouldn't have come here!"
"They sure as hell wouldn't like that. You thinkin' we should croak 'em, then?"
"They taught the ground to fly! Oh, I hope they made the lake fly!"

"They teach both magic and practical skills, both of which are certainly useful to combat mages. For instance, if you've learned to summon enraged monsters, it might also be a good idea to learn to run fast."{n}A smile brushes lightly over Raquillata's face.{/n}
"They tried once. Now they make every effort to stay away. They only show up if they don't have any other options, and even then they just politely ask me to enchant their arrows."
"They try to make walls of rules and laws here, foolishly imagining that this will protect them from endless chaos and the inevitable end."
"They will be back!"

"They will never accept you as their ruler, nor will they live peacefully with humans, in lands they deem their own. Do not pity them. They made the choice to reject civilization and continue living as animals."

"They wish to demolish these idols! They seek to destroy, with fire and chisel, all that would remind them that all things must come to an end." {n}Harrim strokes his beard broodingly.{/n} "Whoever it was that once worshipped these idols, their faith deserves our respect. It is your decision, but I would not destroy these ritual places just because the god they are devoted to isn't well known. I myself serve such a god, often decried by ignorant tongues."
"They won't get away from us! Cut them down like sheep!"
"They won't. We don't have anyone like that in the city."
"They'll be serving pot roast after the ceremony."
"They're back! Kill them before they call for more!"
"They're coming at us! Get ready, lads!"
"They're coming! Get ready!"
"They're coming! Guards! Everyone, here!"
"They're getting bold, the rascals! You just wait, the Swordlords will show'em!"
"They're just peasants, you knucklehead. What else to do you expect them to have? Silverware? Fine mahogany furniture, perhaps? Some nice Taldan paintings?!"

"They're mine, yes. You see, while I'm happy to welcome guests, I prefer those who are capable of coherent speech. I've neither interest in nor desire to waste my time with fighting off every monster that comes across my dwelling. But I did leave a safe passage for those who can read. I even installed a sign. You must have seen it."
"They're so weird, those kobolds. I get goosebumps just looking at them."
"They've attacked several villages, destroyed several bridges, and are scaring away trade caravans. Worse than bandits, by far."
"Thief!"
"Thieves guild! If {mf|King|Queen} {Name} wins, we'll all be hanged! Bring me {mf|his|her} head!"
"Thieves guild! Irovetti has betrayed us! Let's take his head!"
"Thieves! Go! Go away! My pillar!"
"Thieves! Maggots! Wretched pathetic creatures! I'll slay you! I'LL SLAY YOU ALL!"
"Think I might find myself a better wench. Who knows, maybe I'll even have some kids..."
"Think before you speak! 'A tall tale...' A paladin of Iomedae never lies!"
"Think carefully, boy. Serving Iomedae is no joke."

"Thinking about your conscience? I know, conscience is important for a ruler. It must be kept clear. But we spies have a job to do, and a spy's conscience demands only one thing: to protect our country."
"This 'Tartuk' again! It's like he's everywhere! I'm sick of hearing that name. I fear I'm developing a conditioned response — every time I hear 'Tartuk,' I feel the need to vomit!"
"This be King Nok-Nok meeting other King. We tear it down now!"
"This be King Nok-Nok meeting other King."
"This cannot be! The Master is just testing us! Do not falter, faithful ones!"
"This damn place gives me the creeps."
"This expedition is surely doomed..."
"This fight's a trap!"
"This forest so big! We could walk more than a day!"
"This is a bad idea. The more pathetic we look, the safer a target we seem. And I don't want my former friends saying that Linzi now serves the ruler or some backwater country!"
"This is a disgusting practice, but it doesn't violate any laws. I can't forbid you to continue your experiments."
"This is a hidden door. How you might open it from this side is a complete mystery."
"This is a message from the First Faithful. Looks like he's gathering his followers at a new location."
"This is absurd! As if we didn't already have enough problems with Gralton! Let's pile on a little more! They'll make such a lovely burial mound – over our graves!"
"This is all I managed to find."
"This is all just a test! We will show what we are worth!"
"This is careless. You'll merely tease them and make them angry. Far better to simply inspire terror. That alone will prevent them from stabbing you in the back."
"This is folly. The Goddess has abandoned us. We're just wasting our time."

"This is grave news for us all. My fire traps are useless now, and making acid traps will take time and resources... More importantly, for trolls to organize in such a way, there must be some greater intelligence operating behind the scenes. And if that's the case, the list of potential targets for a force that formidable is a short one..." {n}Bartholomew pauses, then begins to rummage through his lab.{/n} "I promised you a reward, so, please, accept these acid wands — I'm afraid you may need them soon..."
"This is it. My time has come... Oh, Groetus, take my soul..."
"This is it. We will all freeze to death."
"This is just conjecture! Empty chests are simply empty! Emptiness is not evidence!"
"This is madness! They are monsters – and you're just letting them go?!"

"This is merely a stop along the way. I don't choose these places, {name}. An island on {g|Candlemere}Candlemere lake{/g}, the {g|Temple of the Elk}Temple of the Elk{/g}... Long ago before remembering, portals from the {g|First World}First World{/g} were opened here. Years passed, and superstitious people, attracted by strange omens, founded temples near these places. One of these portals has brought me here. I'll leave through one as well."
"This is my fate, and I will drain it to the dregs."

"This is no way to settle scores. What do you hope to accomplish? To instill fear? They were bound to fear us in any case. But after this savagery they'll never deal with us again! And how am I supposed to erase these ugly stains from my reputation? I understand – you enjoy being a tyrant. But I've got better plans for my future."
"This is not how I imagined life in official service. I thought it would be more peaceful..."
"This is not how I'd hoped to finish the story of the Kingdom... but it's the will of gods. And of those who worship them."
"This is not the best decision. Your subjects will surely not approve of this — and I can't blame them!" {n}Octavia falls silent, contemplating something.{/n}
"This is not what I imagined being a governor would look like!"
"This is one of the most important decisions in your life. Do what you think is right."
"This is ours! Ours! We will live here again!"
"This is reprehensible. I don't care how you acquired this creature — I won't tolerate such cruelty in my lands! Kill him, quickly and humanely."
"This is suspicious, but doesn't form sufficient grounds for an arrest. Do you have any other evidence against him?"
"This is the answer to sacrilege and blasphemy! There will be no mercy for the enemies of the Master!"

"This is the crown of an ancient elven king named Lethoriel, ruler of the first kingdom Nyrissa destroyed. But it's not just his crown—his soul has been tied to it, his ghost forced to serve its owner. While it's broken, he's trapped in there, unable to manifest. But no wonder Nyrissa's cronies want it so bad."{n} He shakes his head.{/n} "Or {g|Shyka}Shyka{/g}, for that matter."
"This is the end!"
"This is the faith of our fathers and grandfathers!"
"This is the last pamphlet delivery from the academy. They won't print any more for us."
"This is true."
"This is your last chance — drop your weapons, and we'll spare your lives!"
"This isn't the Stag Lord's nest anymore. Your behavior is against the law, and the punishment is a stint in jail. So, you wanna learn what prison food tastes like?"
"This isn't the first time I've seen you here. What if someone else notices and decides to report you?"
"This lass came last."

"This mage has a bunch of traps around his house — scares off the trolls, you see. He even put a warning sign up by the road, so people wouldn't get hurt. You just have to stick to the road. Trolls are stupid, can't read. So they get caught."
"This man is a walking disgrace to our Goddess."
"This man, the playwright. He betrayed us. He hurt Renshala. He made us into bandits. Let him take the blame for his mistakes."
"This pain is nothing compared to losing part of my soul."
"This place is awful. It clearly wasn't meant for humans — or the living, really."
"This place is hidden from time, deceiving Groetus. I don't like it."
"This place makes my skin crawl. Let's leave at once — everything here reeks of foul magic!"
"This prattle bores me! Death to the intruders!"
"This punishment is too severe! Have mercy! Everyone strays from the path sometimes! This punishment is worthy of Razmir, not you!"
"This search will get us killed."
"This servant didn't just turn into a monster. The monster came out of him, ripping him apart! How could that even happen?"
"This should hold you!"
"This spell is so unusual... Not like daemon force at all, or a very ancient one. Well, get out of my way, you silly door!"
"This thing is totally evil. Maybe you shouldn't use it?"
"This tournament is a great idea. And Irovetti is such a gallant host!"

"This town in a foreign land
Has a narrow twisting street
With lanterns hanging on the left and right.
As I walk the twisting path between,
And the lanterns shine behind my back,
I leave one shadow on the wall,
And leave another on the road.
Since the day I settled here,
Every evening when the lanterns shine,
And the shadows dance in their light,
I walk this narrow twisting street,
And you know why."
"This tradition is older than your kingdom, {name}. Is it wise to interfere with other people's laws without first understanding them?"
"This wasn't cast by any human hand though, oh no! The brand was stamped on with some artifact, which would make it possible to make trolls fire-resistant in massive numbers!"
"This weather makes me envy my spellbook. It's much better protected from moisture than I am."
"This will be a glorious fight!"

"This will return to bite you later, Your Grace. You'll see… The moment turn your attention away, they'll be back to make more trouble for you. I do not understand why we should suffer these fools on our lands..."
"This won't be our last battle!"
"This world must be die soon."
"This young man is no passing merchant. He's in collusion with the owners of the inn!"
"This'll teach those slovenly guards not to slack off on the job!"
"This… this is unfair!"
"Those 'good' gods and their famous mercy… The souls of Bloom victims should applaud and weep tears of happiness, I suppose?"
"Those beasts hit us bad!"
"Those harmed by Irovetti can avenge themselves. Myself, I have seen nothing but generosity from him."
"Those kames in the Kamelands... I think they're petrified troll cupcakes! Trolls turn to stone when exposed to sunlight, right? Their food should do it, too!"
"Those merchants had deep pockets, but not THAT deep!"
"Those pirates are a blight on Pitax!"
"Those traps in the woods — are they yours?"
"Those were different times, boy. Dark times! Nowadays, we've got a new ruler, praise the gods, and no one has to take such sins upon their souls. We've got plenty of food on the table."
"Those who oppose me — their fate is ash."

"Though trickery fills our stories and lines,
What lies between them is not always a lie!"

"Though you've killed all the trolls, this is still grave news. To organize in such a way — ally themselves with kobolds — this speaks of some greater intelligence at work. You and your kingdom may be in danger..." {n}Bartholomew pauses, then begins to rummage through his lab.{/n} "I promised you a reward, so, please, accept these acid wands — I'm afraid you may need them soon..."

"Thousands of thousands are buried at the feet of Vordakai. Thousands of thousands will embrace the darkness and rise at Master's call. Thousands of thousands will start a new age in glory of the Four Horsemen."
"Thousands of years have passed, and here you are again, trespasser."
"Thousands of years searching. And for what?"
"Three bottles here!"
"Three times."
"Three... two..."
"Through the Eyes of the Ancients: A Monumental Painting from the First Century of the Age of Enthronement"
"Thunder! Lightning! Flood! Flame!"

"Thus I continue summoning heroes to this place. Many of those who answered my call turn their backs and return to their lives, once they discover how slim are their chances of victory – and I do not blame them.
