But my vigil is nearing its end. – The hour of the last battle with the monster draws near! If you can manage to weaken its shell, I can crack it, and we will finish it together!"
"Tie her up!"
"Tie the girl. She'll be executed after the battle so everyone can see what happens to those who stand in Armag's way!"
"Till we meet again, Your Grace! Thank you for all your help!"
"Till we meet again. Perhaps we'll manage to get along after all."
"Time to flee this barony, I'd say. With a {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} like that, we'll never get any treasure."
"Times are tough, and the guard is stretched thin. We need the aid of brave volunteers!"
"Times change, Knurly Witch. Your influence has waned. The crown is ours."

"Tioko once served Lamashtu. Then this brave and wise woman recognized how disgusting her patron was, and gathered the strength to leave her service, finding shelter in the hands of Desna. Alas, Lamashtu is called the Mistress of Insanity for a reason."
"Tired of being a fisherwoman. Will go for a pirate. Someone's cooking fish soup and here I appear: give me your soup or die!"
"To arms! The dead have returned!"
"To arms! Time to remember that Pitax isn't just trade and songs!"
"To arms!"
"To avenge all the lives he trampled!'
"To clear the city of drug dealers!"
"To glorious battle!"
"To guard the peace and protect our citizens is an honor for me!"
"To long years and new victories!"

"To make a long story short, these volumes were supposedly hidden in the catacombs of Gallowspire. We decided that the books should be retrieved and kept safe by the {g|Pathfinder Society}Society{/g}. We gathered in a tavern, discussed the expedition, then proceeded to {g|Ustalav}Ustalav{/g}. It was a normal mission — a quick and quiet recovery." {n}Anoriel smiles bitterly.{/n} "But everything turned out to be much more complicated. We barely made it through the Witchgate Forest. All those terrible living trees, undead druids and their arches of bone... It was a miracle we managed to make it out alive."

"To many, the Archknights of Avistan were legend. To others they were salvation. And to the wicked they were judgment. Their deeds were many, and spanned from the central jungles of Garund to the realms of Mammoth and Linnorm. Knighted in Taldor, but serving far beyond the scope of any one kingdom or empire, they proved to be more than just knights. Their name was given by a government official in Absalom after they foiled a plot to kill a number of powerful merchants and politicians.
Yet, for a band of heroes to be legend, they must be more than great as individuals or a team. They must have great motivation and they must have class. These Knights were said to find no injustice beneath their time or skill. Yet one goal did drive them like no other across the face of this continent and beyond. It was said that they sought the answer to one of the greatest mysteries of our time. What happened to Aroden, the last Azlanti? Their world trek put them in a position to help many, but it all was made possible by their desire to unravel the true fate of the living god, now thought dead.
And they had class. Guy Shaseur De Lombair was their spokesmen. A strikingly exotic half-elf whose father was a nobleman from Galt, and whose mother was a raven-haired beauty from Rahadoum. Victims of political turmoil in Galt, Guy's parents were executed by a device that would later inspire the creation of the Final Blades during the country's Red Revolution. Guy fled the land of his father and clawed his way up to be a great swordsman, wilderness guide, tracker, and Archknight. His political prowess was said to be as sharp as his dual elven swords. Because of his mother's anti-religious influence, he disliked the gods. He thought that they lacked qualities deserving of worship because of their failure to prevent the everyday evils of man. He was said to say on occasion, "let the gods admire me, for at least I am here making a difference with my own hands. And let the gods of darker dogmas fear me, for I will not rest until their cloisters are graveyards." Attired in glamoured armor, this outdoorsman dressed as elegantly as any could in that profession. And he danced around his opponents like a bird of prey, graceful with every strike.
After surviving slave pits and having to fight and survive in the wilderness alone as a child, he grew to be a man with a purpose. The world seemed to fall apart when Aroden was lost, so Guy vowed to find him..."
"To me, Riversong!"
"To me, fellows! And raise an alarm already!"
"To my deep regret, you're right. Bartholomew, you may keep the troll."

"To my utter regret, reading skill alone doesn't reflect the capacity for critical thought. Waine visited several times and was warned of the traps repeatedly. I pity the fellow, but his fate is his own fault, wouldn't you say? It would be like if someone were to snatch a flask of acid from my table and take a sip; I could hardly be held responsible for their physical distress, now could I?"
"To our {mf|lord|lady}!"
"To remain true to yourself even in death is a great gift."
"To stop being a slave, it's not enough to escape from slavery."
"To the left there's an observation platform — one can take in the whole city from there. You might be curious to see it for yourself, Your Grace."

"To the south of here. It is guarded by centaurs –- pathetic creatures always warring with us. They worship Desna –- a powerless goddess, gone insane. They believe she ordered them to guard the cyclopes ruins from us, that it's their sacred mission... It's ridiculous!"

"To the {mf|king|queen} of this land.
We need not be enemies. Give us the criminal murderer, guilty of the death of our children and friends, and we will leave your realm in peace. Be wise, ruler — your lands have suffered greatly, and keeping treacherous monsters by your side cannot improve your kingdom's lot.
We await your answer in the camp near the southwestern border of your kingdom.
Travelers from Kyonin seeking justice"

"To think I was planning to reward you!" {n}Dalton scoffs.{/n} "I've just fought off a band of trolls…" {n}He gauges you in disgust.{/n} "You won't be much of a fight, I promise you. My advice — leave now, while you still can."

"To you, my {mf|king|queen}, I give advice,
And pray it meets your ear:
Give up the throne and run away,
Or get thrown out of here!"
"To your health, {name}! By the way, if you are looking for where to go after the feast, I know a place. With a very... peculiar... menu. We only live once, he-he..."

"To {Name}, wishing you the best of luck in your endeavours. I pray that you'll never need to use it.
Jamandi Aldori"
"Today is a historic day for Restov — and maybe for all of Brevoy."
"Today is a historic day!"
"Today we raise our cups to Varnhold. I only look forward to the day that we raise them once more to celebrate an independent Rostland!"
"Today we shall finally wash away the filth from our souls, and clear the path for our Kingdom!"
"Today we will definitely get inside! Or tomorrow at the latest!"
"Today's a great day for a feast!"
"Together we'll bring order to these lands!"
"Told ya. These {mf|barons|barons|kings|queens} always think so high of themselves." {n}Shortie spits on the ground.{/n}
"Tomorrow, our glorious journey begins! Are you ready? I hope so — I don't need layabouts on my team!"
"Too bad kobolds left. Funny little bastards, they were."
"Too much fight. Too little food. Not what tiny allies promised!"
"Toothhh hurtsss! Why I bite that bone?"
"Tortured our brother! Killed our brother!"

"Traders... We... We're traders, Leksen and me! We..." {n}Waine waves his hand vaguely. As he relaxes, he starts to babble.{/n} "We usually come to visit the local mage, bring him food, and he gives us magic trinkets in exchange."

"Tragedy in House Lebeda!
According to our latest reports, tragedy has recently befallen House Lebeda. The house's heir, Lord Lander, has been reported missing. The Dowager Head of House and mother of the missing man, Sarrona Lebeda, publicly announced this only a few days ago. Further details about abduction, and the names of any suspects, are yet unknown.
According to rumor, shared by servants of House Lebeda, Lord Lander was captured during a hunt, or abducted directly from his sleeping chamber. However, another source claims that the heir ran away from his house of his own volition, and was last seen in the southernmost part of Brevoy. Many agree that the prolonged silence, maintained by House Lebeda after the heir's disappearance, could be explained by the sensitive political situation.
Sarrona Lebeda urged the abductors to listen to the voice of reason and return her son to her before she takes decisive steps to find him and return him home herself. It is yet unknown if Sarrona will take matters into her own hands, and if she knows anything about the abductors. In the meantime, the heir's disappearance remains an absolute mystery, and a challenge to the best detectives of Brevoy."
"Training fight mode activated."
"Traitor!"
"Traitorous scum! After we snuff out this riot, I'll have every one of your heads!"
"Traitors! How could you forsake your god?!"
"Trap no good. Missstresss will ssscold usss... eat usss!"
"Traveling is not against the law."
"Traveling within a foreign state without proper documents, however, is."
"Treacherousss! Treassson!"
"Treachery! Over here, everyone!"
"Treasure heavy!"
"Tremble, worms. I am your death!"
"Tribe go, find new home."
"Trickery... Treachery... There is no Kaessi here..."
"Trissstian... death whissspered your name..."
"Tristian, I will help you earn forgiveness. Together we will defeat Nyrissa."
"Trobold and King Hargulka help you, {race}! On our word!"
"Trolls are sentient beings, not cattle to be bought and sold. What you're doing is inhumane. Set him free."

"Trolls aren't enough, huh?" {n}Dalton laughs, then frowns.{/n} "Actually, I have heard a disturbing rumor… it's said a hodag has made a lair in a cave south of here. Whether true or not, traders are taking no chances, taking forest routes instead. Let me mark the cave on your map."
"Trolls became just like borba now."
"Trolls! Trolls attacking! Help!"

"Truly blessed and enlightened is that learned man or wise woman whose gaze has pierced the mysteries of alchemy. This path fortifies the spirit, sharpens the mind and teaches temperance in all things. Even the petty and the shallow have, through ardor in their pursuit of alchemical knowledge, achieved virtue. Yet nevertheless, this art is not without its dangers. An alchemist who turns to imbibing his own concoctions, as is custom among the young and impatient, may wreck havoc upon his very nature. For a potion is not merely a concoction, but a mixture of primes, which the naked eye cannot see. These basic elements of spirit, once they take root within, may intermingle and converge, and through their union poison the soul, compel deeds most disgraceful, or excite with the temper of a demon..."
"Trust me, Amiri, some questions are better left unanswered..."

"Trust me, the love of the people is fickle. No matter how much you give them, they'll forget everything at the first petty problem. Mind you, the wealthy class has a significantly better memory. They will remember if you stand up for them – or against them."
"Truth be told, I'm not really comfortable here. I lost my taste for high society."
"Truth be told, Trebricent's pamphlet is pretty banal. It's a shame we have to work with him."
"Truth in temperance."
"Tshe tat'cha! Warmblood — death! Longtail — death!"
"Turn around. It is the lair of a monster that's ruined thousands of lives. And who will keep it from ruining a thousand more? Not you!"
"Turns out, you also need to provide the deed to the land, a renovation permit, and Abadar knows what else!"
"Two week no catch one squirrel. Maybe they all dead?"
"Two-legged! Two-faced! Heartless!"
"Typical of a northern barbarian,"{n} Judge Celvoway snarls. {/n}"Guards! To arms!"
"Ua-ha-ha, here we go!"
"UarRRShe! ubU Sh'TkatrAH Bzha!!!"
"Ugh, it's not easy being a hero! I have a headache..."
"Ugh, that Galtan snake! She played us for fools!"
"Ugh... a good fight!"
"Uhh... Yes. Of course."
"Um... Good day! We're, uh... guarding His Highness' treasures! Yes, from anyone who might steal them!"
"Unbelievable. Have any fights broken out?"
"Unfortunately, that's not a distinction for you to make. You do know unlicensed medicinal trade is against the law, right?"
"Unfortunately, those who prefer law over anarchy must sometimes put up with such... dilemmas. It is a difficult path, but the only right one — especially in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}."
"Unless I was bored and wanted to make a new acquaintance... or rekindle an old flame... or maybe get even with someone."
"Unless you plan to fight the next battle without my best spells, we need to rest."

"Until recently, we knew this world as it was described in books and stories. A sewer, torn apart by hyenas that separate us with nations and borders, oppress us with extortion and lies, and assert their authority and power. However, someone else's hand rules these slaves who act like masters. It's a threat far more intimidating than a handful of arrogant fools. Our lands are secretly ruled by the most ancient creatures of Golarion, the inhabitants of the ever-dark depths, who know both past and future. People are led along paths they cannot see, and do not have the power to leave – to an end known only to our hidden masters. Some insist that the signs are purely coincidental, but they point to a vast conspiracy. Only a fool can fail to see how the myriad coincidences weave into a great cobweb. Or they have submitted their very will and sworn their allegiance to our unseen masters in the depths."
"Until then, Your Highness. I don't know what an extraordinary disaster you've brought upon your kingdom, but I see now that you are entirely capable of handling it. Especially with our help!"
"Until then, my place is here."
"Until then. I can't deny it, this mist had me worried, but now I see you have the situation in hand. I'm sure that together we will overcome this pestilence, whatever it is!"
"Untold swarms of demons descended upon us. But die we falter? Not a bit!"
"Unwise, mortal. Your mistress can't even protect herself from my justice, let alone you."
"Up the Rivalution!"
"VERDRIN!"
"VORDAKAI BE PRAISED THROUGH THE CENTURIES, FOR HE IS THE GREATEST OF THE GREATEST."
"VORDAKAI IS OUR MASTER. WE ARE HIS HUMBLE SERVANTS."
"VORDAKAI ORDERED US TO DIE. WE DIED. IF VORDAKAI ORDERS US TO RISE, WE WILL RISE."
"VVE'zeaWT troMAra! iN ROVAGUG ZEv'roaCH!!!"
"Valor and Honor: Ten Adventures of the Splendid Willas Gunderson in Absalom"
"Vanity and madness. Frail creatures fighting over a handful of ancient dust — that is all I see!"
"Varnhold it is, then. I'll be curious to see what you manage to build there. I might even pay you a visit some time..."
"Varnling Host! My eagles!"
"Verdrin?"
"Very well, so be it."

"Very well. It is good that we value such people. They are the backbone of the country, after all! They may be surrounded by weaklings who only care about their own interests, but they voluntarily offer you their shoulders, because they know that rock-solid governance is good for everyone. I will prepare a letter of commendation on your behalf, and allocate some guards to assist them."
"Very well... Tell Irovetti that I'm coming."
"Vesket stupid! Almost kill the tribe!"
"Village no save now. Must go away."
"Vordakai awaits you near the river. Go to our great lord."
"Vordakai" – this cryptic word must be connected to everything going on around here. But what – or who – is this Vordakai?
"W-welcome, Your Grace! Glad to serve you!"
"WHAT?! NO! LET ME OUT! LET ME OUT!"
"Wait! I am innocent. Any crimes I have committed were a result of Eimar's deception."
"Wait! We need to save these people first!"
"Wait, I'm... I'm not an emperor! But who am I? Then again... what does it matter now?"
"Wait, isn't this illegal propaganda?"
"Wait, you've been standing here screaming in fear for FOUR HOURS because there might be traps around you?"
"Wait... Where are you..."
"Wait... didn't you order this preacher executed?"
"Wake up you lazy dwarf!"
"Want kill us too, borba?"
"Want to do it again?"
"Want to go again? And again! And again!"
"War — fool."
"War! War! Dryskin bring war!"
"Warlord, we've captured an enemy spy! Let's kill her in Gorum's name!"
"Warmblood betray friendship? Thickskin was right!"
"Warmblood done lots for Longtails. But we not take too many gifts, yes. Otherwise, we lose our heart."
"Warmblood save Longtail tribe from huge evil! May sun and moon bless warmblood! May {mf|his|her} ancesters smile always at {mf|him|her}!"
"Warmblood! Your gods rot! Your ancestor eat mud!"
"Wasn't ordered to feed you. Now get up, you wimp!"
"Wasted money. But I guess it's not up to me."
"Watch out!"
"Watch out, you scoundrels! It's the gallows for you!"
"Watch your posture! Who fights like this?"
"We all know how it happens. You're living your life, minding your own business..."
"We all like sick or drunk."
"We already touched you! And kicked you! And tied you!"
"We ancient tribe. We no die easy."
"We are about to get her!"

"We are goblins, we will bite.
We will hurt you out of spite."
"We are great Taldan warriors! We are like lions! We even have fleas!"
"We are here, Lamashtu!"
"We are just in time. The sacrament has already begun."

"We are more than mere mercenaries. We are a brotherhood of warriors devoted to upholding the law – and fighting the ruinous powers of chaos. Each of us has sworn a solemn oath to follow the ideals of Abadar, and stay true to the best interests of society. These are more than words. — By the powers bestowed upon me by our divine benefactor, they have become a sacred pact, guided by the higher spheres."
"We are ready for the coronation. They wait for you outside!"
"We are the heroes of Taldor. We heroically arrived! Dropped heroically dead! And heroically decomposed!"
"We be giving you food! Dinner! Lunch!"
"We be seeing now how Goddess protects you! Why you stopped? Release the beast at him!"
"We build the place up — then it's time to do it all over again..."
"We bury you here!"

"We came to this island at dusk. Decided to spend a night at the shore, and go inland at dawn. We've seen some lights floating over the underbrush. For some reason, they don't approach, keep their distance from us. Tomorrow we'll head for the ruins.
The cleric and the paladin, who hired me to guide them, keep aloof. They exchange whispers about something hidden in these ruins and fall silent as soon as I come close. We've come here to search for treasures for a man called Gunderson, but these two seem to have some plans of their own. It would bother me less, if Rismel wasn't a cleric of Nethys. People say that the moods and methods of his followers change as often as those of their two-faced god. For now, at least, the cleric behaves nicely, except for constant frantic speeches about the ruins. Anyways, Bryt is a paladin of Irori, so I guess I can rely on his sense of justice.
We've heard about strange things that take place on the Candlemere Lake. A few days ago, local folks saw a bright flash of light over the tower at the island, and no one could explain what it was. Another strange thing I witnessed myself: when we were coming to the island on our boat, I noticed an old geezer on the shore — and this island is thought to be deserted. I guess the geezer saw us too, because he disappeared. I would track the old hermit down, but I don't dare to leave the campsite unattended. Can't help thinking this island is really cursed, as locals used to say.
If the curse is just a fable, and if Rismel doesn't try any tricks, we'll come back here and I'll take this note away. And if you find this note, traveler, hop on your boat and go back where you came from.
Erastil, bless me.
Morry Focrey"
"We can afford food now. Thank you!"
"We can handle the investigation. You can count on us, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
"We can worship Lamashtu? Nok-Nok be real hero!"
"We can't handle it without your help!"
"We can't just pass by! The man's clearly in trouble. We have to help him!"
"We cleared out a nearby lair of trolls who were resistant to fire, somehow. I'd like to be sure new ones with the same resistance won't appear. Do you happen to know anything about the matter?"
"We come help you, friend! You no angry if we set fire to city a little?"
"We destroy shrines now? Nooooooo! We just build them..."
"We did nothing, of the sort, crone. You've destroyed our property with your ignorance of magic."
"We didn't do anything! We just wanted to have a look at these ruins..."
"We don't give up! Lamashtu be with us! Bread-breeders will bloom!"
"We don't have time for this."
"We follow the way of Remus! We follow the way of the great Goddess!"
"We found Leksen — he's dead. Here's his brooch. Give it to his relatives so they have something to remember him by."
"We found Leksen. He's dead."
"We found the right trail! The ritual was held here. But be careful — there are dangerous beasts ahead."
"We had to knock about, of course. Had some bad times — then suddenly, we heard at the market that they Stag Lord was overthrown, and now there's a real baron{mf||ess} instead!"
"We had to start all over... but you know, without bandits shaking you down every week, things go a hundred times faster. I even travel to the capital to trade now!"

"We had to start over from scratch... but that's a whole lot easier when you don't have thugs shaking you down every week. See for yourself — now I can bring my goods all the way to the capital itself to trade!"
"We hail from Galt. Moving north to find work."
"We have a visitor — Jhod Kavken, a venerable priest of Erastil. He wants a word with you."
"We have stood guard here for thousands of years. In such times as these, we must become not only guardians, but fighters."
"We have suffered so much... And it's all her fault!"
"We have to get him out of here! Let me talk to him. I'm sure I can calm him down."
"We heroes are all such exceptional fools!"
"We honor the goddess!"
"We just lost our way. We'll take our leave."
"We just need to reach the tavern, take a rest, then Verdrin will be just fine! Right, Verdrin?"
"We know nothing."

"We last came a month ago, left him some supplies. We were riding back today, and we wanted to stop and pick up an order he promised to complete... Well, Leksen stayed to guard the cart while I went to the mage's house."
"We live quietly, and mind our own business."
"We make him count to ten?!"
"We make warmblood remember their place!"
"We may not be wholly to blame, but Eimar is not entirely guilty. Others lives hang in the balance. It is only right that we accept the blame to shield those who would otherwise suffer."

"We met some barbarians. I asked them who might know what tribe I'm from – but they didn't know anything. I don't have any tribal tattoos. Nothing. Actually they are all right. Well, some of them. The Blood Pikes, for one – they're great. All the rivers are theirs! We sailed with them during one of our escapes, almost all the way to {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, and they didn't turn us in! But the White Scars got us after that. Those guys are shit! They've sold their pride to the {g|Technic League}Technic League{/g}."
"We must trust in him. He deserves a second chance. Everyone does."
"We must understand how he got so smart, so we be like him."
"We need no weaklings!"
"We need to dress our wounds. Go, we're right behind you!"
"We need to get to the fort! Varn and his squad are already there!"
"We need to hurry."
"We need to run!"
"We need to think about our family, not about gods!"
"We not defeat Thickskin for long. Soon they eat us."
"We old like world... Is this end?"
"We paid him two gold. He wanted three, but we could only gather two... He told us anyway, though."

"We parted ways not on the best terms. But duty demands me to inform you that the well-known criminal called Darven has founded a city in the Kamelands, in the vicinity of your southern border. This hotbed of vice must be stamped out, and Darven brought to justice. I'm heading to this 'Brineheart' immediately. If you have even a pinch of decency, you will do the same.
Fulfill your duty.
Linxia Benzekri, the Order of the Rack."
"We plough this land! We should rule it as well!"
"We probably woke up the entire palace... Or maybe the entire city!"
"We promise, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}. We kneel before you and swear to become model citizens, you mark our words!"
"We saved your life, and you dare turn your back on us? Come now, thank {mf|His|Her} Grace for all {mf|he|she}'s done for you!"
"We see who Lamashtu-favored here!"
"We serve the great Charon, Horseman of Death! Bow before us, creature!"
"We set nothing on fire. Boring!"
"We shall watch them closely. But unless their faith demands something outrageous, sacrificing humans or dodging taxes, then I see no reason to suppress it."
"We should be careful. Dreams are already full of monsters — I dread to think what we might find in Nyrissa's head!"
"We should build a solid stone wall around the town... There are plenty of cyclops tombs all around. Should we take them down for bricks?"
"We should leave him. He was surely fated to die by this trap." {n}Harrim strokes his beard.{/n} "It would be wrong of us to prevent this man from reaching the end of his path."
"We should take care. If they raise the alarm, bandits from all over the fortress will come running."
"We shouldn't be seen together. – You remember that, right?"
"We shouldn't have agreed to this game... now we'll never be able to return. Ever."
"We stand for our homes, brothers! Hit them hard! Varnhold will be ours!"
"We stupid like children! Believe evil spirit!"
"We sure showed them what's what!"

"We take pride in our friendship.
Goblins have good leadership."
"We want to save you! Come to our meeting!"
"We want to see the {mf|baron|baroness}!"
"We were ambushed..."

"We were hoping you could tell us. It must be the spells of the fey — or who else did you manage to enrage? This mist is no mere fog — it bewilders the senses and makes you wander in circles. But phantoms are worse. They appear from out of the mist, and there's no end to them. Shadows of our warriors and barbarians, endlessly repeating a fearful battle, none distinguishing friend and foe..." {n}Jamandi shivers, as if icy cold wind is blowing at her back.{/n}
"We will Winn!"

"We will cut you with our blade.
Into shadows we will fade."
"We will enjoy letting our worms crawl through your skull."
"We will meet at the capital!"
"We will meet in the capital!"
"We will never fight for others' gold again."
"We will not leave! This is the legacy of our ancestors!"
"We will not let you trample the shrine!"
"We will remain here on guard for as long as the magic of the key holds. Rest now. The way will open soon."
"We won't let the Varnhold nightmare repeat itself."
"We won. The monster is defeated. So why do I feel that our victory is not complete? I am filled with doubt. Something is wrong."
"We'd accept Oleg's invitatin and rest".
"We'd be better off building the town underground. That damned dragon Ilthuliak wouldn't find us there!"
"We'd been associating with the Stag Lord's band, but since you went and beat the stag out of him, we're left on our own."

"We'd chosen Renchurch to stop at. It was marked on Vermelt's map as a safe enough haven to hole up in and lick our wounds... How I wish that had been true... Vermelt was the first to perish. He was attacked by one of the monsters hiding in the stables. It tossed him about like a feather, and threw him down an ancient well. His shout echoed for a long time, and I didn't hear the sound of him landing. And then..." {n}Anoriel pauses and turns away, hiding her eyes.{/n}
"We'll appoint a trusted cleric as the new leader of the village. Someone to make sure the cultists don't return to their old ways."
"We'll bury them here!"
"We'll clean this place up! Everything will be good as new!"
"We'll crush them and return to Numeria as rich men!"
"We'll crush this rebellion with force. Gather the troops."
"We'll do it, {name}. It will take time, of course, but eventually we'll be better for it."
"We'll do well with Armag leading us!"
"We'll end both you and your hideous kingdom, monster!"
"We'll feed you to the wolves!"
"We'll find us a better god!"
"We'll finish him later. He won't get away!"
"We'll get on our knees before him, empty our pockets if need be. He'll forgive us, then he'll tell us where the treasure really is. Let's go! Come on!"
"We'll leave at once!"
"We'll make it to the camp on our own. Please, save the others!"
"We'll rebuild everything — even better than before!"
"We'll rest a bit, then look for a way out."
"We'll return to this later."
"We'll speak tomorrow, good {mf|lord|lady}. I need to count the losses."
"We'll start a new life in your barony!"
"We'll stay here a little while longer, and then we'll go wandering around! We'll see the world!"
"We'll still fell the tree and dig here, {mf|m'lord|m'lady}. Since we've already started, and all."

"We'll support {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}, even though elves won't even consider sharing their revenue or connections with us? {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, I lack the wisdom to understand your decisions!"
"We'll survive. Don't know how, but we will."
"We'll talk tomorrow. I still need to clean this mess. Getting rid of all this blood will take forever!"
"We're better off on our own!"
"We're coming up. I mean, closer. I mean... we're approaching the real Nyrissa!"
"We're doomed!"
"We're from the village nearby, {mf|m'lord|m'lady}," {n}the bravest of them answers, and the others nod along.{/n} "We wanna cut this here tree, see?"
"We're here for our money, sweetheart. Now cough it up."
"We're missing a good opportunity."
"We're not theoreticians or professors, Your Highness. We're arcane practitioners, combat specialists, and frontline workers. We're willing to share our knowledge with your military mages."
"We're still finding bodies in the rubble..."
"We're under attack! To battle, everyone!"
"We've also been told you're a troublemaker — just one step from becoming a rebel, in fact."
"We've been expecting you and Valerie. Please inform the priest of your arrival."
"We've been preparing this celebration for many centuries. Ah, I am having so much fun! Join us!"
"We've been waiting so long — we were finally going to found a dynasty! A trade empire!"
"We've chastised the apostates. This will be the fate of any blasphemer!"

"We've learned the name of the one who was plotting against you. It's an ordinary man from Gralton. However, he's a major spy for Litran, the Grey Gardeners' capital in {g|Galt}Galt{/g}. I don't know what attracted him to us, but now we have him on the hook."
"We've lived all our lives around here, {mf|m'lord|m'lady}. Got nothing to be scared of."
"We've received a letter from {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} concerning Oleg's Trading Post."
"We've received reports that a dangerous criminal is hiding in the nearby forest."
"We've repelled the attack, but the battle is far from over."
"We've repelled the attack. Thank you — you've saved my life again."
"We've seen enough horrors! Die!"
"We... are simple travelers from Brevoy."
"We... we didn't cross at a border guard posting!"
"We... we haven't lived like a husband and wife for a long time. The love that once bound us has cooled."
"Weak! Pathetic! Worthless!"

"Wealth comes in different forms. Sometimes neighbors build it together, enriching each other. Some decimate each other instead. An agreement with Daggermark will definitely bring much profits... But to whom? Think about it!"
"Welcome to Varnhold!"
"Welcome to Varnhold, Your Grace!"
"Welcome to the Inconsequent Debates! We'll begin in a moment."
"Welcome to the mansion of Swordlord Jamandi Aldori."
"Welcome to the temple of Erastil."
"Welcome, Your Grace! Always a pleasure to see you."
"Welcome, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}! Always a pleasure to see you."
"Welcome, my robin. Greetings from the House at the Edge of Time and its mistress."
"Well hello, hello. The Honest Guy's shop welcomes every guest!"
"Well well well, what have we here... Time to get to work!"

"Well, 15 slaves have just been delivered from Ustalav. I made an order for 40. More than a half died on the way, and the rest came with some sort of disease. I've sent them to the lab — they weren't good for anything else anyway.
---
We had to change barracks to get rid of the disease. Burned the old one to the ground, along with the slaves that remained there. I doubled my order for new ones. Delivery is expected to arrive by spring.
---
Worthless, stupid dreams. Again, the same wench as before. All night long, promising me a crown and a throne in exchange for some piece of garbage from the Stolen Lands. The throne's location and the kind of crown, she never mentioned. I need to prepare some magical protections.
---
The agents have dragged back the slaves who fled two days ago. I've made an example of them — whipped them to death in front of the others. Now to change the locks and shackles.
---
That fey keeps bargaining. Now she's offering me all the secrets of the First World in exchange for some artifact. So, she wants me to go all the way to the middle of nowhere to search for no-one-knows-what? Just who does she think I am?
I'm tired. Not a single night passes without her coming. But I'm intrigued. Maybe I'll have a use for this wench after all.
---
Now Nyrissa comes even during my midday naps. She's so impatient.
Regongar and Octavia have found themselves a new owner. I should have guessed it would end like that. So many years and so much effort — wasted.
I have to do everything myself.
---
I'm going crazy. Nyrissa keeps hiding her face from me, for the third night in a row! I'm trying to sleep both at night and during the day. I need some sign to know that I'm doing what I'm supposed to!
It's dusty here, hard to breathe, but that doesn't matter. There's been no Technic League hideout in history as useful as this one! I was lucky that some of our people had previously arranged for a safe spot within the Stolen Lands. There could be no better place for us to set an ambush! It should be easy to lure this {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} out.
---
My dream was short, but I got what I'd been craving. A light touch from mistress Nyrissa was all I needed. She gave me a chance! My head won't touch pillow again until I kill the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}! That filth will pay for all {mf|he|she}'s done, or my life is over.
I will not disappoint my mistress."
"Well, I liked the Stag Lord, but who says I won't like him dead?"
"Well, I saw how wonderfully he plays with Kyt, and I thought... Maybe your son would be amenable to accompanying Ronald on his journey?"
"Well, Tartuccio... Hic! W-well, scum... And how did we... Hmm, maybe I've had one too many..."
"Well, at least we got the chance to explore the region. And the locals were happy to learn they didn't have an evil undead neighbor after all."
"Well, at least we had some luck here... I'll sail upstream, Your Grace. I hope you'll join me soon!"
"Well, compared to the Lantern King's pranks, my tricks are just boring..."
"Well, don't be shy! Go, and meet your subjects!"
"Well, flower, let's see what's inside you..."
"Well, good luck with your work."
"Well, hurry it up, before — stop! Someone's coming!"
"Well, if only with my work… I work with wood. I can make spears, bows, shields..."
"Well, it won't be long before you learn the ropes. You seem like a bright lad. Brighter than I was."
"Well, it's harder to ask you out if I don't know your name."
"Well, now you're selling to the right market. Let's see what you have... Heh, not bad for a day's work!"
"Well, now, not out of NOWHERE... {mf|He|She} came from Brevoy! Sent by the Swordlords themselves!"

"Well, one day, this little tot came by and traded her father's belt, two bottles, and a hunk of bread for a two-volume collection of legends about the Archknights of {g|Avistan}Avistan{/g}. Came back later all tearstained — looked like her daddy didn't need the belt after all. So she sniffles at me and says, 'Take me with you, I can help,' and looks at me like a lost puppy. So I took her along — why not? And that's what got the ball rolling."
"Well, people say your daughter has grown into quite the beautiful young lady..."
"Well, put your backs into it! I can smell the gold, I can!"
"Well, the Surtovans I can understand — they're the lawful heirs to the lands, not those sword-swinging upstarts. When the Rogarvians..."
"Well, the cattle were gone, which is to be expected, but the house was practically untouched! Too far from the Stag Lord's fort for them to bother with, I guess."
"Well, their adventures have certainly come to an end!"
"Well, then, summon your power! Or maybe you'd like to try the acid?! I am not your slave any longer."
"Well, then... Some things made of iron... pots... boards... Damn, it's not here! They stole it! We've been robbed!"
"Well, there we go again. Working for the commoners instead of making them work for us…"
"Well, these are only drafts... But of course you're welcome to read them! Just keep in mind that even if you don't like what I write about, I won't change a single letter – so don't even ask!"
"Well, we might shake down a foreign merchant every once in a while, but we've never laid a finger on one of our own. And as you can see, we always pay for our drinks."
"Well, we'll have to make do. This should at least last us a while..."
"Well, what do we have here? Where are you headed from?"
"Well, what kind of question is that? You're all grown-up {mf|boy|girl} already, so guess yourself". {n}Octavia looks embarrassed, but her eyes sparkle with tease.{/n}
"Well, you can't let just anyone work in the mines — that'd be a recipe for disaster!"
"Well, {race}... Today you've helped the dweomercat."
"Well... At least allow me to thank you for sparing my life."
"Well... I mean, what's a halfling going to do underground? You're so... small... And..."
"Well... what about your reputation?"
"Well..."

"Went into the woods. Found many roots, pine cones, flowers — and a dead squirrel. Scant little I can make of that! I must consider where I might gain rarer ingredients for my experiments.
...
Some damnable racoons got into the hut while I was exploring the woods. Broke all the glassware. The only things left are ten flat-bottom glass tubes, five round-bottom flasks, a couple porcelain mortars, three pestles and the precious spiral. — A good thing all the pots are still there. So many good chemicals wasted! Shame. Need to lock everything up in the closet.
...
Tried to finish the experiment today, the one I started at the old lab. Used the lead powder from the master's box. At the crystallization stage the liquid foamed, changed color and formed a deposit. Another unsuccessful experiment — and I've all but exhausted my supply of essential materials.
...
Caught a racoon with a snare trap. Didn't get the bastard to the hut in time. Perhaps I should ask some hunters for help in catching experimental subjects? But I must save money, and besides, I see how those bumpkins scowl at me. As if I've grown horns!
...
Third attempt at the crystallization experiment. Broke the last round bottom flask. — I recall my tutor calling me ham-handed and making me clean up. Perhaps he was right. But he did teach me much, despite everything. But why didn't he wish me to develop my abilities? Didn't he want me to learn anything beyond the basic potion recipes?! Kept saying I wasn't ready, but in truth he feared the student surpassing the teacher, and for good reason: I shall prove this process works. I'll prove it to everyone.
...
Today an old lady came from the nearby village, asking me to make her goats yield more milk. I had to help — I'm in desperate need of money. Oh, why must I spend my time so?
...
Boring, boring, BORING!"
Several pages remain empty, then the writings continue.
"Observation day 1
Finally. I finally got a chance I can't miss. I found a dying elf in the woods. She was barely breathing, and ants were swarming all over her. Who is she? What happened to her?
It matters not: this is the opportunity I've been waiting for.
With great effort I managed to drag her to the hut, remove her clothes and hide her behind the bags in the corner. Enough wasting my talents on trifles — it's time for action.
Used the largest glass tube from the master's box, the one with the warning ("In case of contact with skin, wash off immediately"! Ha! The dottering parrot of all the standard warnings.) I spread it evenly over her body, and began my observations.
Observation day 3
The subject has survived. Had to tie her up and gag her — the moaning could attract unwanted attention. Her skin is changing, but… it's hard to determine the precise character of these changes. The early stages of festering, perhaps? The treated areas do smell faintly.
Observation day 5
The changes continue, faster and faster. The epidermis has festered away, the joints are grown swollen, tough and calloused. — And the subject has a fever.
Observation day 9
Over the past few days, the subject's legs became covered with mildew and moss. Her fingers and toes grow long and crooked — as though she would grow into the ground? I shall move the subject outside. The experiment now demands sunlight.
Observation day 13
The body's changes are so significant, it's impossible to recall the creature's original appearance, from the way it looks now. A seething growth covers the whole body's surface. Every day I find new kinds of moss, mildew, grass and other plants.
The subject attempts to move. Had to immobilize her. I try to make contact, but she utters inarticulate sounds, alike to howling. Might intelligence be restored at a further stage of regeneration?
Observation day 18
The subject has grown larger, several times. She is now… strangely quiet these last few days. I'm beginning to worry: in the end I see I've become attached to her. She will make me famous!
Observation day 25
My living experiment shows all signs of obedience. She is much like a little tree — a magnificent walking tree! She is already eight feet tall, and the child keeps growing! I wish to give her space, more fresh air and sunlight. I suspect we shall need some fertilizer… For now, I only walk her around the woods on a leash.
This is the greatest achievement of my career! Soon we'll be ready for a journey to Absalom, and there… there I will present my masterpiece. I must think of a name for my girl..."
