"Will {kingdomname} really become part of Pitax? Can you imagine what possibilities that would open?"

"Will-o'-wisp
An amusing glowing ball, which looks harmless and doesn't arouse any natural suspicion. Pretends to be a guiding light in the marshes, but leads travelers to certain death. The agonizing fear of their victims is this monster's nourishing dinner. If you manage to resist their tricks, make sure you have some electrical protection. The monster electrocutes any visitors it fails to lure into terror.
Werewolf
Werewolves prefer to hunt in groups, and attack lone travelers. It's entirely possible that a Varisian camp or troupe could turn into a pack of bloodthirsty lycanthropes under cover of darkness. Ordinary weapons stand little chance against them, but a silver blade greatly increases your chances of survival.
Primals
Powerful creatures of the Primal realm occasionally visit this world for amusement. It's best to stay out of a Primal's way. Don't fight it – it's extremely dangerous. But if a life is at stake, resort to cold steel."
"Willingness to fight for your dominion no matter the cost, against any enemy — that is the foremost quality of a ruler."
"Winter's not far off, you know. Gonna need some wood," {n}the second man adds.{/n} "And with this much, we maybe could build a boat, too."
"Winters are harsh here... But milder than in Brevoy!"
"Wise. Rage is a horse dragging a cart down a hill. You must hold its reins tightly."
"Wish the tavern was rebuilt already."
"With just a whistle, this whole street — guards included — will fly to my side! Then, it'll be you and your thugs getting a proper beating!"
"Without Nilak we will not survive the wild southern lands..."
"Without a doubt, for such prices you're going to Hell. We'll see you there!"
"Without the support of the throne, we're no militia — we're just plain thieves! That won't do!''
"Wits must be in tongue. Rip out his tongue, then we eat it and get smarts."
"Wizards are the best lovers. Though I guess I never tried druids..."
"Woe is me! I didn't get a chance to pack!"
"Wonderful. Now the centaur barbarians have added themselves to our already too-long list of our problems. We'd best order long pikes for the infantry, and beef up the fortifications..."
"Woof! Bowwow!"
"Woof! Woof!"
"Woof!"
"World become old, become rotten. End near..."
"Worry? Only that my dear husband drinks himself blind while lounging at the fort!"
"Worshipping Lamashtu right at my doorstep... These are troubled times indeed."
"Worshipping Lamashtu... What's next? Rovagug shrines?"
"Would you arrest someone who just saved your life?"
"Would you like some fresh fish?"
"Would you like to see the fresh catch?"
"Would you listen to that? Guess these young ones are growing up just fine..."
"Would you please behave at least in front of {mf|His|Her} Grace! We've had quite enough of this manner you allow yourself with the peasantry!"
"Would you... like to try the oil anyway? It's a most incredible medicine!"
"Wouldn't want to have mobs of disorganized vigilantes wandering the forest, now would we?"
"Wounds are a matter of course for a fighter. It's not the wounds that bother me, but the forced idleness."
"Wow! It worked. We did it!"
"Wow, that was some trick!"
"Wrath"
"Write whatever you wish – it's your right. But I shall decide if your book is allowed on my lands."
"Wrong again, mister. Whatever we do, we make sure it's fair. You work more, you earn more. You got the most respect, you get to be the boss."
"Yeah, I know you — just like I know all the rest of the scum around here. I still got more than enough sense not to trust any of you on your word."
"Yeah, that illusionist really knew how to make sure everyone gave his laboratory wide berth!"
"Years."
"Yep. All that thieving and robbery — that's all behind us. From now on, we'll be livin' like magnets! Er, magnates? Whatever, you know what I mean."
"Yergrace! Chest good, no need kicking!"
"Yes! All our lives have changed under the baron{mf||ess}!"
"Yes! At last!"
"Yes! I felt {g|Gorum}Our Lord in Iron{/g} looking down on me!"
"Yes!"
"Yes, I am," {n}the wizard answers curtly.{/n} "It's become far too dangerous to stay here. Besides..." {n}He doesn't finish the thought.{/n} "Never mind. It doesn't matter."
"Yes, I helped them! And I'd do it again! Their love is stronger than your petty prejudice!"
"Yes, Your Grace," {n}Bartholomew mutters.{/n} "I released the beast into the woods. If you meet it, give it my regards."
"Yes, Your Grace," {n}Bartholomew mutters.{/n} "You've seen it with your own eyes. At least I managed to gather some useful data from its corpse. I hope you're satisfied."
"Yes, Your Grace. It's become too dangerous to stay here, even with your protection. I'm going to look for somewhere safe and quiet."
"Yes, everything seems to be in order... Wait, why is the seal cracked?"
"Yes, mASter, yeS! deVOUr my fLESh, ROVAGUG! DeVOUr my lIFe!!!"
"Yes, of course! Here are my papers."
"Yes, of course, you're right. Bartholomew, do as she says."
"Yes, the caravan sure was lucky no one attacked them. A rare thing in these parts!"
"Yes, this goes beyond mere coincidence! Will you confess, or shall I give you to my friend Cephal?"
"Yes, you are right, my {mf|brother|sister}."
"Yes. And you are...?"
"Yes. I saw it. It was dark when she came. Take this one, it's her. My husband can confirm my words."
"Yes. Let's go."
"Yes. Will you make me regret this, {name}? I just thought... I felt you might be someone who could help my sister and me change our fates."
"Yes. You must leave, Kimo."
"Yes."
"Yes?"
"Yes?" {n}The elf is so impatient that he's tying his fingers in a knot.{/n}
"You 'invited' us when your trolls started attacking peaceful villages."

"You act as though you have another set of subjects in your pocket, who are somehow entirely different from Davor. Don't you understand that by prosecuting him, you are making half your citizens nervous? They're all doing the same thing, you know."
"You again?! I will not allow you to defile this place as well!"
"You already do. Daily."
"You are a criminal, Amiri. You won't get away!"
"You are a mercenary party no more. You are my personal guard, the best of the best!"
"You are amazingly gullible for someone who stands against the king of lies and masks, {name}."
"You are apostates! Blasphemers! Return to the true faith or die!"
"You are awfully quiet."
"You are dead, my brother. Killed by these miserable mortal creatures. And I'm free. Finally. Free!"
"You are here! Please, follow me..."
"You are just a pencil mark in the margins of my epic!"
"You are marked by all-seeing Nethys – which means we're going the same way!"
"You are right to withhold judgment on unproven accusations. Your job is to find out the truth, and conduct a fair trial. You cannot pronounce a sentence until you ascertain there was a crime."

"You are the head of a foreign state,"{n} the magistrate admits with disdain. {/n}"Although putting you under arrest is not within my humble power, you shall be reviled as a treacherous murderer and scoundrel throughout the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}!"
"You are the one behind all this and I can prove it!"
"You are wrong, mighty Tane. I've learned much. And I'll prove it to you."
"You asked for it, vagrant."
"You be dead!"
"You be good {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}! Goblins will make great songs about you when you die!"
"You be puny-full! No way, you swindle-try, traytor!"
"You be scared? Scared, huh? You be afraid?!"
"You believed in your death so much that you really died, dwarf. Few can boast such powerful beliefs..."
"You bet!" {n}Amiri thrusts her chest forward, anticipating a good fight.{/n} "But I'll call you if I need you."
"You call this a blizzard? You've never been to the mountains!"
"You call this justice, Walsh? Fine. I will comply." {n}Jhofre looks you in the eye.{/n} "I hope we'll never see each other again. For your own sake."
"You call this justice, Walsh? Fine. I will comply." {n}Renshala looks you in the eye.{/n} "I hope we'll never see each other again. For your own sake."
"You came after all... May I leave my post?"
"You can always move to one of the communal farms on the outskirts of the city. There your children will be taken care of while you fend for your family."
"You can buy every lock seen in the contest, and many more!"
"You can go harder... I cherish every scar I got from you two!"
"You can stay here for the night."
"You can't always get what you want, you know. Unless you're me." {n}Darven gives you a smug smile.{/n}
"You can't cast spells, you're a barbarian! Where is the wizard? Don't we have a wizard in our party?"
"You can't go here! Get lost to where you came from!"
"You can't judge a predator for killing sheep. It's the natural order of things, which neither you nor I can control. Banishing someone who makes your pack stronger is... foolish. Truly foolish."
"You can't stop nature's wrath!"
"You can't treat the rich and the poor the same! You just can't! This is how you devastate your people!"
"You cannot even comprehend my grandeur!"
"You cannot kill the water. If you dry up the stream, it will simply come back with the rain!"
"You chose this fate for me. I simply must accept it."

"You could say I returned {g|Torag}Torag's{/g} gift... Or did I finally use {g|Groetus}Groetus'{/g} gifts as he intended? Or was it that I shed a curse? It depends on how you look at it... how you look at it..."
"You could spread the word of {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}. Help people understand the futility of existence. The sooner this agony of life ends, the sooner eternal tranquility will come."
"You didn't expect this, did you, commander? You see, my new patron, let's call him the Horned Hunter... promised Varnhold to me."
"You do understand that your so-called offer in fact leaves me no choice?"
"You don't have to prove anything to me. I already know you're brave — and a skilled warrior."

"You don't know what you're saying! A good guard has to be either lean and mean, or fat and cunning. These guys don't score too high in the brains department, so I keep them running so they stay mean. We keep doing things your way, you'll end up with a horde of fat, lazy bumknuckles!
"You don't seem to like my curses. Maybe you'll like my jokes better?"
"You doom yourself, warmblood. Longtail eat you, then your kin!"
"You dumb little shit..."
"You eat not me, you eat him!"
"You fool! Get lossst!"
"You fools came to us! You won't leave here alive!"
"You fools! What is this, a revolt?! Drop your weapons!"
"You freely and calmly admit that you pillage corpses."
"You go Queen? Joy see her!"
"You go ahead. We need to prepare for the battle first."
"You go first. I'll come later."
"You got that right! It shows — a real {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}! Everyone pees their pants and calls for their mommies as you approach!"
"You got the wrong guy! I'm healthy!"
"You grave-rotted imbecile! You broke it!"
"You guess yourself? Or you have help? No, not yourself. King Hargulka gave you hint. Smart borba. So smart." {n}Hargulka grins viciously.{/n}
"You happy Nok-Nok allows you travel with him?"
"You have a strange life, {race}. A flying stone city, attacking shadows. You kill it and it's gone. Nothing to eat!"
"You have a strange notion of thrift. I suggested minting our own coins because at present your treasury is taking in much less than it could."

"You have accomplished a great feat. I bow to you. Now turn away from this kingdom of darkness, and return home. – The peace that you have won will last for many generations. I will remain here. My duty is not yet fulfilled. My vigil will continue..."
"You have an incredible gift for bringing upon yourself the wrath of great powers."
"You have crossed paths with the Technic League. This shall be your undoing."
"You have ears everywhere. Put them to use. Report anything suspicious that you come across."
"You have learned nothing, trespasser. And what of you, cursed {mf|king|queen}? Are you ready for one final lesson?"
"You have my thanks, my pupil."
"You have no authority over me!"
"You have no power over me! I will destroy you! Now!"
"You have overrrcome the gate! Now go to the Valley of the Dead! Go and meet your fate!"
"You have paid for your crime, in bringing us a cup filled with the dust of a thousand ruined kingdoms."
"You have such a sweet birth mark just here... It's a pity you can't see it!"
"You have won, where I lost in disgrace. You have saved the entire world from a monster – and me, from my pride. I bow to your victory."
"You haven't answered the question! What is this gift?"
"You haven't been to Restov for a long time, Your Grace. The guild has inflated the prices, and the guards cost much more nowadays."
"You hear about what the Surtovans did at the border?"
"You heard him, Dalton. Turn out your pockets."
"You heard the magistrate, sergeant. Remember the oaths you swore to the city."
"You heard {mf|him|her}, Shortie. Sorry, but today just isn't your day."
"You helped cure a terrible plague. Accept the gratitude of {g|Pharasma}Pharasma's{/g} faithful servant — and this reward."
"You hid your surname from us – Yorgesh Bragic! You are related to the owners of this inn!"
"You hired someone to burn down my shop! You bankrupted me!"
"You hit me? I hit you more!"
"You human {mf|king|queen}? So tiny, but still {mf|king|queen}? Must be smart."
"You idiot! Have you learned nothing?!"
"You idiot! That was nothing more than a young girl's whim! How could she ever love some threadbare beggar?!"
"You interfere in a war you have no stake in. I hope you know what you are doing."
"You just hide from me. Even in death."
"You just piss me off. Honestly."
"You kill your own kin!"
"You know how many brave souls have been lost in the Stolen Lands? Hundreds, at least! You think you're any luckier?"
"You know only too well where... where this 'gift' came from!"
"You know what I feel when I kiss you? I taste mystery. I taste strength, and passion, and sweetness."
"You know what I hate? Mummies. Perhaps it's because I'm the librarian."
"You know what? I really liked that adventure with the soul eater!"
"You know what? Let's not do this. I value our friendship and don't want to ruin it."
"You know what? Screw it! For {mf|King|Queen} {Name}!"

"You know, Lissa, my father always used to scold me, saying, 'Ivar, you shouldn't wag your tongue so much.' I never listened. Remember the Day of Matchmaking? The headman's son came to you, gave you those nice boots only city ladies wear, and his servants brought a barrel of honey and a crate of sausages. Then Mengar the Smith came — brought an ornate door casing, skillfully crafted locks, and piles of other housewares — and said he was going to decorate a house for the two of you with all he crafted. I came late in the evening, after all of them had left, and all I brought was a bunch of wild flowers. I set them on the porch and said, 'I saw a nixie crying in the forest. She'd planned to make a lantern of my heart, but she found my heart was already taken! It's bad fortune to make nixies cry, so Lady Lissa, would you go to the forest and give the heart you've taken to anyone who may need it more than you?'
You told me I was such a fool, and then you kissed me.
For our wedding, you invited your relatives, the old miller's widow, and stupid Aysel, the fisherman — out of pity, I suspect, as no one else wanted to spend time around him. I invited frogs, wind, and the full moon. 'Brother Moon,' I said, 'please be so kind as to share your light with everyone, for my bride tires of shining over this world alone.' The frogs sang along with Aysel, and you were more beautiful than the moon and more cheerful than the spring wind.
Arry was about to turn five and Mika was just four, and I'd spent a month dragging fish to the cliff and cursing a stupid wyvern who just wouldn't be lured. When I finally lured her, I chased her through the bushes, collecting her silver scales here and there after they fell. It wouldn't have been so hard to decorate our garden with those scales if I hadn't done it at night. Then the morning came, and our children went silent, their mouths agape — hundreds of silver lights sparkled atop apple and cherry trees. I hid my scratched hands in my sleeves and scoffed. 'This isn't so special — you've never noticed before how the stars hide in the trees from the cunning Sky Cat?' You looked at me without a word, but I could still hear your words in my mind. 'You're such a fool, Ivar. I love you.'
...I don't remember how I came up with the story of the Silver Dragon. I came home late with a black grouse I'd shot and said, 'It was a hard fight! I just couldn't aim properly. This dragon kept peeping out from the clouds, blinding me with his shiny silver wings.' 'You saw a real dragon, Dad?' 'Not the whole dragon, no. You see, the only way to see the dragon is if two loving souls climb up the high cliff under a new moon, hand in hand.' At the time, I wasn't thinking about how dark the night was, or how steep the path to the top of the cliff was — especially for little feet — or how wet the rocks were after the rain. I was just looking at you, wishing it was us — two loving souls, hand in hand, sneaking away up to the skies, as we did when we weren't that much older than Arry and Mika.
The next morning you woke first, and it was you who found our children's beds empty.
You said nothing to me then. Not then, not when we walked through the misty woods, not when we found Mika's doll at the start of the path leading to the cliff. You kept silent as I ascended from the chasm with Arry's body in my hands. You said nothing when Aysel brought Mika's body, found further out, at the lake shore near the cliff.
You're such a fool, Ivar. You wag your tongue too much. It was just a story, another of your stupid fairy tales, how could it end this way?!
I'm so sorry, Lissa.
Better you'd married the smith. Or the headman's son. Or even stupid Aysel. Anyone but me.
It's all my fault. Forgive me. Please.
And let me go.
Today, I'll go to the children's graves and…"
"You know, how they're running things now. The strict laws, the ordered procedures, how you need to get approval for everything."

"You know, {name}... As much as I struggle to keep your domain from economic collapse, you – you make every effort to stymie me at every turn! This might seem all in good fun to you. Indeed, it's not like a provincial ruler has anything better to do than make a fool of a famous traveler. In fact, I've got an idea for a new book, and I can't presently afford the luxury of wasting my time on useless debates and unheeded advice. I'm sure you can easily find a more flexible Treasurer once I am gone."

"You know, {name}... I think it's time I resigned as your advisor. I'm sorry, but what's going on here makes me feel really bad. I will gladly set out on campaigns with you, and I'm not giving up on my book, but public service... Well, it's just not for me. I'm sorry. I hope you understand."

"You know…" {n}Amiri scratches her nose, then sighs.{/n} "Fine, I'll just say it. I don't like being your General. I give you good advice, and you never listen. Of course I'll do what you say this time, but after this – forget it. Find yourself another general."
"You left scratches on me... I hope I didn't hurt you."
"You leprous hyena spawn!"
"You like playing with fire, don't you?"
"You look... outlandish. Where do you hail from?"
"You lost, there? Get out of here, before I decide to wake up the commander!"
"You lying monster! You tricked me into stepping through the portal, but you can't defeat me! The Master sent you to test my faith!"
"You made it out to see us! Quite an achievement, for someone who claims to be king of these lands!"
"You make a living by robbing people!"
"You must be either very bold or very stupid to come to the lair of Ilthuliak. It makes no difference which — the end is the same for both!"
"You must search the depths of your heart, as well as the depths of your mind."
"You need space?" {n}Regongar starts screaming.{/n} "Please! All of {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} is yours, go wherever you want! Just don't call it 'love'!"
"You never cease to surprise me. I like this."
"You next, borba!"

"You not leave this place, dumb borba. Should not have come." {n}He rubs the half-worn brand mark on his chest.{/n} "Hargulka needs to prepare, though. Find Hargulka later, if you can, stranger. Dur borba! Dur garban dzarg!" {n}Hargulka pounds the {g|Torag}Torag{/g} statue with his fist and leaps into the side hallway.{/n}

"You obviously have some strategy, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. But I cannot approve of your methods, so as your Councilor I will fare poorly at providing the assistance you need. It only makes sense for me to retire after fulfilling this order. You can recruit an advisor whose thoughts are more attuned to your own."
"You order destroy things! You be good King!"
"You pay for this! You pay!"
"You promised to show me your wares. Something about 'the most modest of prices,' if I recall."
"You put the interests of peasants and serfs above your own. Do you hope to buy their loyalty with a show of weakness? How naïve."
"You really think I serve him for the money?" {n}Kressle smirks bitterly.{/n} "Enough talk. Die!"
"You revealed your secret to me – it means you broke one of the rules set by the deity's herald..."
"You ruined the tribe, but then you saved it."
"You said it. I'm a magnate now, after all — I got a fortune to keep. The others can bite it. Damn, I just can't stop looking at this fine suit!"
"You said the rod was magical!"
"You said you'd pay us to protect the caravan! And we made sure it arrived safe and sound."
"You see, I came back for you. Everything is different in Varnhold now, but you and I are still a team...."
"You see, my dear hostess, scientific disputes can become rather heated..."

"You see, my sister died, and I... couldn't get over it. Kanerah was killed by a soul eater – a monster summoned by secret followers of {g|Abaddon}Abaddon's{/g} archdaemons. Those who summoned him died in the fight, but the beast was too strong for my sister... and I wasn't even there to protect her." {n}Kalikke catches her breath.{/n} "I... we'd just had a fight, and we both did some stupid things just before. But I don't want to talk about that now."
"You seem an educated man. What are you doing in these woods?"
"You should have submitted the old man for justice. Accessory to slavery is a heavy crime."
"You should've listened to us back then!"
"You shouldn't flirt with these men who imagine they own things, {name}. Now that they've bought you, they'll find some way to sell you for a good price."
"You shouldn't have come here, weaklings!"
"You shouldn't have come to this place..."
"You shouldn't have done that!"
"You shouldn't imagine that invading his immediate neighbors will sate Razmir's appetite. There will come a day when we see his mask on soldiers at our gates."
"You shouldn't. Governance is not something you can learn as a merchant or craftsman. It takes talent and an understanding of social responsibility. Community leaders hardly possess such skill."
"You stay away from him!"
"You still haven't told me what you want from me."
"You surprised King Hargulka is smart? Trolls were dumb and cowardly before... but not anymore." {n}Hargulka grins viciously.{/n}
"You talk Queen. Queen no talk — we no let in!"
"You there! Help me with this thing!"
"You think I'm wet behind the ears? I don't need help." {n}She frowns slightly.{/n} "But stay close. Call you if I need you."
"You told me of the so-called pirates, Judge Celvoway. What could you have to gain by painting your own people as outlaws?"
"You too, Moskoni? You too have betrayed me? You won't get away with this!"
"You tore my family apart! Put my husband behind bars — my only support, the last helping hand I had!"

"You try to tell me what to do? You shouldn't. Everyone who tried it before, met a bad end." {n}A sinister smile flickers over Regongar's face and sinks in the depth of his eyes.{/n} "Chill out. We're just going to play a little with my Octavia. No one dies, I promise."
"You two almost tore me in half."
"You understand nothing of town planning! A hospital must be built on a cursed cemetery!"
"You want me to beg them for peace? How revolting! Do you even see the giant gap there is between us?!"
"You want my help. I want my services to be handsomely rewarded."
"You want something?"
"You want to complain about the law, you're looking at the wrong guy."
"You want to do it again right now?"

"You want to teach them a lesson. This I understand. But this is worthy of a wild animal. If you behave like a wild animal today, then be assured, tomorrow you will be treated like one. They will put out traps and hunt you down."
"You wanted to ask something of me…"
"You wanted to become one of us, one of the Eldest. — To create your own kingdom of Love and Joy, stealing pieces from others' dominions."
"You wanted to know if there was a place you could settle in around here…"
"You warned Renshala Vascari of an impending attack, not from pirates but from me. It's as though you had hoped I would attack her and incriminate myself."
"You watch your words..."
"You were a part of me. What are you now?"
"You were born for glory, my wolf cub!"
"You were deceived!"

"You who reads these lines! Whoever you are, please heed my words. I am in desperate need of help!
My name is Farnirras the Pensive, and I am a mage from the great empire of Iobaria, may the gods prolong the years of its prosperity. I retired to these wild lands, in the furthest of our provinces, to peacefully engage in magical experiments. But now a terrible danger looms over my work, and even my life itself. I'm not even sure I will have time to finish this message before it takes me. Oh, unknown reader, if this letter is in your hands, I am either dead or trapped in a magical prison in a barrow near the western spurs of Tors of Levenies. If you do not lack virtue, or at least desire to receive a well-deserved reward, then find the dungeon and save me (or recover my mortal remains).
It will be difficult to open the door. Here in the laboratory I store the magic key you will need for this. But in addition to the key, the door is locked by a mighty spell. The door will open only for the one who defeats forty-five monstrous creatures of all kinds. Magic tags their lairs with a special mark, which you may have already seen on your way.
It may be foolish to hope there's a daredevil out there, who is capable of overcoming dozens of monsters and combating the terrible power that has ruined me... but still I hope for a miracle.
F."
"You will be the lady of dust, of trampled flowers, of ruined undertakings. From now until forever, this is your dominion."
"You will become one of the Eldest, Nyrissa. Your journey was long, but now it is over."
"You will never give me orders again."
"You will not corrupt me!"
"You will not take our lives easily!"
"You wish to enter my service?"
"You wish to see the marchioness?"
"You wished to see me, my lady?"
"You won't dare to sentence me to death!"
"You won't escape, traitor!"
"You won't find a more loyal servant — or one more deserving to be a king!"
"You won't fool me! Begone!"

"You won't fool me! Begone!"
"... she said, mere moments before I fooled her again. Oh, mortals, mortals!"
"You won't intimidate us!"
"You won't lead me astray! I will destroy you! I'll pass the test!"
"You won't leave! Death to the intruders!"
"You won't take me so easily!"
"You! You ruined me!"
"You'd be wise to listen to the woman closely. She's clearly the smartest among you."
"You'd better work hard to atone for your mistakes, Tristian – unless you want to beg for my executioner's forgiveness."
"You'd love it there. Everyone does."
"You'll cause trouble for your pack. The day you pay for this mistake will surely be a black day indeed."
"You'll never crush the spirit of freedom! It shall always live on — in me, and in your daughter!"
"You'll never hear about me again, I promise, {mf|baron|baroness}!"
"You'll see — another year or two, and we'll be taking boats to Restov!"
"You're a brave one. What's your name?"
"You're a crazy goat! How do you even survive without me?"
"You're bleeding me dry! Lower the price!"
"You're cursed my child to die!"
"You're dead, Armag!"
"You're evil! Pure evil! Go away! Someone will rescue me eventually! You'll see!" {n}Waine resumes his previous yelling.{/n} "HEEEEEEELP! SAVE MEEEEE!"
"You're from Mivon, you say? What is their view on this new barony?"
"You're going to jail. Right now."
"You're hired. Just remember your promise."
"You're just in time, mortals. I'm hungry!"
"You're just in time, {name}! We're expecting the attack any minute now!"
"You're not eating at all — that is ill-advised. If you find nothing left for you, don't say I didn't warn you."
"You're not going anywhere!"
"You're not in trouble. Just tell me everything."
"You're not welcome here!"
"You're nothing but a greedy, money-grubbing tyrant. You couldn't care less for your daughter's happiness!"
"You're on your own, sergeant."
"You're right, these roads are dangerous. Trolls are the least of your concerns — if you were to leave the barony, you might be killed on the road by a random traveler — even one such as myself."
"You're right. Vengeance is a sacred cause!"
"You're robbing me blind! What, you think I have a money tree or something?"
"You're sitting on OUR street begging for money! Who said you could do that? Who'd you pay for the rights?"
"You're still here? What are you waiting for? Get to the capital!"
"You're sure there's nothing you'd like to confess? Nothing you might want to ask forgiveness for?"
"You're terribly sweet when you blush. I should make you do it more often."
"You're the king of trolls, I'm the {mf|king|queen} of humans. Let's make peace, as rulers do. Your people won't go near our villages, and in turn, we will leave you be."
"You're too scared to make it to a road that's just a few steps away? Those traps would be doing the world a favor."
"You're too tender with me. Don't be afraid of hurting me."
"You're welcome!"
"You're welcome."

"You're wrong if you think gold has no odor. Believe me, by accepting dirty money today, you take on the reek of sewage for years to come. Don't be surprised if no one wishes to shake hands with you tomorrow!"
"You're. A damn. Idiot."
"You're... probably right. But it's so hard to take that plunge!"
"You've brought a terrible curse upon your lands. But we will help you break it."
"You've caused enough trouble already!"
"You've chosen a bad time to pay a visit!"
"You've dreamed of this for a long time, haven't you? To dive into a vortex of wonder and discovery, while your foes tramp the dusty roads of Golarion."
"You've gone clean mad over your faith!"
"You've got nothing to support your case apart from accusations and threats. I'm calling the guards — this is blatant extortion!"
"You've got to save the kingdom! Who else if not you?"
"You've made Gorum proud this day!"

"You've managed to establish a country whose citizens look to foreign lands with great interest, rather than keeping their distance out of fear. This is a great achievement, especially considering how things once were around here. Many foreigners arrive at our borders seeking citizenship, though they understand that such things are not handed out lightly. They are prepared to serve in the army to earn their place in your domain."

"You've sent your guard to Varnhold. But firstly, they're strangers here. Second, they're not your best people. Think about it — who would ever want to get posted all the way down here? So that's why there's are so many guards there and so little order. As for us, we know the people we're dealing with. We can tell the real thug from the harmless drunk who likes to tie one on and wave his fists around. Who to watch because he's a dangerous fool, and who to watch because he's an eager fool!"
"You, me... All of us will find ourselves on the path to the Boneyard. So let us pray that we'll be met by our loved ones after Pharasma has passed judgment upon us."

"You, trollsnout! Stay inside the circle! Pah — what does he care if he loses a few toes, though? He'll grow new ones... Yeah, stand as you want, no worries! He-he... Well... Where should we throw this batch..."

"You," the kobold hissed, pointing at the biggest troll. "You were taken into the tribe by the chieftain himself! By Hargulka!"
Hearing the chieftain's name, the troll froze, and the kobold continued his violent hissing. "Why? You do not dessserve thisss! Coward! Disssgraccce! Tartuk, the great kobold, no give brand to you!" The kobold spat on the ground. "You ssshame the tribe. Ssshame all trollsss." With an angry growl, the troll stepped closer to the fire.
"You... You'll pay for this..."
"You... are aware that insulting a representative of the law is a finable offense, right?"
"You... you are very... beautiful!"
"Your Grace! Don't leave me!"
"Your Grace!"

"Your Grace,
Please, forgive me my sudden disappearance. I deemed myself of more use among your subjects than at court.
The people are afraid, Your Grace. They believe that they've been forgotten, that their ruler couldn't care less about the simple folk, even as they perish each and every day. For this reason, those who can bear arms are starting to take matters into their own hands. A wild mob is a force to be reckoned with, and you already have enough to worry about. Fortunately, I was able to convince these people that I'm on their side. In the end, I have decided to lead this militia myself, in order to be the first one to know whenever the people learn something new and to protect them from making rash decisions. I've led troops before, and your subjects view me as one of their own, so they trust me and are willing to follow me.
It was with a heavy heart that I left your castle, but my hope was that once among the common people, I would be able to track down the source of the disease that struck the barony. I was recently informed that one of the squads scouring the outlying regions of Kamelands had encountered a mysterious shrine. Our spies report that at the beginning of each week, cultists gather there to worship the dark goddess Lamashtu, the patroness of all manner of hideous creatures.
I know little of the gods and their affairs, but the appearance of the Mother of Beasts and her followers in a land teeming with monsters can hardly be a coincidence. As soon as I've finished writing this letter, I shall lead a squad of my best men there and await your arrival. I ask for your help, Your Grace, for I shall need it to strangle this filth in its cradle. Who knows — perhaps, we'll capture one of the cultists alive and find out if they and their goddess are behind the misfortunes of your barony.
Your loyal servant,
Kesten Garess"
"Your Grace, I shall pray to Erastil for you till the end of my days!"

"Your Grace, I'm afraid we must interrupt that conversation for now. A moment ago, a troll was caught in one of my fire traps... and it was unharmed. I suggest that giving me a chance to explore its corpse would better equip me to answer your questions."
"Your Grace, hurry! Your people await!"
"Your Grace, make haste! Help the defenders of the camp!"
"Your Grace, save us!"

"Your Grace, there is one small matter... a series of small matters, actually, that's growing into a larger problem... your goblin... ally... seems to have invited more of his tribe to the capital, and they are acting as if… as if it is their home."
"Your Grace, those are our guards. They keep order in the city — or keep their mouths busy with gossip. Their commander is Captain Hyland. He must be nearby."
"Your Grace."
"Your Highness is in trouble now!"
"Your Highness! Drive off these phantoms!"
"Your Highness! Everyone who could be saved has left the city! We should follow them!"
"Your Highness! I won't let them near you!"
"Your Highness! I'm glad to see you again!"
"Your Highness!"
"Your Highness, it seems the goblin tribe has left the kingdom. Good riddance, if you ask me! Everyone seems happy… except your goblin ally, perhaps."
"Your Highness, please allow me to assure you of the eternal loyalty of the family of Della- ha ha ha, oh, I can't!"
"Your Highness, pleased to meet you! I'm Edna Aldori, and this is my sister, Julia."

"Your Highness, there is something transpiring outside the city. You may want to go yourself – it seems your goblin... ally... has been industrious again and fashioned some sort of... something." {n}He sighs.{/n} "It may be best you go see for yourself."
"Your Highness, we are preparing to repel an attack!"
"Your Highness, we're under attack!"
"Your Highness. Tiger Lords are forever your allies."
"Your Highness? It's wonderful to finally meet you in person."
"Your Royal Highness! What an honor!"

"Your Royal Highness, the much-esteemed and illustrious {Name}, tamer of Dunsward and the Stolen Lands, hero{mf||ine} of the battle against the barbarian hordes on the Flintrock Grassland, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera.
I am happy to hereby invite you to the Rushlight Tournament — the most important social event in the River Kingdoms, where the whole region's upper crust will gather to mingle and have some innocent fun. The Tournament, as always, will take place on the shore of the Rushlight River. I eagerly await your arrival, and look forward to the chance to finally meet you in person!
Cordially yours,
Castruccio Irovetti, King of Pitax"
"Your blood will satiate the Unquenchable Fire!"
"Your brother seems to have been a fine lad. I wish he were still with us."
"Your common is exceptional."
"Your death will be quick and painless – the final mercy of Shelyn!"
"Your death will bring glory to Norgorber!"
"Your entry permit. That you received when you crossed the border?"

"Your esteemed Grace!
It is with deep regret that I must inform you that I can no longer await your decisive action in relation to restoring my right to the valuables located on the island of Candlemere Lake. Please be informed that I shall be leaving the borders of your barony and heading into the dominion of Maegar Varn — a well-respected lord and a valiant warrior, quite worthy of his own chronicle. As I'm sure I can expect to make a name for myself in the ranks of Varn's army, I have decided to magnanimously renounce my claim on the treasure to be found at Candlemere Lake. It is yours to deal with at your sole discretion.
Warmest regards,
Willas Gunderson"
"Your experiments aren't safe — stop them immediately. And kill the troll."
"Your eyes are far more confident now than when we last met. The eyes of a true {mf|king|queen}!"
"Your face, commander! You didn't expect to see your General again, did you?"
"Your faithful servant calls to you… heed my prayer, Sarenrae… I beg you, hear me…"
"Your fate was decided before you were born, yet you chose to go your own way — as I once did. And you can achieve so much more!"
"Your fear tastes so delicious!"
"Your gold smells funny, friend."
"Your hairy monster couldn't be in here! Not unless you gave it an invisibility potion. You didn't, right?"
"Your last order, my lady… it frightens me. The seed of an Everblooming Flower is almost prepared, as you requested. But what will it bring?
"Your lord drew a winning ticket! You must be glad that you serve in his army."
"Your money or your life!"
"Your money?! You screwed things up so badly, you should be paying me! You ruined everything, you nitwits!"
"Your nightmare has only just begun, mask. Silence!"
"Your people are in danger. We must act without delay!"

"Your soldiers are... brave, but weak. By the will of Kurgess, we'll sort out your pathetic forces. My priests know how to strengthen a soldier with magic that will give them the power and speed of a mighty animal. And if that fails to protect them, our prayers will heal your warriors and restore them to perfect fighting form."
"Your soul is poisoned, like an animal gone mad. I will leave you with that. Farewell..."
"Your spouse robbed an innocent passer-by, seriously wounding him in the process. I see no reason the law should make an exception for him."
"Your title is very unusual."
"Your tribe has taken a huge blow. If you wish, we could give you shelter in one of our towns."
"Your tribe will suffer for your crimes!"
"Your vision is clouded. You do not seek to pursue a goal, but to avenge an insult."
"Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!"

"Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}, I hope that matters of state in this land of ours are indeed all fine and well – and what troubles there are don't weigh too heavily upon your mind! I write to ask you to check our local herb doctor, Bokken. The poor old man is losing his mind. – He spends all day and night stooped over his cauldron! He looks about to lash out at anyone, especially those he doesn't know. He even snarls at me and Oleg, which he'd never have let himself do before... Please come and see him before the old codger loses his mind completely, may Erastil save him. We've no one to turn to but you!
Hoping you come as soon as possible, I remain,
Very truly yours,
Svetlana Leveton"
"Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}? Linzi? Praise {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}! I beg you, save us from this... music connoisseur!"
"Your... friends? Am I hearing it right? You think any of them are still alive?"
"You… you'd really do that for me? Oh, I'm in such luck! It's a deal, friend!"
"Yuck! Is that a fly in my mug?"
"Yup, we'll be living the good life. I'm gonna buy myself a little tavern, keep myself fat, drunk, and happy."
"Zimar", "Cassomir", "Oppara" — fastened to the chests are metal plaques, etched with the names of Taldor's cities.
"b'ZHVEra'TCH at'SCH'aSCH SviarRA'HKE! VRidShUu ROVAGUG asVVItchi!!!"
"moRE sLAVes of The mASTer! MORe mEAt!!!"
"tMCHisah'scAA! EEI Hsh'raTZE!!!"
"{Name} — the tamer of the Shrike Hills, who put an end to the atrocities of the Stag Lord's bandits!"
"{Name}! You're just in time! Help us!"
"{Name}, how could you say such a monstrous thing?! Is that the way the hero of my book would talk? You sound more like a villain!"
"{Name}, the hero{mf||ine} of the Stolen Lands, the slayer of the Stag Lord!"
"{Name}, you have a hair on your shoulder... And I think it's mine."
"{Race}'s foes are Hargulka's foes!"

"{d|Tartuk}Tartuk{/d} the kobold king made trolls immortal, taught us to talk with borba. Now trolls are smarter than borba, stronger than borba, better than borba!" {n}Hargulka straightens up and looms over you, flexing his shoulders.{/n} "What you say, borba? What you say now, when trolls are better than you?"
"{d|Varn}Maegar Varn{/d} and his people will fight for you as they'd fight for their own lives."

"{g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} is closely connected to the First World. Spontaneous portals between the two worlds are not uncommon. – All I did was give one such portal some extra stability. Once every few months it opened wide enough to allow Nyrissa's creatures to come charging through."

"{g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} is a timeless watcher. He's been locked away by {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g}, the goddess of rebirth. From her {g|Boneyard}Boneyard{/g} he watches over the world, knowing the time for the final reaping shall come. He's the bloated moon hanging in the sky. He's the Harbinger of the Last Days. He's the one who will stay when all the others are gone."
"{g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu{/g}? Disgusting. Do you know the kind of worship she patronizes? Kill them. And wash your hands afterward."
"{mf|Aron|Aronesss}!"

"{mf|Baron|Baroness} {name},
I have received your demands and accept your terms and conditions. Along with this letter, I send you the entire ransom for the body of my son. Also, I wish to use this opportunity to offer you a formal apology, on behalf the noble House Lebeda, for the insult that my son inflicted upon you and your family. There's no doubt that what Lander did was inexcusable. However, if he really had intended to stab you in the back, you would surely be dead by now. Apparently, my son took pity on you, so you shouldn't harbor any resentment against him.
I must confess, I am surprised by your nobleness. I sincerely hope that your mother will likewise be allowed to recover your body, after you perish. If the family of the highly esteemed {mf|baron|baroness} lacks the necessary financial surety, I shall purchase your body personally, to repay for your kindness. Be assured, your remains shall fall into good hands.
Unfortunately, I will not be able to visit your lands in person — my doctors recommend against travel in damp climates. But be assured that if I learn of your presence in our realm, I shall prepare a solemn welcome for you without delay.
With best regards,
Sarrona Lebeda, head of House Lebeda"

"{mf|Baron|Baroness} {name},
first of all, I would like to thank you for your mercy, and for the lesson you've taught to me. No one has ever done me such an honor. I hope our little conflict won't cause you to reject your better memories of me. Just think about all the difficulties I've helped you through, and all the heroic deeds I inspired you to pursue. I dread to think how long it will take you to find a suitable replacement for me. As for me, I can assure you I don't hold a grudge, and will do everything in my power to avoid crossing your path again.
Forever grateful,
Lord Lander Lebeda"
"{mf|Baron|Baroness}, we need to hurry and catch the cultist!"
"{mf|Brother|Sister}! Armag is here and will share the trials of battle with you."
"{mf|He|She} may let you leave, but I do not. For the Riversong!"
"{mf|He|She} robs folk worse than us, and then has the nerve to spew all this righteous crap at us. I say we get 'em!"
"{mf|He|She} robs folk worse than us, and then has the nerve to spew all this righteous crap at us."
"{mf|He|She}'s here!"
"{mf|My Baron|My Baroness}, we have to catch the fleeing cultist!"
"{mf|My Baron|My Baroness}, you are so merciful!"
"{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! I have a gift for you. This is an orc weapon, and they know a thing or two about war."

"{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! I'm probably not wise enough to understand your orders. But I feel a complete fool every time I recommend one thing, and you do something completely different! Does my advice mean so little to you? Did you invite me to become a diplomat just to make fun of me? Alas, I am tired of being a buffoon. You should find a replacement for me, and I will continue to serve you elsewhere."
"{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! We finally meet in person. It's an honor for me."
"{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}!"

"{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, I've been thinking about this a lot lately, and I'd like to resign as your curator. You and I regard life very differently. Our values seem to be in opposition. I hope you will understand my decision."
"{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, thank you! My luck nearly ran out today!"
"{name}! Here!"
"{name}! I thought I'd never find you in this House!"
"{name}! {name}!"

"{name}!" {n}shouts an approaching woman, her voice silencing all of the other conversations for a hundred feet. It is Renshala Vascari, who had overseen the convoy you attacked, and she proudly wears light blue clothing embroidered with the heron insignia of the Riversong Trade House.{/n} "You have the gall to show your face in Pitax after what you {d|c51 Renshala Rude}did{/d} to me? A brazen attack on this kingdom's river against one of its eminent trade houses, and now you gallivant about while snubbing justice!"{n} Several of her personal guards array themselves behind her, watching grimly. At the same time, onlookers begin gathering to see what's happening.{/n} "You attacked my shipments, my family, and my crewmembers!"

"{name}!"{n} shouts a steely-faced man, his voice silencing all of the other conversations for a hundred feet. {/n}"I am Jhofre Vascari, head of the Riversong Trade House whose convoy you attacked near the {g|Pitax River}Pitax River{/g}. You have the gall to show your face in {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} after what you {d|c51 Renshala Killed}did{/d} to my sister and my shipments? A brazen attack on this kingdom's river against one of its eminent trade houses, and now you gallivant about while snubbing justice!"{n} Several of his personal guards array themselves behind him, watching grimly. At the same time, onlookers begin gathering to see what's happening.{/n} "You attacked my shipments, my family, and my crewmembers!"

"{name},
I have a problem, and no one else to turn to but you. I need someone to travel to a town south of Restov, Varnhold. The town was founded by Maegar Varn — you met him at the reception to celebrate your new title.
Recently, I've stopped getting reports from him. I didn't pay much attention to it, but in the past week, not a single traveler, merchant, or messenger from Varnhold has showed up in Restov. No one knows what has happened to the town.
If I were you, I would make sure I was ready for this journey: the plains of Dunsward are dangerous. Also, we have yet to find out what was it that cut off communication with Varnhold: an attack, arcane magic, or some epidemic or plague. I would have gladly investigated the matter, but the current state of affairs dictates I refrain from dealing with this personally. I am counting on you and your help: head out for Dunsward and find out what — or who — stands behind the vanishing of Varnhold.
Your friend and ally,
Swordlord Jamandi Aldori"

"{name},
I knew the day would come when you began to doubt me. At least you didn't proceed immediately to bite the hand that feeds you. It is a fair question, what reasons led me to write to you when I could have traveled to Varnhold myself. Well then, let me lay my cards on the table.
There are reasons for this, grave reasons indeed. The threat of Numeria looms over Rostland. More and more, barbarians make their way into our lands and attack our caravans. Our scouts report that barbarian tribes gather on our borders. I would have gladly turned from this crisis and dealt with Varnhold myself, were it not for my sentimental attachment to my country, my city and its people, who are about to be swallowed up by the Numerian hydra that crawls towards us from the east. Of course, Restov does have a ruler — but it would be ignoble to leave Lord Mayor Sellemius without my support in such a difficult time.
There was no one I could ask for help but you. I ask of you, as an old comrade in arms: gather your men and discover what has happened in Varnhold — at least so that whatever devoured its inhabitants doesn't find its way to your own subjects.
P.S. I've sent some resources along with this letter. Consider them a sign of my good will, and an expression of my gratitude for your help.
Your friend and ally,
Swordlord Jamandi Aldori"

"{name}, I must refuse the position of diplomat. To be honest, your decisions disappoint me, and I don't wish to feel like that towards someone I've sworn to serve loyally and faithfully. I shall guard your back and slay your enemies, but I will not argue over matters of state. You must find yourself another diplomat."

"{name}, I… I just can't go on like this. We're just too different! All the things that I'd pursue, you just say they're useless. Whenever I come up with an idea, you reject it. Worst of all, your sense of right and wrong is completely different from mine! {n}Octavia exhales decisively.{/n} "I'll just have to give up my position as Magister... no matter how difficult that is for me. But don't worry, I'll still be glad to join you on your adventures and follow you into battle."
"{name}... The darknesss callsss to you..."

"– Tell us, oh Teacher, why would Brevoy call us barbarians in the books you give us?
– The Gods became angry with our homeland, my son. This land has devoured so many great empires, as if it was unwilling to bear life... There are centuries-old ruins around our settlement. They were ravaged by a star that fell from the sky. The Kingdom of the Cyclopes was the first victim of its curse. New settlers claimed this land ten centuries later, to establish a beautiful country named Iobaria, which stretched from the Lake of Mists and Veils to the Castrovin Sea. But the curse still lay upon these lands, and trouble came once again. Our ancestors suffered numerous maladies. The Tearplague, the Chardeath, the Choking Death – one after another, leaving only pain behind.
– People say that Otib the Necromancer was to blame...
– But who knows... A great civilization was turned to dust. This is why I'm teaching you. Brevoy shouldn't make fun of you or call you barbarians..."
"… Especially on romantic encounters. Encounters that might be continued..."
"… how you, so devoted to good, could so diligently look the other way, while there was evil happening right under your nose?"
"… lady mine?"
"… well, I had to conceal my tiefling nature. It was so hard to hide my tail!"
"… will you continue to look the other way as you always have?"
"…and miss the battle! Better we concern ourselves with the woes of today."

"…crushing bone. Hear me. Each word I speak shall turn to stone. The world shall shudder at my word. Open your eyes and see. The world becomes beautiful. Burnt forests stretching to the horizon. Mounds of bodies. Blackened skies. Skulls littering the coasts like gravel. I, the one who renders the flesh of her enemies, take in this beauty. All living beings tremble at my sight. Bow to me. Search. Search the children of Shelyn. Tear them apart. Destroy them. No. Transform them. Grant them the gift of rebirth. Let them become beautiful. Befitting the beauty I shall bring into this world. Oh Great Lamashtu, the eater of hearts, reveal your truth to us. We hear your call. All of you shall live in a better world. Curse Pazuzu. The flying worm. He shall fall in this war. Soon. Myriads of warriors under my command. The mountains themselves shall crumble at our feet. Burn all. Make the world beautiful. The ground thirsts for blood. I thirst for beauty. Give birth to beasts. I shall..."

You apply your character's Persuasion skill to checks required for: • Change others' attitudes. • Create diversions. • Gather information. • Intimidate. • Lie. • Make requests. • Pass secret messages.

(Charisma; Trained Only) This skill represents character's talent at activating magic items, even if you are not otherwise trained in their use. You apply your character's Use Magic Device skill to checks required for: • Activate wands and scrolls that you would normally be unable to use • Equip magic items that you would normally be prohibited from equipping. • Avoid negative consequences of using dangerous magic items and cursed items.

This skill covers hiding and moving silently. You apply your character's Stealth skill to checks required for: • Avoid being noticed.

You apply your character's Acrobatics skill to checks required for: • Move near opponents without provoking attacks of opportunity. • Keep your balance. • Escape from restraints. • Soften falls. • Squeeze through a tight spot.

You apply your character's Knowledge (Arcana) skill to checks required for: • Identify magic. • Identify monsters (constructs, dragons, and magical beasts). • Learn or borrow spells (from spellbooks and scrolls). • Recall knowledge (about arcana).

You apply your character's Lore (Nature) skill to checks required for: • Handle animals. • Identify monsters (aberrations, animals, fey, monstrous humanoids, oozes, plants, vermin). • Recall knowledge (about dungeons or nature). • Hunt. • Help to cure a disease. • Skin the dead animals.

(Intelligence; Trained Only) This skill represents character's knowledge about the secrets of deities, holy lore, and extraplanar realms. You apply your character's Lore (Religion) skill to checks required for: • Identify monsters (outsiders and undead). • Recall knowledge (about the planes or religions).

(Strength; Armor Check Penalty) This skill represents the character's talent at deeds of physical prowess such as leaping, scaling walls, and swimming. You apply your character's Athletics skill to checks required to: • Catch an object. • Climb an obstacle. • Jump. • Swim.

(Wisdom) This skill represents character's acuity of your senses allows you to notice fine details, see danger coming, and tell when people are lying or otherwise behaving suspiciously. You apply your character's Perception skill to checks required for: • Discern secret messages. • Get hunches. • Notice creatures and details. • Search locations. • Sense enchantments. • Sense motives.

Adventurers: Although dwarven adventurers are rare compared to humans, they can be found in most regions of the world. Dwarves often leave the confines of their redoubts to seek glory for their clans, to find wealth with which to enrich the fortress-homes of their birth, or to reclaim fallen dwarven citadels from racial enemies. Dwarven warfare is often characterized by tunnel fighting and melee combat, and as such most dwarves tend toward classes such as fighters and barbarians.

Arcane Bond At 1st level, wizards form a powerful bond with an object or a creature. This bond can take one of two forms: a familiar or a bonded object. Cantrips Wizards can cast a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again. Specialist School A wizard can choose to specialize in one school of magic, gaining additional spells and powers based on that school. This choice must be made at 1st level, and once made, it cannot be changed. A wizard that does not select a school receives the universalist school instead. Each arcane school gives the wizard a number of school powers. In addition, specialist wizards receive an additional spell slot of each spell level he can cast, from 1st on up. Each day, a wizard can prepare a spell from his specialty school in that slot. This spell must be in the wizard's spellbook. A wizard can select a spell modified by a metamagic feat to prepare in his school slot, but it uses up a higher-level spell slot. Wizards with the universalist school do not receive a school slot. Opposition School A wizard that chooses to specialize in one school of magic must select two other schools as his opposition schools, representing knowledge sacrificed in one area of arcane lore to gain mastery in another. A wizard who prepares spells from his opposition schools must use two spell slots of that level to prepare the spell. Wizard Bonus Feat At 1th, 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th level, a wizard gains a bonus feat. At each such opportunity, he can choose a metamagic feat, spell focus feat or any other spellcaster feat. The wizard must still meet all prerequisites for a bonus feat, including caster level minimums. Selectable Features Specialist Schools: Specialist School – Conjuration The conjurer focuses on the study of summoning monsters and magic alike to bend to his will. Summoner's Charm Whenever you cast a conjuration (summoning) spell, increase the duration by a number of rounds equal to 1/2 your wizard level (minimum 1). This increase is not doubled by Extend Spell. At 20th level, you can change the duration of all summon monster spells to permanent. You can have no more than one summon monster spell made permanent in this way at one time. If you designate another summon monster spell as permanent, the previous spell immediately ends. Acid Dart As a standard action you can unleash an acid dart targeting any foe within 30 feet as a ranged touch attack. The acid dart deals 1d6 points of acid damage + 1 for every two wizard levels you possess. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier. This attack ignores spell resistance. Dimensional Steps At 8th level, you can use this ability to teleport up to 30 feet per wizard level per day as a standard action. This teleportation must be used in 5-foot increments and such movement does not provoke an attack of opportunity. You can bring other willing creatures with you, but you must expend an equal amount of distance for each additional creature brought with you. Specialist School – Evocation Evokers revel in the raw power of magic, and can use it to create and destroy with shocking ease. Intense Spells Whenever you cast an evocation spell that deals hit point damage, add 1/2 your wizard level to the damage (minimum +1). This bonus only applies once to a spell, not once per missile or ray, and cannot be split between multiple missiles or rays. This bonus damage is not increased by Empower Spell or similar effects. This damage is of the same type as the spell. At 20th level, whenever you cast an evocation spell you can roll twice to penetrate a creature's spell resistance and take the better result. Force Missile As a standard action you can unleash a force missile that automatically strikes a foe, as magic missile. The force missile deals 1d4 points of damage plus the damage from your intense spells evocation power. This is a force effect. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier. Elemental Wall At 8th level, you can create a wall of energy that lasts for a number of rounds per day equal to your wizard level. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. This wall deals acid, cold, electricity, or fire damage, determined when you create it. The elemental wall otherwise functions like wall of fire. Specialist School – Necromancy The dread and feared necromancer commands undead and uses the foul power of unlife against his enemies. Power over Undead You receive Turn Undead as a bonus feat. You can channel energy a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier, but only to use the selected feat. The DC to save against these feats is equal to 10 + 1/2 your wizard level + your Charisma modifier. At 20th level, undead cannot add their channel resistance to the save against this ability. Grave Touch As a standard action, you can make a melee touch attack that causes a living creature to become shaken for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 your wizard level (minimum 1). If you touch a shaken creature with this ability, it becomes frightened for 1 round if it has fewer Hit Dice than your wizard level. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier. Life Sight At 8th level, you gain blindsight to a range of 10 feet for a number of rounds per day equal to your wizard level. This ability only allows you to detect living creatures and undead creatures. This sight also tells you whether a creature is living or undead. Constructs and other creatures that are neither living nor undead cannot be seen with this ability. The range of this ability increases by 10 feet at 12th level, and by an additional 10 feet for every four levels beyond 12th. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. Specialist School – Transmutation Transmuters use magic to change the world around them. Physical Enhancement: You gain a +1 enhancement bonus to one physical ability score (Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution). This bonus increases by +1 for every five wizard levels you possess to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. You can change this bonus to a new ability score when you prepare spells. At 20th level, this bonus applies to two physical ability scores of your choice. Telekinetic Fist As a standard action you can strike with a telekinetic fist, targeting any foe within 30 feet as a ranged touch attack. The telekinetic fist deals 1d4 points of bludgeoning damage + 1 for every two wizard levels you possess. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier. Change Shape At 8th level, you can change your shape for a number of rounds per day equal to your wizard level. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. This ability otherwise functions like beast shape II or elemental body I. At 12th level, this ability functions like beast shape III or elemental body II.

Armor Class: The higher a character's Armor Class, the more difficult it is to successfully attack them. It combines a base defense of 10 with other factors, such as equipment stats, Dexterity bonus, passive abilities, etc.

Attack Roll: An attack is a character's attempt to strike an opponent. The result of an attack roll depends on many factors: wielded weapons, the combatant's abilities, etc. An attack succeeds if the result of an attack roll equals or exceeds the target's Armor Class. If the d20 roll results in a 20, the attack automatically hits, regardless of the target's AC.

Attacking on a Charge After moving, you may make a single melee attack. You get a +2 bonus on the attack roll and take a –2 penalty to your AC until the start of your next turn. A charging character gets a +2 bonus on combat maneuver attack rolls made to bull rush an opponent.
